sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text: We built good stuff in SN5 and barely wrote any of it down properly: not one doc had a revision number, changelog, or approver, and "what stack did the seat use last year?" was answerable only by whoever happened to remember (PP-09). This doc is how we name, structure, revise, and approve our documents so the knowledge outlives whoever wrote it. On a student team, turnover isn't a risk, it's a schedule.

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text:
All controlled composites documents: CS-XXX standards, work orders (WO-SNx-###), and formal deliverables (test reports, RCA docs). It does not control meeting notes, Slack threads, or scratch R&D notes, but any conclusion from those that the team relies on must graduate into a controlled doc.

Quick references (QR-XXX, §4) are covered here too, as derived documents without approval.

Some rules are enforced by the app from values a lead can change: the team cure holds (in the app, from the "Why N hours?" window of a step whose hold is running), the layup technique checklists (in the app, Reports → Layup techniques) and the restock minimums (in the Firebase console, `config/restock`; the app has no editor for them). Each has an owning standard: CS-008 for the holds, CS-013 for the techniques, CS-011 for the minimums. The owning standard states the rule and the value at its current revision and names the app as the live value. A lead who changes one of these values shall open a revision of the owning standard (§7.2) within two weeks.

Paul's answers, Steve's notes, and anything an AI read off a receipt, packing slip or label are not controlled documents and are never a source under §7.1 step 3. Cite the datasheet, record or standard the number came from.

Steve's notes (`06 Composites App/steve/`) are a joke character's material, not documents under this standard, and are never cited.

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text:
- **Controlled document**: a document with a Doc ID, revision letter, and named approver; the team treats its current released revision as the way work is done.
- **CS-XXX**: a Composites Standard, numbered CS-000 through CS-999. The number never changes once assigned, even if the title is edited.
- **Title**: written once, identically, in the H1 (`# CS-0xx Title`), the header's Title field and the CS-INDEX row. The status text in the header and in CS-INDEX match exactly too (except while a revision is in flight: Under Revision in CS-INDEX, see Status).
- **Revision**: letters, starting at A. Any change to procedure content bumps the revision by one letter per change set, however many drafts it took. Typo fixes may wait for the next content revision. A path fix (a renamed folder or file updated inside the text) takes no letter; record it in `src/rev-exemptions.txt` so the bump check accepts it.
- **Status**: Draft, pending Lead signature (written and reviewed but unsigned: usable as guidance, not yet the rule; Paul cites a Draft standard as the team's current guidance and names its revision), Released (current practice; approver row signed), Under Revision (follow it, but changes are coming; written in CS-INDEX only, while the new draft lives outside `src/`, and the `src/` header keeps its status until the revision lands, §7.2 step 2), Retired (kept for history; do not follow, its header must name the replacement). **A doc whose Approver row is blank is never Released, no exceptions.** The header must say so itself, because members read headers, not CS-INDEX.
- **Normative verbs**: every standard in this series uses them one way. **Shall** is a requirement: deviating from it takes a work-order revision or a lead's logged override. **Should** is a recommendation: the stated way is the default, and departing from it needs a reason you could say out loud at the weekly meeting, not paperwork. **May** marks an allowed option. A numbered step in any §7 procedure is a requirement even without the word "shall"; imperative mood carries the same force.
- **Quick reference (QR-XXX)**: a short derived document, numbered QR-001 upward, that restates a standard's key numbers and steps where a member and Paul find them fast. It is not a controlled document: no approval table, no status, no revision letter. Its header names a `Parent` (the standard and section it is drawn f

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text: No physical hazards; this is a process standard. (The section exists because every CS doc must carry one: CS-Template §6.)

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text:
1. Check CS-INDEX for an existing standard covering the topic; extend rather than duplicate.
2. Copy CS-Template; take the next free CS number from CS-INDEX and add a row there with Status = Draft immediately (this reserves the number).
3. Write the draft. Every quantitative claim gets a source: a TDS/SDS in `03 Datasheets/` (add it and its INDEX row if missing), a test report, or a recorded team measurement (work order ID). "We've always done it this way" is not a source; if that's all there is, say so explicitly in the text.
4. Draw a figure where one carries the geometry better than prose: keep-out zones, stack-ups, plumbing, anything dimensioned. The SVG in `02 CS Standards/src/figures/` is the source. `node tools/render_figures.mjs` renders it to PNG in Saira (titles) and Inter (labels), and the markdown references the PNG with the caption as its alt text; the build numbers the captions. Every distinction in a figure must survive a grayscale print (line weight, hatching, solid against hollow); Berkeley blue and gold are enhancement only, same rule as the shop travelers. No text smaller than about 9 pt at 6.5 in print width. A changed figure gets a new filename, because the app's host caches PNGs for a year. Details are in STYLE.md §5.
5. Get the draft reviewed by someone who did not write it. An agent review, recorded as "simon (reviewer agent)" with its date, satisfies this step for a process standard. A shop procedure also needs a member who did not write it to walk it, physically where the steps are physical, before the lead signs; record their name in the Reviewer row beside the agent's. The Reviewer row names the review of the current revision, with its date.
6. The Composites Lead approves in writing: a Slack message or a comment on the PDF that names the document and revision is enough. Whoever maintains the repo records it: the lead's name and the date in the Approver row, Status → Released in the header and in CS-INDEX, and a link to the approval in the commit message. Then rebuild and deploy as §7.2 steps 6 and 7 say.

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text:
1. Anyone may propose a revision. The trigger that matters most is an incident: **if a part or mold is lost to a process failure, the relevant standard gets reviewed within two weeks** while memory is fresh, and either revised or explicitly re-affirmed in its changelog.
2. Set Status → Under Revision in CS-INDEX so users know changes are coming. Write it in CS-INDEX only, while the draft lives outside `src/`; the header of the current `src/` copy keeps its status until the revision lands. `check_traceability.py --strict` may report the INDEX and header pair while a revision is in flight; that warning is expected until the revision lands.
3. Make the change, add a revision-history row (what changed and *why*, one line each), bump the revision letter.
4. Same review + approval as 7.1.
5. In the same change as step 3, update everything that depends on this standard: re-check each quick reference whose Parent is this standard and move its Checked against; update each card in `04 Printables/printables.html` that names the revision; and if a section number moved, update every `CS-0xx §n.n` reference in other standards and in the app's code. `python3 tools/check_traceability.py` lists the quick references and references that no longer agree.
6. Rebuild the outputs from the repo root: `node tools/render_figures.mjs` (only if an SVG changed), `tools/.venv/bin/python tools/build_docx.py --all`, `python3 tools/gen_docs_manifest.py`, `node tools/build_ai_corpus.mjs`, then `python3 tools/check_traceability.py --strict`. Commit the source and every rebuilt file together.
7. Deploy both. A revision reaches members only after the app's hosting deploy (`firebase deploy --only hosting` from `06 Composites App/`, which carries the in-app PDF), and reaches Paul only after the functions deploy (`firebase deploy --only functions`, which carries the corpus Paul searches; it is deployed separately from hosting). The step 6 commit message names both deploys still to run; run them after the push. Announce a released revision in the weekly summary message only after both deploys.

2. Never delete the file. Retired docs are the team's institutional memory (the Duratec story is worth more retired than deleted).

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text:
1. Each summer, the incoming lead skims every Released or Draft standard with the outgoing lead (budget ~2 hours total) and marks each: still right / needs revision / retire.
2. Findings go into CS-INDEX under Handoff reviews; revisions get scheduled, not just wished for.

Keep CS-INDEX current at the moment of change, not later: it is the one place that lists every document, its revision and its status.

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.section: 7.5 Writing or updating a quick reference
sections.text:
1. Take the next free QR number from CS-INDEX and add its row to the Quick references table there. This reserves the number, as §7.1 step 2 does for a standard.
2. Copy `template/QR-Template.md`. The H1 is `# QR-0xx Title`; the header carries Doc ID, Title, Parent and Checked against, or Covers for a quick reference about using the app.
3. Copy every number from the parent or a datasheet, with its citation. A quick reference never introduces a number.
4. Write each `##` section to stand alone: 300 to 2,400 characters, the answer in its first 240 characters, the heading in the words people ask with, and an `Also called:` line (STYLE.md §6).
5. Run `python3 tools/check_traceability.py --strict`. It fails a quick reference whose Parent does not resolve to a heading or whose parent has moved past its Checked against revision.
6. Rebuild and deploy as §7.2 steps 6 and 7 say. A quick reference reaches Paul only after the functions deploy.
7. When the parent is revised, re-check the quick reference and move its Checked against in the same change (§7.2 step 5).

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text: CS-INDEX is the record of what exists and its status. Each standard's revision history says what changed and why. The repo's commit history of `02 CS Standards/src/` is the record of every edit, including path fixes that took no letter (`src/rev-exemptions.txt`). Work orders (CS-013) record per-part execution; this standard records how the documents themselves are kept honest.

sections.title: CS-000 Documentation Standards, Template & Revision Process
sections.text: SN5's two documentation tiers were formal deliverables (author + date, no versioning) and stub templates (often empty). Both rotted silently: the *Mold Sealer Alternatives* study (Oct 2025) recommended S120/water-based sealers, was overtaken by the XCR decision (Feb–Apr 2026), and nothing marked it superseded. A new member reading the Drive in July 2026 could not tell which document described current practice. Status fields and CS-INDEX exist to make "which doc is true" a lookup instead of an archaeology project.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
Unlabeled molds sat blocking shared storage for weeks while nobody was sure whose they were (PP-10), and unlabeled offcuts made "wait, which gsm is this?" a weekly guessing game (PP-09). So: everything physical gets a label that points back to a record.

This standard says what goes on each label, which stock survives where it is going, where it may and may not be stuck, and how the app prints and scans it.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
Molds, parts (from demold onward), work orders, tooling-board stock, cloth rolls and offcuts, resin, hardener and chemical consumable containers (identified by their UC EH&S tag, §7.11), other consumables (by box or bin), mixed-chemical containers, test panels, R&D studies and coupons, jigs and fixtures, and storage locations.

Not covered: electrical and wiring labeling, which is electrical's own standard, and anything not physically ours. Records that are not physical objects never get a label: issues (`PROJ`), purchases (`BUY`), documents (`DOC`) and stack plans (`STK`). Keeping `PROJ` off labels is also what stops it being misread as `P` (app `labels.js`, `LABELABLE`).

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
- **ID**: the record's own identifier, `PREFIX-SNx-###`, assigned by the app and never reused (CS-013 §4). The ID is the label text; there is no separate part number.
- **Label**: a printed 4 × 1 in label (1⅓ × 4 in on Avery 5522, 29 × 90 mm on DK-1201 die-cut). Top to bottom: the name, in the largest size that fits on one or two lines; the ID, with the R&D box when it applies; the key line in bold, which is the one fact that identifies that class of object (§7.6); a detail line; and a footer ending in the FEB mark. When the name needs two lines, the detail line folds into the footer. The QR code sits on the right (R11, `labelMarkup`).
- **Class word**: the word for what kind of object a record is: PART, MOLD, WORK ORDER, TEST PANEL, STUDY, COUPON, FABRIC, RESIN (which covers hardener; the key line says which), CONSUMABLE, BOARD, JIG, STORAGE. The app derives it from the ID prefix and shows it on the public scan page and in the app. It is not printed on the label, except on a storage location, whose key line reads STORAGE (R11, `labelLines`). Every other label leads with the name, because the label's vertical space is spent (R11). The list maps one-to-one onto ID prefixes. Records that are not physical objects have no class word and never get a label (§2), so `PROJ-SN6-007` never sits on a shelf where it could be read as `P-SN6-007`.
- **QR code**: encodes `HTTPS://FEB-COMPOSITES.WEB.APP/Q/<ID>`. Uppercase, no query string, no fragment. Scanning it with any phone camera opens a public page naming the object, with no account needed. On a weak connection the page still shows the class and ID, because those come from the code itself; with no connection at all the phone cannot open the page, so read the label. This is also why the R&D mark below is printed beside the code and never encoded into it: a suffix costs a character budget and an error-correction level, a query string leaves alphanumeric mode entirely, and either would make reclassifying a build a relabelling job. The mark is on the card and mirrored to the scan page; the code itself never changes.
- **Mark**: a hand-written identifier in oil-based paint marker, used where a label cannot go (§7.4, §7.7).
- **R&D mark**: the word `R&D`, in a ruled box on the ID line of the label, for an object built under an R&D work order (CS-013 §4). It is not a class word and must never join the list above: the class-

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
word list maps one-to-one onto ID prefixes and must never change under the reader, whereas R&D qualifies a class. There is no such thing as an `R&D PART` class: there is a PART that is marked R&D. On the printed traveler the same fact reads in full: `R&D — NOT A SEASON DELIVERABLE`.
- **Engraving**: the ID cut into a mold during machining. The record of record (§7.4).
- **EH&S tag**: the UC EH&S barcode sticker that campus (RSS Chemicals) puts on every chemical container at RFS and on some storage sublocations. A Data Matrix square marked RSS, with a 24-character code of uppercase letters and digits printed underneath in six groups of four, and the last twelve characters reprinted, rotated, down the right edge (the edge print). Example, made up: `CA00 0000 0000 0000 0024 3F1C`, edge print `0000 0024 3F1C`. The app stores it in the record's EH&S barcode field as a second identity for the container (R11, `core.js` `EHS_LEN`, `EHS_TAIL`). FEB never prints one.
- **Data Matrix**: the square 2-D code on an EH&S tag. FEB's own labels are QR. The app's scanner reads both.

![Label anatomy: name, ID line with the R&D box, key line, detail line and footer, beside the QR code. No class word is printed. The ID line is the only capped line, which is why the R&D mark lives there.](figures/cs001-label-anatomy.v2.png)

> The QR payload must stay inside QR alphanumeric mode (`0-9 A-Z space $%*+-./:`, per R8). One lowercase letter, one `?utm=`, or a `#` fragment pushes the code from version 3 to version 4 and drops its error correction from 25% to 15%, at the same physical size. The printed label looks identical and simply scans worse once it has resin on it. The app draws the code at 21.4 mm (27 mm on 5522) and refuses to draw one below 14 mm, with the 4-module quiet zone inside the label (R11, `QR_MIN_MM`, `LABEL_ROLLS`); do not trim a label into that margin.

Survives a hardener drip; paper does not. The extra third of an inch lets the app draw the QR at 27 mm instead of 21.4 mm (R11). |

Not required to start: §7.8 is the documented zero-cost path and stays the fallback. The app has no printer address to set: if the printer does not appear in the print dialog, it is off the network (Reports → Label media). |
| Roll stock, everyday | Brother DK-2210, 29 mm continuous direct-thermal paper, cut at 101.6 mm | With the printer (CS-012) | The Avery 5161 cell to within a millimetre, so the same label on different paper (R11, `LABEL_ROLLS`). Direct thermal fades in UV, blackens with heat and smears under solvent (R11, app README Labels), so it is for shelves, bins, dry fabric and consumables only. |
| Roll stock, fallback | Brother DK-1201, 29 × 90 mm die-cut direct-thermal | With the printer (CS-012) | Only if iOS refuses a custom length on continuous stock. 86.6 mm of printable length against 101.6 mm, so long names drop to two lines sooner (R11). Same thermal limits as DK-2210. |
| Tags | Laminating pouches and 100 mm zip ties | Campus store | For anything tag-able: rolls, remnants, bins, coupon sets. |

The label printer and its rolls go through CS-012 like any other purchase. Nothing else on this list needs ordering approval.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
Labeling has no physical hazards of its own. Three rules exist to stop labeling from *creating* hazards or scrap:

1. **Never label a mold's working surface.** Anything on the tool face telegraphs through into the part; a 0.08 mm label edge prints through two plies.
2. **Never label within 40 mm of a flange perimeter, on either face.** Tacky tape is 12.7 mm (1/2 in) wide (R12), and a label edge under or across the seal is a leak channel you will not find at 27 inHg. CS-006 §7.4 step 3 already names tacky-tape seams as the first place to hunt leaks; do not add a second cause.
3. **No silicone-adhesive tape anywhere in the shop**, which is Kapton and most amber films. Trace silicone causes fisheyes in clear coat and kills DP420 adhesion. Its heat resistance buys nothing here: there is no oven and no post-cure (CS-008 §5.1).

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
1. Open the record and press Label: on a work order, part, mold, board, test panel, jig, storage location or material lot. On an R&D study press Study label; on a coupon, press the print icon on its row. For several at once, press Labels on Inventory (and on its Items list and Materials list) or on Molds, or Label sheet under Reports → Labels. Labels and Label sheet open the Print labels builder.
2. Choose the stock. The Label button prints on this device's media, set under Reports → Label media ("This device prints to"). A lead's Team default only seeds a device nobody has set. To print one record on a different stock, such as 5522 from a device set to the roll, open the builder and pick it under Media. Avery 5161 is the everyday sheet; 5522 is for anything that will see IPA, acetone or resin (§7.2 stock rule).
3. On a sheet, in the Print labels builder (a record's own Label button always starts at cell 1): if the sheet has already been partly used, set Start at cell to the first unused one. A three-label batch onto a fresh sheet wastes seventeen.
4. On a sheet: leave Include the 100 mm calibration bar ticked in the builder (a record's own Label button always prints it). Print, then measure the bar with a steel rule: it must be exactly 100 mm. If it is not, the browser applied "Fit to page" scaling and every label on the sheet is misregistered. Set printer scaling to 100% or Actual Size and reprint.
5. Peel and apply per §7.2.
6. On a roll (DK-2210 or DK-1201): there is no Start at cell and no calibration bar. For more than one of each, use the builder and set Copies of each (1 to 50, R11 `LABEL_COPIES_MAX`).
7. On a roll: in the preview press Print, and choose the Brother QL in the phone's print dialog.
8. On a roll: measure the first label of the session with a steel rule. On DK-2210 it must be 101.6 mm (R11, `LABEL_ROLLS`). Short or long means the print dialog scaled it; set scaling to 100% and reprint. Then apply per §7.2.

> Browsers apply that scaling silently. Ten seconds with a rule is cheaper than a wasted sheet of polyester.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling

sections.text:

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.2 Where each class of object gets its label (2/2)
sections.text:
-clamping face | Printed; stamped aluminium if it outlives the season |

**Stock rule.** Anything that will see IPA, acetone or resin shall get a 5522 polyester label, or a §7.8 overlaminated sheet label where 5522 is not on hand, never direct-thermal roll stock (DK-2210, DK-1201). Thermal paper fades in UV, blackens with heat and smears under solvent (R11, app README Labels). Roll stock is for shelves, bins, dry fabric and consumables.

> A coupon label in the gauge section changes the cross-section and can seed the failure; in the grip section it changes thickness and causes slip (R9). Marker on the tab is the only correct answer.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.3 Engrave, encapsulate or laminate: choosing the label method
sections.text: The durable answer for a tool is subtractive: engrave it. For a part it is encapsulation: put the label under the clear coat. For everything else it is laminated or polyester media, with thermal roll stock only for dry indoor things (§7.2 stock rule). Choose in that order.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.4 A mold is identified three times (1/2)
sections.text:
There is no moment when a flange label is clean: XCR goes over the whole working surface and the flanges, then four coats of wax, then PVA. So a mold gets three artifacts with three lifetimes. Before any of them, each blank is marked as it comes off the saw (CS-003 §7.3 step 4): its mold ID (or the plan name) and its layer tag from the cut sheet (L1, L2b), in paint marker, so the loose blanks for several molds cannot be mixed up before glue-up. Step 1 then marks the glued stack.

![Where a mold's identity lives, and the two keep-out zones: never the working surface, never within 40 mm of the flange perimeter on either face.](figures/cs001-mold-identity.v2.png)

1. **At glue-up (CS-003 §7.3).** Mark the mold ID (`MOLD-SN6-###`), the part name, the WO and an up arrow in paint marker, 15 mm characters, on two adjacent side faces of the glued stack. Between glue-up and the CNC slot a glued block sits on a shelf beside three other glued blocks, which is the highest-confusion and lowest-cost-to-fix moment in the whole process. Mark faces the toolpath will remove less than 6 mm from, or mark the bottom.
2. **At machining (CS-005).** Engrave the mold ID on the back face: 6 mm cap height, 1.0 mm deep, single-line font, 3.175 mm ball or 90° V-bit. The machine is already set up and the part already fixtured, so it costs about 90 seconds. This is the record of record. It survives IPA, acetone, four coats of wax, PVA, sanding, the label falling off, and the printer being broken. Every other layer is a convenience wrapped around it.
3. **At the end of sealing (CS-004 §7.5 Identify).** After the fourth wax coat is buffed and the PVA is dry, so every wet operation is finished. Scuff a patch of the back face to 220 grit, wipe with IPA, apply the printed 5522 label. Tooling board is porous; without the scuff the adhesive has nothing to key into and the label curls off within a month.

> Do not apply the printed label before sealing. It either gets brushed over with XCR, becoming a permanent bump in the seal coat, or it gets peeled off and leaves adhesive that XCR will not wet out.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.4 A mold is identified three times (2/2)
sections.text: **Re-sealing.** When a mold is stripped and re-sealed, the old label comes off with the strip and a new one is printed, carrying the incremented parts-pulled count and the new seal date. That is a feature: a label reading `SEALED 2025-11-02 · J LEE · USES 09` is telling you something important, and forcing the reprint is how it stays true.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.5 A part's label moves once, by printing two
sections.text:
Do not peel and re-stick. A label peeled off a demolded part carries wax and PVA on its adhesive. It will not restick to a freshly sanded face, and if it does, it puts release agent onto a surface about to be clear-coated.

1. **At demold (CS-006 / CS-007).** Print two identical labels on 5522 (use the Print labels builder and §7.1 step 3 for a second print on the same sheet). Apply label A to the trim area on the bag side, inside the CAD trim line. Staple label B to the work order traveler.
2. **At trim (CS-009).** Label A is cut off and discarded with the trim. Identity now lives on the traveler, which is physically with the part.
3. **After sanding, before clear coat (CS-009).** Apply label B to the scuffed, IPA-wiped hidden face.
4. **Clear coat (CS-009).** The acrylic urethane goes over label B where geometry allows, encapsulating it permanently.

The pair is 5522 because label B goes under clear coat (§7.2 stock rule). On a sheet the app prints one label per record, so the second label is a second print. On a roll, Copies of each set to 2 prints the pair, but roll stock is thermal paper, so a roll pair serves only a part that will not be wiped or clear-coated.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
Every label carries the name and the ID. The bold key line under those is the one fact that identifies that class of object, and it is the reason the label is worth printing:

| Class | The identifying fact |
|---|---|
| Part, test panel | The layup stack, in CS-002 shorthand (`6X 195 TWILL + .125 NOMEX`) |
| Mold | The sealing record: sealed date, by whom, parts pulled, revision |
| Fabric | No key line (dry fabric has no ratio or role); the vendor lot number is on the detail line under the ID; received date and shelf in the footer. Dry fabric has no expiry field (R11, `shop.js`). |
| Resin, hardener, consumable with no EH&S tag | The vendor lot number and opened date, on the line under the bold mix ratio and role; received date, expiry and shelf in the footer. A container wearing an EH&S tag gets no FEB label (§7.2). |
| Board, remnant | Density in the key line; dimensions and quantity beneath; the mold it came off and its shelf in the footer |
| Storage location | Key line STORAGE; site and kind of location, and `FLAMMABLES OK` when the shelf is rated for flammables. The footer reads `CONTENTS CONFIRMED <date>` after a walk (§7.10), or `CONTENTS LISTED IN THE APP` before the first one; the contents show when scanned in the app, not on the public page. |

"What layup stack was used for seat last year" is the question PP-09 records nobody being able to answer. It is on the label, so it can be answered with the phone still in your pocket.

The vendor lot and expiry print from whatever the record holds. If they were filled by ✨ Read label on the lot's page, check them against the container before printing. CS-014 owns that rule for every AI fill.

**R&D builds.** A part, panel or mold produced under an R&D work order (CS-013 §4) carries the mark `R&D` in a ruled box on the ID line, to the right of the ID. It sits there rather than on any content line for two reasons. The ID is the only line on the label whose length is capped (14 characters, CS-013 §4.1), so it is the one place a mark can be put and guaranteed never to truncate; the name, the key line and the footer cut long content short, and the detail line folds into the footer whenever the name needs two lines. And R&D qualifies the object's identity, not the fact printed beneath it. The mark never displaces the identifying fact above, and never displaces the FEB mark.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
The mark says the part is not a season deliverable. It does not say the part is scrap, a mock-up, a draft, or exempt from this standard. An R&D part is real carbon with a real cost, and it gets the same label, the same record and the same traceability as anything else on the shelf.

**Coupons.** Write every coupon ID on the panel before the first cut, across the cut lines, so each piece inherits a legible fragment. A coupon is `CPN-SNx-###`, its own record on the app's R&D bench under a study `RDS-SNx-###` (CS-013 §4.1). At eleven characters both fit the QR budget, so their printed labels carry a QR like everything else; the label goes on the coupon's bag or tag and the study's on the tray, never on the specimen (§7.2). The retired `PNL-SNx-###-Cnn` spelling was 15 characters, over budget, which is why SN5-era coupon labels are text-only.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
A pot of XCR has an 8 minute pot life at 20 °C (CS-004 §7.3). Printing a label for it is a process smell: it means someone stood at a printer while pot life burned. Write on the cup:

```
IN2 2142 JS product · time mixed (HHMM, 24 h) · initials
XCR 0906 SS 140g add batch mass where CS-004 §7.3 requires it
```

Four characters of time is what a gloved hand will actually write on a curved cup, and the minute is the only granularity that answers what a pot label is asked: is this still good, and whose is it. Anything unlabeled and curing is treated as hot waste (CS-008).

Anything opened but not given a lot record gets an opened sticker: `OPEN 2026-10-14 JS`.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.8 When there is no label printer
sections.text:
This is the documented path, not a degraded one, and it stays the fallback after a printer is bought.

1. Print the label sheet on plain paper from the app.
2. Cut on the guillotine, on the crop marks. Not with scissors.
3. Overlaminate with 3 in clear packing tape, overlapping the label by at least 6 mm on all four sides, so the paper is fully encapsulated with no exposed edge anywhere. Burnish hard with a thumbnail.

> Done this way it survives repeated IPA wipes, CF dust and compressed air for months, because the solvent never reaches paper or toner. Done wrong, with the tape flush to the label edge, solvent wicks underneath and it delaminates in a week. 2 in tape over a 2 in label is exactly wrong.

For anything tag-able, a laminating pouch on a zip tie beats packing tape, because the lamination seals all four edges. Punch the hole through the sealed margin, never through the paper.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.9 When the printer breaks the week before comp
sections.text:
In order:

1. **The spare roll**, taped to the printer in a bag, permanently, never allowed to become the working roll. Most of "the label printer is broken" is an empty or jammed roll, or a printer that has dropped off the shed wifi and so does not appear in the print dialog.
2. **Avery 5161 on the office laser** through the app (pick 5161 under Media in the builder if the device is set to the roll), with the §7.8 overlaminate. Full fidelity, one grade down in durability, and no purchase decision at 11 pm. Keep one unopened box in the cabinet.
3. **Paint marker on masking tape.** Always works, never scannable, acceptable for 72 hours.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.10 Labeling a shelf or storage location
sections.text:
Every shelf, bin and rack holding tracked composites material gets a storage record and a label on its front edge, printed from that record and not from Custom label (§7.13). That is what turns the location field into a controlled value rather than the freeform string CS-011 §7.3 flags, and it is what lets a move be recorded by scanning the object and then the shelf (§7.12).

1. On Inventory → Storage map, press + Location and fill in Name, Site, Type and Rated for flammables.
2. On the location's page, press Label. Fix it to the front edge of the shelf, readable standing up.
3. If campus has put an RSS tag on the shelf or cabinet, press Edit location and enter that tag in EH&S barcode (or use the scan button beside it, Scan the EH&S tag), so either tag finds the shelf.
4. After a stock walk, press Confirm contents on the shelf's page. The confirmed date prints in the label's footer (§7.6), so it is only as current as the last reprint.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.section: 7.11 Chemical containers and the UC EH&S tag
sections.text:
Campus EH&S (RSS Chemicals) puts a tag on every chemical container at RFS. That tag is the container's label, and FEB does not add a second sticker to a tagged container (§7.2). The app stores the tag on the lot record, in EH&S barcode, so scanning the campus tag opens the FEB record. Resin, hardener and consumable lots and storage locations carry that field; fabric lots do not, because dry fabric is not in the campus chemical system (R11). The receiving desk itself, the RSS import and the reconciliation export are CS-014.

![Two codes on one container: the FEB QR label and the UC EH&S Data Matrix tag, and what each one opens when scanned.](figures/cs001-two-codes.v2.png)

1. At receiving, press Receive a delivery on Inventory to open the Receiving desk. Scan or type each container's tag into the EH&S tag cell of its line. The scan button beside the cell (Scan the tag(s) with the camera) stays open across codes. A line for several containers takes several codes, separated by spaces or commas, dealt to the records in order.
2. For a container already on a shelf: open its record, press Edit, and press the scan button beside EH&S barcode (Scan the EH&S tag), or type the code.
3. If the face of the tag is scuffed or wrapped round a bottle neck, type the twelve characters printed down its right edge. Twelve is the fewest the app matches as part of a code; if two containers share those twelve, it refuses and asks for more of the code (R11, `core.js` `EHS_TAIL`).
4. One tag, one container. The app refuses a tag that another record already wears and names that record. Fix whichever record is wrong; never put one code on two records.
5. A tag no record wears, scanned with the app's Scan, offers Log it, which opens the Receiving desk with the code already in the tag cell. Log the container there (CS-014).
6. A code that is not 24 characters saves with a warning, because older hand-entered codes are shorter and real. Check it against the tag before moving on.
7. A chemical container with no tag yet gets a 5522 FEB label (§7.2). When campus tags it, enter the tag in EH&S barcode and leave the FEB label on: a label is never peeled off (§7.5).

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
There are two ways to scan, and they open different things. A phone's own camera pointed at an FEB QR opens the public page for that record (§9): no account, but it needs a connection. Inside the app, the scan button in the top bar (Scan a label) opens Scan, which reads an FEB QR or a UC EH&S tag and opens the record itself. On an iPhone the app loads its scanner the first time, which takes a few seconds.

![How the app resolves a scanned code: an FEB /Q/ link opens the record it names; otherwise an exact EH&S tag; otherwise a 12-character edge print (refused if it matches two containers); an unknown tag offers "Log it" at the Receiving desk.](figures/cs001-scan-chain.v2.png)

1. To open a record, press the top-bar scan button and point the camera at the label.
2. To move one thing, open it (a mold, item or lot), press Move, then Scan the shelf and point the camera at the shelf's label. Picking the shelf under Location and pressing Move it does the same without the camera.
3. To restock a shelf, open the shelf's page from Inventory → Storage map, press Move here (scan), and scan each thing as you put it on the shelf. The camera stays open and each scan saves as it lands; press Cancel to close the camera when the pile is done.
4. Either code works at either end: the FEB QR or the UC EH&S tag on a container, and the shelf's FEB label or its RSS tag once that is recorded (§7.10 step 3).
5. If the camera will not open or will not read the code, type it into "…or type the code" and press Use this code: the ID (`MOLD-SN6-004`), or a tag's last twelve characters. The app accepts the full URL, the bare ID, lowercase, or spaces.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
Custom label prints typed text with no record behind it: a cabinet sign, a warning such as DO NOT CUT, a bin of untracked things. It is on the Inventory toolbar, on a storage location's page, and under Reports → Labels. Its fields are Name (the big line), Second line, Key line (bold), Footer, QR (optional), Media, and Copies (roll media only); Print one again lists the last ten printed on this device.

1. Custom label shall not be used for anything that has a record. Open the record and press its own Label, which prints the identifying fact and a QR that resolves.
2. A custom label shall not carry an ID-shaped line. The app enforces this on the Second line: a real ID is sent back to its record's Label button, and an invented one is refused outright (R11, `clProblem`).
3. A shelf that holds tracked material gets a storage record and its own Label (§7.10), not a custom label.
4. The QR text can carry only `0-9 A-Z space $%*+-./:` (R8); anything else, such as `?`, `#`, `&` or `_`, is refused (R11, `clQrTrouble`). Lowercase is uppercased. The app refuses a code whose modules would come out under 0.4 mm at the label's QR size; shorten the text.
5. With no printer at all, paint marker on masking tape (§7.9 step 3) does the same job for 72 hours.

sections.title: CS-001 Part, Mold & Material Labeling
sections.text:
The labels themselves, the records they point at, and the location field on each record, which is what the monthly stock walk checks against. A scan of any label resolves to the public page for that record, so a stock walk can be done with a phone, a connection and no account. Beside those, the app keeps:

- **EH&S barcode** on resin, hardener and consumable lots and on storage locations. It is the join key between FEB's records and campus's RSS Chemicals inventory (Inventory → Export → EH&S reconciliation; CS-014).
- **The public nameplate** for every labelled record, which is what a phone-camera scan opens. It shows the class, ID and name, then Stage, Location (the shelf's name), Work order, Revision, Updated, and the R&D note on an R&D build. It never shows a layup stack, a sealing record or a person (R11, `pubProjection`; `firestore.rules` `/pub`). A lead rebuilds every nameplate with Rebuild scan mirror under Reports → Maintenance.
- **Contents last confirmed** and **Confirmed by** on each storage location, stamped by Confirm contents (§7.10 step 4).

A label that scans to "No record with this ID yet" on the public page was printed before its record was saved, belongs to another season, belongs to a deleted record, or is waiting on Rebuild scan mirror. Scanned inside the app, a deleted record's label says who deleted it and when. Restore it under Reports → Recently deleted, where a deleted record stays for 30 days (R11, `core.js` `TRASH_DAYS`). Do not relabel; restore.

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text: In SN5 our stacks lived in the tracker as shorthand ("6X 195 + CORE", "195 88 .25 NOMEX"). That's the *intent*, not what actually got laid. Orientations, core placement, where the copper mesh went, what we substituted when we ran out of cloth: all of it lived in people's heads. That's how the dashboard got remade 3+ times against a spec that existed nowhere (PP-04), how the UT stack was still up in the air three weeks before layup (PP-07), and why nobody could answer "what stack did the seat use last year?" (PP-09). This doc is how we write a stack down before we build, and record what we actually did after.

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text:
- **Stack / layup schedule**: the full ordered list of plies from mold surface (P1) outward, including cores, meshes, and inserts.
- **Orientation**: warp direction relative to the part's marked 0° datum. For woven cloth use 0/90 or ±45; for spread-tow/UD state the fiber direction.
- **Cloth naming**: `<gsm> <weave>` from the team's stock: 88 spread-tow, 195 twill, 220 twill, 670 twill (Sigmatex); always gsm, never "the thick one". A cloth whose gsm has not been measured yet is written by type and source until it is, for example `UD carbon, ACP, gsm TBD`. Measuring it is a task to assign, not a footnote.
- **Inserts**: a G10 (or other) insert is a ply in the table like a core, with its material and thickness written in the row. A thickness mismatch between an insert and the core around it is a deviation to record (§7.4).
- **ME / RE**: the part's Mold Engineer (ME) and Manufacturing Engineer (RE), the two engineer fields on the part and on each of its runs. Both are picked from the app's roster, not typed (CS-013 §4).
- **Plan and as-built**: the plan is the stack on the part (Parts tab, Layup stack). The as-built is the copy each run takes when it is started (from the plan, or from a previous run if chosen), kept in the run's Stack & BOM section. Editing the run's copy never changes the plan.
- **Stack freeze**: the buy-off of the Stack frozen step on a run (§7.2). From then on, edits to the part's plan no longer reach that run, and the run's stack changes only as §7.2 steps 3 to 6 say.

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text: None; this is a specification standard. The planned stack lives on the part (Parts tab, Layup stack section, R5). Each run (work order) gets a copy when it is started with + New run, and that copy becomes the run's as-built record in its Stack & BOM section (CS-013 §7.1, §7.2). On a part that already has runs, + New run asks for a Starting point: Start fresh copies the plan; Use a previous run can copy that run's Layup stack as laid and BOM instead, and the new run then starts as as-built.

sections.text: No physical hazards; specification standard. Shop-floor safety lives in the process standards it feeds (CS-006, CS-007).

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text:
1. The part's Manufacturing Engineer (RE) drafts the stack on the part: Parts tab, Layup stack, + ply, one row per ply from the mold surface outward, in the format of §7.3.
2. Justify the choice in one or two lines per decision: coupon data (R4), the SN5 as-built for a similar part (its WO), or an explicit assumption flagged for testing. New unproven stacks on schedule-critical parts require a coupon or test panel first.
3. Include function plies explicitly: sacrificial 88 spread-tow outer layers for sanding protection, copper mesh position and overlap for grounded parts (CS-010), core chamfers/grooves.
4. State the target: cured thickness (mm), mass (g), and any acceptance measurement (e.g. grounding Ω per CS-010).

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text:
1. **The stack freezes before mold machining starts.** Mold geometry (offsets, flange height) can depend on stack thickness, and machine slots are too scarce to cut twice (PP-03, PP-06). For mold-less flat panels, freeze before cloth is cut. Inside a run the app holds this order: Stack frozen is a blocker ahead of the mold steps. A mold advanced on the Molds tab or from the cut list is not checked against it, so the lead checks those at the weekly meeting (§8).
2. The freeze is the buy-off of the Stack frozen step on the run. Before signing, the signer shall have agreed the stack with the RE and the Composites Lead (plus the requesting subteam's lead for cross-team parts, the dashboard lesson, PP-04), and shall name them in the step's note. The app refuses a member's signature while the run has no plies; a lead can sign without it (Sign without it), with the reason logged in the work order's event log. The note naming who agreed is this standard's requirement, not the app's.
3. Every stack-freeze date appears as a deadline in the Schedule tab, reviewed at the weekly meeting (PP-07). A frozen stack changes only by a run revision (steps 4 to 6): quick to do, but visible and counted.
4. Edit the run's stack in Stack & BOM. The run then shows how many plies differ from the part's plan.
5. Raise the run's Revision by one letter in its Details, and write why in the run's Notes.
6. If future runs should follow the change, press Compare on the run's stack, then Adopt as the part's plan.

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text:
1. During layup, the RE checks each ply against the run's stack in Stack & BOM. Any change (substituted cloth, extra ply, mesh moved) is edited into the run's stack row by row, with the reason in that ply's Notes cell. The RE may also tick each ply in pen on the printed traveler. No deviation is too small to note: "we were out of 195 so used 220" is exactly the data that explains a mass or thickness surprise later.
2. Photograph the stack at: cores/mesh placed, and bagged-before-infusion. Photos attach to the WO steps.
3. After cure, record actual mass and thickness next to targets in the run's Quality section.
4. At the buy-off that starts the cure (Infuse, Wet layup and bag or Wet layup over core), confirm or correct Materials used for each BOM line. The app prefills each line from the plan; a blank means not measured, and stays that way in the record.
5. If this run proved a BOM line of the plan wrong, press ↩ plan on that line, so the next run starts from what this one learned. The button shows once a line's used quantity differs from the plan.
6. If this run proved the plan's stack wrong, press Compare on the run's stack, then Adopt as the part's plan.

![Plan and as-built: the part's Layup stack and Materials (plan) are copied into each run at + New run (or a previous run's are, if chosen); the run's edits make it as-built with a count of plies that differ; Adopt as the part's plan and ↩ plan carry a run's changes back; Stack frozen stops later plan edits reaching the run.](figures/cs002-plan-asbuilt.v2.png)

sections.title: CS-002 Layup Schedule Specification & Recording
sections.text:
A coupon is `CPN-SNx-###`: its own record on the app's R&D bench, belonging to a study `RDS-SNx-###` (CS-013 §4.1). The study's Materials carry the Layup stack (as text, in the §7.3 order from P1 outward, or the ID of the run whose panel the coupons were cut from), the Fabric lot, Resin lot and Hardener lot, the Lot record, Laid up on and Laid up by. Every coupon inherits them. A coupon that was different says so in its own row, and clearing that cell hands it back to the study. That inheritance is what makes one coupon ID enough to recover the whole build. (The retired suffix spelling `PNL-SNx-###-Cnn` survives only on frozen SN5-era records.)

1. **Write every coupon ID on the panel before the first cut**, across the cut lines, so each piece inherits a legible fragment. After the saw there is no way to recover which piece was which.
2. Name the raw data file after the coupon: `CPN-SN6-042.csv`. That one filename then carries the study, the stack, the session and the material lots, through one link each, none of them retyped.

> This is written against a real failure. The SN5 tensile set is seventeen CSVs named `TensileTesting_12_8_2025_<n>.csv` whose contents are Time, Displacement and Force with no header block and no specimen identity of any kind. The mapping from specimen to layup exists only in a Word table that contradicts itself. Untraceable test data is noise (§2).

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text: A mold error you find after machining burns our three scarcest things at once: tooling board, machine time, and calendar. The SN5 clamshell CAD error (raised middle section, Feb 2026) forced a re-glue and re-machine and killed a week of slots in our tightest month (PP-03). This doc collects our mold design rules and adds the one check that would have caught it: someone who didn't design the mold reviews it before any board gets glued or cut.

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text: Female/male molds machined from polyurethane tooling board (30–60 lb/ft³) for infusion and wet layup, including split molds for parts with an overhang (§7.1 step 4). Appendix A covers 3D-printed compression (forged CF) molds. Hotwire foam molds: out of scope (own project doc until standardized).

**Why Ure-Bond 90:** SN4's board-stacking method (vacuum-bag with laminating resin) was slow and resin-hungry (R2). Ure-Bond 90 (R1) is a purpose-made rigid urethane adhesive: strong bond between boards, ~4 h clamp time, no bagging. Dowels + spot resin remain acceptable for very large stacks where adhesive cost bites.

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
- **Flange**: flat margin around the part cavity for tacky tape, infusion lines, and trimming reference. 
- **Scribe line**: machined V-groove marking the part trim boundary and datums.
- **Stack (mold stock)**: tooling boards glued into a block thick enough for the mold.
- **Max-Z**: the machine's maximum cut depth; molds taller than max-Z must be split into sections with alignment datums, unless the split is waived (§7.1 step 6).
- **Mold record**: the mold's own record in the app, `MOLD-SN6-###`, on the Molds tab. It exists from the moment the stack is planned (§7.1 step 8) and is separate from any work order.
- **Mold file**: the mold's current stack plan, `STK-SN6-###`, shown under Mold file on the mold page. Older plans stay listed under Earlier and are marked Superseded.
- **Mold stage**: where a mold is in its life, set on the mold page. The track is Designed, Tooling cut, Board glued, Machined, Sealed, Ready for layup; Retired sits off the track (`app/shop.js`). Each step below names the stage it sets. A mold that will not be used again is retired, never deleted.
- **Datum cut plan**: the drawing of the reference cuts taken off a mold after a part comes out of it, attached on the mold page under Datum cut plans. Most molds never need one.

**Board grades:** grades shall not be swapped silently. Plan a mold at one grade, or give a range in the New mold dialog with Board density, min (lb/ft³) and Board density, max (lb/ft³). Inside that range any board may supply any blank, including two grades side by side in one layer. The densest board cut sets the feed for the whole stack (CS-005 §7.4); the app records it as the mold's Highest density cut when the boards are marked cut (`app/stock.js`).

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
- **Tooling-board dust** (gluing prep, any hand-shaping): abrasive and irritating, dust mask minimum, respirator + extraction for power sanding (CS-009 PPE table).
- **Ure-Bond 90** (R1, SDS `03 Datasheets/1386A_2-1386B_2.pdf`): two-part urethane. Part A contains MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate, CAS 101-68-8, 15 to 35 %), an isocyanate (SDS §3). Part A causes skin and eye irritation, may cause an allergic skin reaction, is harmful if inhaled, may cause allergy or asthma symptoms if inhaled, may irritate the airways, is suspected of causing cancer and may damage the airways through repeated exposure (H315, H319, H317, H332, H334, H335, H351, H373; SDS 1386A §2). Part B is not classified (SDS 1386B §2). Mix and glue only with room-size ventilation, and never heat or spray it: the TB warns the vapors become significant when heated or sprayed (`03 Datasheets/URE_BOND_90_TB.pdf`). Wear safety glasses with side shields (SDS 1386A §8) and long sleeves (TB). Gloves: the SDS names liquid-tight butyl rubber, neoprene or PVC gloves (SDS 1386A §8) and the TB says rubber gloves; neither names nitrile. Until the shop stocks one of those, wear the shop's nitrile gloves (team practice). You should wear butyl, neoprene or PVC gloves; they are on the purchase list. If the room cannot be ventilated, wear the CS-009 respirator (SDS P284). Eyes: flush with water for 15 min and get medical attention (TB). Skin: remove with soap and water (TB). Clamped assemblies stay put for 4 h (TB).
- **Past reaction or asthma:** anyone with asthma or a past reaction to isocyanates shall not mix Ure-Bond 90, and tells a lead (SDS 1386A §2, H334). There is other work on a gluing night.
- Heavy stacks: two people to move anything over ~half a sheet; watch pinch points at clamping.

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
1. Build the mold body from the part surface per the R3 process (section curves → loft → mirror); keep the machining time target ≤ ~3 h per mold section where practical.
2. **Flanges:** ≥75 mm flat margin beyond the part edge on all sides; tacky tape + spiral tubing + trim allowance need it (SN4 lesson: insufficient side stock, R2).
3. **Scribe lines:** machine part-boundary scribes parallel to ribs/features plus two datum scribes; they must survive sealing (CS-004 §7.3 step 5).
4. **No overhangs.** 3-axis machining only; check every face has positive draft from the machining direction. Target ≥2° draft on deep walls. A part with an overhang is made on a split mold: each piece has positive draft from its own machining direction, and the split line and its alignment features are designed in CAD.
5. **Foam support:** no unsupported sections thinner than 15 mm; tooling board snaps (R3). Fillet internal corners ≥ the finishing-tool radius.
6. **Max-Z check:** if mold height exceeds machine max-Z, split into sections in CAD with dowel/datum features designed in, not improvised at the machine (R2). The planner splits any stack over 6 in into sections automatically (`app/slicer.js`, 152.4 mm). Tick "Machined depth stays under 6in" in the mold dialog only when the design keeps the cutter within 6 in of a face it can reach (a shallow cavity in a tall blank, dowelled inserts, a face machined from both sides). The app records who ticked it and when, and shows the mold as split waived.
7. **Attachment/mounting points:** where the part needs marked hole locations (seat lesson, Oct 2025 meeting notes), design small conical divots into the mold surface.
8. **Stack plan:** plan the stack in the app before the §7.2 review.
 - On the Molds tab press + Mold. For an existing mold, a lead presses Re-plan (or Plan the stack, on a mold with no plan yet).
 - Start from an STL exported in millimetres with STL units set to millimetres (the app warns that a mismatch is a 25.4× mistake), from dimensions (X × Y × Z), or from the Fusion add-in (step 9).
 - Plan one body at a time. A multi-body STL asks "Which body?" and plans the one you pick.
 - With Boards set to choose them for me, from stock (the default), the planner picks thicknesses only from boards recorded in Inventory → Boards. I'll pick the thicknesses is not checked against the rack: use it only for boards you have in hand. E

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
ither way the planner splits any stack over 6 in (step 6) and creates the mold record at Designed, with the plan (`STK-SN6-###`) as its Mold file. Starting from nothing yet, just record the mold creates the mold at Designed with no Mold file; plan its stack before the §7.2 review.
 - STL planning is marked beta in the app. Check the Stack drawing on the mold page (under the heading Stack, below Mold in stock) before anyone cuts, and plan from dimensions if it looks wrong.
 - Re-plans are a lead's. The old plan stays under Earlier, marked Superseded. Cut and machine only from the current plan.
9. **Plan from Fusion:** install the FEBPlanStock add-in from Molds → Plan from Fusion (R8). In Fusion, open the mold design and press Utilities tab → FEB panel → Plan stock. Select the Mold body, one body at a time. Select the Bottom face too if the mold is not modelled bottom-down (a split mold on its side). Set density in the app's mold dialog that opens in the palette, and press Plan. The blanks come back as see-through bodies in a component named after the plan (`STK-SN6-###`); use them as CAM stock. The add-in saves nothing to the document: save it yourself.
10. **Split molds:** each piece of a split mold is its own mold record. Link every piece on the part page ("+ Link a mold…", then "+ Link another mold…"). A work order covers one mold, so the second piece gets its own run and its own §7.2 review. + New run fills in the part's first linked mold: on the second piece's run, set Mold ID in the run's Details to that piece's `MOLD-SN6-###`.

![The §7.1 design rules dimensioned on a mold section: flange width, draft, minimum section, fillets, scribes, and the max-Z ceiling, all from the one spindle direction that exists.](figures/cs003-mold-section.v2.png)

![Mold stages on the app's track: Designed, Tooling cut, Board glued, Machined, Sealed, Ready for layup, with Retired off to the side, what moves a mold to each stage, and the Mold design review blocker before any blank is cut.](figures/cs003-mold-stages.v2.png)

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
1. Before any blank is cut from the cut list, any stock is glued or any ShopSabre slot is booked, a reviewer who is not the mold's designer walks this checklist against the CAD and the mold's stack plan (10 minutes):

| # | Check |
|---|---|
| 1 | Part surface matches current part CAD revision (open both; overlay) |
| 2 | Flanges ≥75 mm all around |
| 3 | Scribe + datum lines present |
| 4 | No overhangs / negative draft from machining direction |
| 5 | No sections <15 mm; internal fillets ≥ tool radius |
| 6 | Height ≤ machine max-Z (value in CS-005 §5); or splits + alignment features designed; or a split waiver, with the reviewer having checked the deepest machined point and the tool's reach past the collet |
| 7 | Mold file (`STK-SN6-###`) exists and the Molds overview shows no Short N blanks (stock is recorded in Inventory → Boards) |
| 8 | Machining time estimate written in the work order's Machine mold step note (Glue and machine mold on a wet-layup run); there is no estimate field |
| 9 | Stack frozen per CS-002 §7.2 (mold offsets depend on it) |
| 10 | The plan is the mold's current Mold file, not one marked Superseded |
| 11 | In the Stack drawing on the mold page (under the heading Stack), the dashed mold outline sits inside every block |
| 12 | Every plan warning is fixed in CAD or answered in the Mold design review step note |

2. Reviewer initials the WO "Mold design review" step. No initials, no cutting, no glue, no booking.

The app holds Mold design review until the CAD is attached or linked on the work order and the signer holds Mold design training, which a lead grants on the People tab (`app/workorders.js`). A lead can sign without the CAD (Sign without it), and the reason goes in the work order's event log. If the signer is the run's Mold Engineer, the app asks Self-review and lets them press Sign it anyway; it does not refuse. Check that the Mold Engineer field names the mold's actual designer before relying on that warning. The cut list does not check the review at all, so check the run's Mold design review is signed before cutting any blank (§7.3 step 1).

sections.section: 7.3 Cutting blanks and gluing tooling board (Ure-Bond 90) (2/3)
sections.text:
1. Open Molds → Cut list. It offers only molds at Designed whose plan is not Superseded (`app/stock.js`). Cut only for molds whose Mold design review is signed (§7.2).
2. Press Print cut list. Before cutting to a sheet that has been in a drawer, check its batch tag (the four-character tag in the batch stamp) matches the rest of the set (R7).
3. Cut each board on a saw (the ShopSabre may be used) along the sheet's numbered cuts, all the way across each time. The cut list allows a 1/8 in kerf per cut (`app/packer.js`).
4. Before each blank leaves the saw, write its mold ID (or the plan name) and its layer tag from the cut sheet (L1, L2b) on it in oil-based paint marker (CS-001 §7.4).
5. Press "Mark these boards cut…".
6. Untick any board you did not cut.
7. Correct every offcut size, in millimetres, to the piece in your hand.
8. Press Mark cut. The app moves the mold to Tooling cut.
9. Press Print labels on the bar that appears and label each offcut now (CS-001).
10. To re-cut a mold, move its stage back to Designed on the mold page (the app asks first). It returns to the cut list.
11. Dry-fit boards; mark orientation.
12. Place each layer from its layer sheet in the mold's Drawings set: set the insets from the board below, then check the Datum A table. Datum A is the near-left corner of the stack (`app/drawings.js`). Blanks carry 1 to 2 in of margin past the mold and are rounded to a 1/2 in size (`app/slicer.js`), so a small shift still machines; the Datum A check catches a board sawn oversize.
13. Vacuum the faces, wipe them with IPA, and let the IPA flash off fully before glue touches them (TB: let the solvent fully dry).
14. Pre-mix Part B (TB).
15. Measure 1A:1B by volume, which is 100A:88B by weight (TB).
16. Mix for 3 min, scraping the sides and bottom of the container (TB). Pot life is 8 min at 73 °F (23 °C) (TB), so mix only what one joint takes.
17. Spread thin and even on one face, mate, and clamp evenly. 4 h clamp minimum (TB). For stacks >3 boards or very large molds: dowels + spot resin alternative (R2).
18. Mark the stack immediately, in oil-based paint marker, 15 mm characters, on two adjacent side faces: the mold ID (`MOLD-SN6-###`), part name, WO, and the up-direction (CS-001 §7.4). Mark faces the toolpath will remove less than 6 mm from, or mark the bottom.
19. Set the mold's stage to Board glued.
20. Write the mix time and clamp-off time in

the note on the work order's Glue mold stock step and sign it. On a wet-layup run, write them in the note on Glue and machine mold and sign that step after machining (CS-005 §7.5).
21. Do not machine until full cure: 16 h at 73 °F (23 °C) after glue-up (TB). The TB also calls the joint machinable at 4 h; that is the datasheet figure, and FEB waits for full cure.

> A Sharpie does not survive here. Between glue-up and the CNC slot a glued block sits on a shelf beside three other glued blocks, gets clamped, weighted and IPA-wiped, and the shop's own isopropyl dissolves a Sharpie mark. This is the highest-confusion and lowest-cost-to-fix moment in the whole mold process.

sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text:
The mold record (`MOLD-SN6-###`) holds the stage, Home location, Board density min and max, Highest density cut, Board layers, Sealing system, Sealed on, Sealed by, Parts pulled, the Mold file (`STK-SN6-###`) and any Datum cut plans. sections.title: CS-003 Mold Design & Manufacturing
sections.text: From the SN5 *Forged/Compression Molded Carbon Fiber* study: PLA/PETG molds (40–50% infill, 4–5 walls, 0.1 mm layers) are free at Jacobs but deform/crack at ~50–100 psi and soften at 60–100 °C, with no hydraulic press and no heated cure. Design: piston-into-cavity, stroke ≈ 2× part depth, 0.1 mm sliding-face offset, chamfered split points for wedging, vent grooves against hydrolock. Clamp math: four 600 lbf trigger clamps ≈ 2,400 lbf spread over the part area → ~150 psi at 4×4 in (16 in²) but only ~37 psi at 8×8 in (64 in²). Read the two limits together: parts must be small (≲24 in² for 100 psi, ≲48 in² for 50 psi) for clamps to even reach the 50–100 psi consolidation target, and at exactly those pressures a printed mold is at its cracking threshold. So for small forged parts, always distribute the load with through-bolts + aluminum backup plates rather than bare trigger clamps (whose pads also relax over time); for anything larger, clamps cannot reach target pressure at all, so redesign, or accept low-pressure quality. First-part failure mode to avoid: resin starvation (see CS-008 mix math).

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text: Mold surface prep was our single most expensive recurring problem in SN5 (PP-01). Duratec was pricey, pooled in crevices and hid our scribe lines, needed high-grit sanding on soft board, and we sanded through it constantly; every incident cost a day-plus re-coat cycle. In spring 2026 we switched to XCR coating resin: paint it on, no sand-back, better finish, better geometric accuracy. This doc locks that decision in and gives one procedure from "machined mold" to "ready for layup", so the reasoning doesn't get lost and re-argued next year.

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text: CNC-machined polyurethane tooling-board molds (30–60 lb/ft³, Coastal Enterprises stock) used for resin infusion or wet layup. Not covered: 3D-printed compression (forged CF) molds (CS-003 Appendix A) and hotwire foam male molds.

**Why these products:** XCR is a purpose-made brushable epoxy coating (R1) that cures to a hard surface without requiring sand-back. It fixes exactly the two Duratec failure modes (mandatory sanding on soft board; pooling that hides marks). The Rexco release system (R3–R5) is sponsor-supplied (~free) and wax + PVA film is the industry-standard belt-and-suspenders release for epoxy on epoxy-sealed molds.

**XCR key numbers (from R1 unless the row says otherwise):**

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
- **Sealing**: closing the open cells of machined tooling board so laminating resin cannot soak in and lock the part on.
- **Release system**: the sacrificial layers (wax, then PVA film) that let the cured part separate from the sealed mold.
- **Etch / scribe lines**: machined reference marks on the mold (part trim lines, datums). Preserving their visibility is a hard requirement of sealing.
- **B-stage / firm-but-tacky**: resin firm enough not to flow, soft enough to indent with a fingernail, slight surface tack: the correct state for overcoating (R1).

sections.text:

| Digital scale | 1 g resolution or better | RFS | Ratio errors = soft spots |
| Mixing cups ×2 per batch | Graduated | Consumables box | Double-pot per R1 (transfer + remix) |

![Sealing a mold from the board up: XCR coats with the fingernail check between them (firm but tacky: coat again with no prep), the 12 h FEB hold after the last coat, then wax and PVA, with the laminate last.](figures/cs004-seal-stack.v2.png)

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
Per R2 (XCR SDS §2): the resin and the hardener both cause allergic skin reactions (H317) and serious eye damage (H318). The hardener is corrosive and causes severe skin burns (H314). The resin is suspected of causing genetic defects (H341). Neither part is classified as a respiratory sensitizer (no H334), though the resin SDS §11.1 says it may be a respiratory tract sensitiser; the respirator rule below is for vapor. Repeated careless exposure can make you permanently allergic to epoxies, which ends your composites career.

- **Past reaction:** anyone who has had a skin reaction to epoxy shall not mix or brush XCR, and tells a lead (R2 §7.1). There is other work on a sealing night.
- **Gloves:** nitrile (chemical-resistant per EN ISO 374-1), always, both components and mixed resin. Change gloves if resin gets on them.
- **Ventilation:** use only with adequate ventilation (R2 §8.2). Seal molds in the open shop area or with doors open, not in a closed side room.
- **Respirator:** for prolonged brushing on large molds (undertray-scale) or poorly ventilated conditions, wear the team respirator with A-type (brown, EN 14387 A1) organic-vapor cartridges; dust filters alone do nothing against epoxy vapors.
- **Eyes:** safety glasses with side shields whenever XCR resin or hardener is open; prescription glasses are not eye protection. You should wear safety goggles with side protection (EN 166) when mixing or brushing XCR (R2 §8.2); goggles are on the purchase list.
- **Skin:** wash any skin contact immediately with soap and water (not solvent). Contaminated clothing stays at the shop (R2 P272).
- **Exotherm:** mixed XCR left in the pot self-accelerates (R1). Small batches, transfer to the surface promptly; if a cup gets hot/smokes, set it outside on concrete and let it finish; do not bin it hot (see CS-008).
- PVA/wax (R3–R5): low hazard; gloves and ventilation suffice.

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
1. Blow all dust off the mold with compressed air, including pockets and scribe lines. [held for Simon: vacuum instead, REGISTER R-004-15]
2. Wipe the entire surface with IPA-dampened microfiber cloth; repeat with a clean face until the cloth comes away clean.

> Never use acetone on tooling board (it attacks the board) and never use fibrous cloths/paper shop towels (strings pull out and embed in the surface): both are SN4-documented failure modes (R7).

3. From this point, gloves only; skin oils contaminate the surface.

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
1. Check every scribe line and datum is crisp and visible. Photograph the dry mold; this is the reference for "did sealing obscure anything".
2. Fill any machining defects/gouges per CS-003 before sealing.

[PHOTO: machined, cleaned mold with scribe lines visible, before sealing]

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.section: 7.3 Sealing with XCR: batch size, coats, overcoat window (1/2)
sections.text:
1. Confirm workspace is 15–30 °C and can stay ≥20 °C through the cure (R1). Both jugs, resin and hardener, are inside 15–30 °C before you mix; on a cold night, bring them in from storage first. Avoid a humid room (R1). Do not seal outdoors on cold evenings; R1 rates XCR for 15–30 °C only.
2. Batch size: mix 150 g or less at a time. Pot life at that size is only 8 minutes at 20 °C (4 at 30 °C), and a bigger batch is shorter-lived and hotter. A 150 g batch covers roughly a medium mold section per coat; mix again rather than mixing big. Record each batch mass on the WO.
3. Weigh XCR at 100:41 resin:hardener by weight (R1). Mix thoroughly ≥2 min, scraping walls and base; then double-pot: transfer to a second cup and remix with a fresh stick (R1). Unmixed streaks from cup walls are the classic soft-spot cause.
4. Brush a thin, even first coat over the whole working surface plus flanges, working quickly (see step 2's clock). Work resin *out of* corners and fillets: pooling in crevices is the Duratec failure mode we are not repeating; a thin coat that needs a second pass beats a thick coat that pools.
 How many coats: 30 lb board usually needs a second coat; 60 lb board often seals in one. Plan two coats on 45 lb board until the team has a record of it sealing in one (team rule). A mold cut from a range of grades seals like its softest board, so you should plan two coats if any of it is 30 or 45 lb (the mold's "Board density, min" and "Board density, max" fields show the range).
5. Watch scribe lines as you coat: they must remain visible. If a line floods, drag the brush along it to re-open the meniscus before the resin gels.
6. **Second coat timing:** overcoat when the first coat is firm but tacky: firm, soft enough to indent with a fingernail, a slight tack on the surface. At 20 °C that is usually about 2 h 50 after the coat went on (1 h 30 at 30 °C), but the clock is an estimate; check with a fingernail, and the state decides (R1). A coat applied in that state bonds chemically with no prep (R1).
 If the first coat has gone tack-free (coming back another day always means tack-free), recoat this way (R1):
 - Wait at least 9 h from application.
 - Key the surface with 120 grit.
 - Blow off the dust.
 - Wipe with IPA.
 - Recoat.
7. Wait out the FEB hold of 12 h after the last coat before the release system (§7.4) goes on (team hold, CS-008 §5). The datasheet gives i

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.section: 7.3 Sealing with XCR: batch size, coats, overcoat window (2/2)
sections.text:
nitial cure as 8 h 30 at 20 °C, handleable at about 9 h (R1); the 12 h is the team's margin over it. The app does not lock this hold, so write the last-coat time in the note on the work order's "Seal and release mold" step. Only if a run/nib formed: locally denib with ≥800 grit (team value), then re-wipe with IPA.
8. Keep water away from the sealed surface for 24 h (R1).

> Mix only a ≤150 g batch and get it out of the cup fast. At 8 minutes of pot life, a phone call is the difference between a coat and a smoking cup.

[PHOTO: first XCR coat going on, brush working resin out of a fillet]

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
1. On a fresh sealed mold, once the 12 h hold in §7.3 step 7 has passed: apply Formula Five wax per R4: thin film, let haze, buff with clean microfiber. 4 coats minimum on a new mold (team count; R4 asks for at least three), buffing between coats.
2. Wait at least 1 h after the last wax coat before the PVA goes on, so the wax solvents out-gas (R4; R3).
3. Apply Partall #10 PVA film per R3: thin, even coats; let each dry fully (it dries to a visible glossy film), about 15 to 45 min a coat (R3). 2 coats (team count; R3 gives a mist coat then flow coats on a new mold).
4. On a re-used sealed mold: clean with Clean 'N Glaze (R5), then 1–2 wax coats, the 1 h wait and PVA as above.
5. On the Molds tab, open the mold and set Sealing system = XCR, Sealed on = the date of the last XCR coat, Sealed by = you (pick yourself from the list), and Stage = Sealed. Write the XCR batch masses, coat count, coat times, and the wax and PVA coat counts in the note on the work order's "Seal and release mold" step.

[PHOTO: PVA film drying: even gloss, no fisheyes]

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text:
The last step, after every wet operation is finished. Doing it earlier does not work: a label applied before the XCR either gets brushed over, becoming a permanent bump in the seal coat, or gets peeled off and leaves adhesive the XCR will not wet out.

1. Choose a patch on the back face, inboard of the 40 mm keep-out at every edge (CS-001 §6 rule 2). Never the working surface. The keep-out is there because tacky tape is 12.7 mm wide, and a label edge under the seal is a leak channel you will not find at 27 inHg (CS-001 §6).
2. Scuff the patch to 220 grit and wipe with IPA. Tooling board is porous; without this the adhesive has nothing to key into and the label curls off within a month.
3. Print the mold's label from the app and apply it. Check the printed parts-pulled count, seal date and sealed-by name match what you just recorded.
4. Confirm the engraved ID from CS-005 is still legible. If machining or rework removed it, re-engrave or stamp before the mold leaves.
5. Set the mold's Stage to Ready for layup. It is now cleared for CS-006 (infusion) or CS-007 (wet layup).

> On a re-seal, the old label comes off with the strip and a new one is printed carrying the new seal date and the incremented parts-pulled count. A label reading `SEALED 2025-11-02 · J LEE · USES 09` is telling you something important, and reprinting is how it stays true.

sections.text:
| Check | Target | Method | Record where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scribe/datum visibility after sealing | All lines identifiable vs 7.2 photo | Visual compare | WO qualityChecks + photo |
| No pooling | No glossy pools in fillets/corners | Visual, raking light | WO qualityChecks |
| Cure | Fingernail does not mark surface, checked at or after the 12 h hold (CS-008 §5) and before the release system goes on | Press test on flange (not part surface) | WO step |
| Release film | Continuous PVA gloss, no fisheyes/dry patches | Visual | WO qualityChecks |
| First-article release (new mold or new product batch) | Test patch releases by hand | Small cured resin dab on flange, pop off | WO notes |

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text: The mold record carries Sealing system, Sealed on, Sealed by and Stage (§7.4 step 5, §7.5 step 5). The note on the work order's "Seal and release mold" step carries the XCR batch masses and count, coat count and coat times (in or out of the overcoat time), the last-coat time that starts the 12 h hold, and the wax and PVA coat counts. The work order also holds the 7.2 and 7.4 photos and the quality-check table. This is what makes "why did part X stick?" answerable in minutes.

sections.title: CS-004 Mold Sealing, Release & Surface Prep
sections.text: Duratec (SN4–early SN5): expensive, hid etch marks by pooling, mandatory high-grit sand-back on soft board, frequent sand-through → re-coat cycles. The Oct 2025 *Mold Sealer Alternatives* study recommended S120/water-based sealers as a cheap replacement; by Feb 2026 the team instead ordered XCR with the Easy Composites basket, first parts sealed with it in April 2026 ("Core and XCR has arrived, good to seal", #composites, 2026-04-28), and the undertray was coated with XCR in May. Root-cause note (PP-01): the durable fix wasn't the product swap itself but *owning the selection decision in a standard*, this document. If XCR is ever replaced, revise this standard (CS-000 §7.2), don't just switch cans.
