sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
- **WO ID**: `WO-SNx-###`, assigned from the app (or the next free number in the printed log). Never reused.
- **Part and run**: a part (`P-SNx-###`) is the durable thing the car needs. A run is one attempt at making it; the app's Work Orders tab calls a run a work order. A part has many runs, and each run belongs to one part (§7.1).
- **ME / RE**: the part's Mold Engineer (ME) and Manufacturing Engineer (RE), the two engineer fields on the part and on each of its runs. Both are roster picks (Person fields, below). Same definition as CS-002 §4.
- **Person fields**: every field that names a person (Mold Engineer, Manufacturing Engineer, Sealed by, Laid up by and the rest) is picked from the app's roster, not typed. Pick Use “name” only for someone who is not on the app.
- **Buy-off**: pressing a step's buy-off while signed in. The app stores the signer's name as it read at signing, their account, and the date and time; screens show the person's current roster name. Self-buy-off is allowed except on Mold design review (below). It isn't tamper-proof: any roster member can still edit any record, so treat it as "who was signed in when this was clicked," not a notarized signature.
- **Training to sign**: a step that names a training (the §7.5 table shows which built-in step needs which) can be bought off only by someone a lead has recorded as holding it on the People tab. A lead may sign without it, and must write why; the reason goes in the run's event log. A lead is not trained by being a lead. For the ShopSabre, the app's ShopSabre CNC training mirrors the RFS record, which CS-005 §4 names as the authority.
- **Independent design review**: Mold design review shall be bought off by someone other than the mold's designer, the part's Mold Engineer (CS-003 §7.2). The app only warns: when the run's Mold Engineer signs it, it asks "Self-review" ("You are this run's Mold Engineer…") with Sign it anyway, and it does not refuse. It reads only the Mold Engineer field, so the signer still checks who actually drew the CAD.
- **Blocker step**: a step that blocks everything after it until it's bought off (stack freeze, design review, drop test, and the acceptance criterion that opens the Other technique).
- **Cure hold**: the wait on the step after the one that starts a cure (Cure and demould, or Cure), as long as the team hold for the resin recorded at that buy-off (CS-008

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
§5.1). A member is refused with "Still curing". A lead can sign through it from "Demould early?" with a written reason, which goes in the event log.
- **OnHold** (run status): a run a person has parked. It blocks nothing in the app.
- **Evidence**: what a step needs before it can be signed. Stack frozen needs a layup stack; Mold design review needs the CAD, attached or linked; Machine mold, Glue and machine mold, the drop test and the acceptance criterion need a note on the step. A lead can Sign without it, with a written reason.
- **Retro WO**: a back-filled historical record (all `WO-SN5-*`); its unverifiable fields say "not recorded (retro)"; retro records are honest references, not exemplars of process compliance.
- **R&D part / R&D WO**: a build that feeds a decision rather than the car: coupon campaigns, flat test panels, layup trials, sealing and grounding experiments, mold shakedowns. An R&D build is real carbon, real machine time, real cost and a real deadline, with a full record under this standard.

An R&D part is not a bench coupon: a `CPN` record has no work order and enforces nothing (§2), while an R&D part keeps every blocker, hold and evidence check. R&D is a property of the object, not a status: a work order is R&D on the day it is a Draft and still R&D when it is Complete, and an R&D work order enforces its blockers, cure holds and evidence exactly like any other.

What an R&D part is not is a season deliverable. It is kept off the Season tab, the Google Sheet mirror, and the Parts and Work Orders lists; it lives on the R&D tab, and each of those two lists shows an R&D count that jumps there. It is counted and marked everywhere else, including the Dashboard and Reports, and marked `R&D` on screen, on the label (CS-001 §7.6), on the printed traveler and on the public scan page. The flag lives on the part; a work order inherits it from the part it builds, and a work order with no part carries its own.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
Until Rev C the only controlled identifier in the whole system was the WO ID. A mold was free text inside one work order, a material lot was the colour of its packaging, and a tensile coupon was a trailing integer in a filename. This is the grammar for all of it.

```
PREFIX-SNx-### e.g. MOLD-SN6-004, P-SN6-007, CPN-SN6-042
```

| Prefix | What it names |
|---|---|
| `WO` | a work order (the job) |
| `P` | a part |
| `MOLD` | a mold |
| `PNL` | a flat test panel |
| `BRD` | a tooling-board sheet or offcut |
| `FAB` | a fabric roll or usable offcut |
| `RSN` | a resin or hardener lot |
| `CON` | a consumable lot |
| `JIG` | a jig or fixture |
| `BIN` | a storage location |
| `RDS` | an R&D study: a named set of coupons. Labels the bag or tray they live in |
| `CPN` | one coupon: a single physical test piece, belonging to a study |
| `PROJ` | an issue (older records say ticket). Not a physical object, and never gets a printed label (CS-001 §4). |
| `STK` | a mold's stack plan: how the mold is cut from tooling board, shown as the Mold file. Not a physical object |
| `BUY` | a purchase. Not a physical object |
| `DOC` | a document on the Documents tab. Not a physical object |

Four rules:

1. **An ID names a physical object, never a job.** The one exception is `WO`, which is the job. Encode a work order into a part's ID and every re-lay either lies or forces a relabel. A `P` record names the part the car needs; each physical piece of it is told apart by the run that made it (rule 3). `PROJ`, `STK`, `BUY` and `DOC` name records that are not objects at all, and none of them gets a label.
2. **IDs are never reused**, across seasons or after a delete. The season segment (`SN5`, `SN6`) partitions the namespaces, so SN5 IDs are frozen and stay valid forever.
3. **A re-laid part is a new run, not a new part.** Scrap a layup for porosity and lay it again: dispose the issue on the failed run as Scrap, saying why it could not be saved (§7.6), then start a second run on the same part with + New run. The part keeps its `P` ID, and the run ID tells the two pieces of carbon apart. The mold's ID, the board's ID and every existing label are untouched.
4. **A remachined mold keeps its ID.** It is the same physical object at a new revision, so the revision letter changes and the label is reprinted; the ID does not move.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
An ID is capped at **14 characters** by the QR code: version 3 at 25% error correction holds 47 alphanumeric characters, of which the host takes 30 and `/Q/` takes 3. Everything above fits; `MOLD-SNx-###` at 12 characters is the longest. The retired coupon spelling `PNL-SNx-###-Cnn` was 15, one over budget, which is why those labels were text-only; it survives only on frozen SN5-era records (rule 2), and `tools/test_qr.mjs` keeps the 15-character form as a counterfactual so the cliff stays proven.

![The record graph for one job: the work order builds a part, points at a mold record, and consumes lots; a study's coupons are records of their own, inheriting the study's stack and lots. The rules under the boxes are §4.1's, drawn where they apply.](figures/cs013-records.v2.png)

Dates are **fields, never ID segments.** A session that starts 23:50 and ends 00:10 has two valid dates, and a date typed wrong into an ID can only be corrected with acetone, while a date typed wrong into a field is corrected with an edit.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text: The WO app (R2): a shared workspace at feb-composites.web.app, running on Firebase. Make an account on the sign-in page with New here? Create account: your name (it goes on your buy-offs), a username and a password. You start as a member and can work straight away. A lead makes someone a lead on the People tab, and removes someone who has left with Remove there; their name stays on every record they signed. View as guest reads the whole app and changes nothing, because every buy-off carries a name. Every edit saves live to a shared database, so the whole team sees the same record at once; there's nothing to import or merge. `work-orders.html` (R2b) still opens any exported JSON with no server at all, and stays useful as an offline archive viewer, but it's not where day-to-day work happens anymore. Printed WOs: any printer + a pen at RFS.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text: No physical hazards; process standard. (Safety content lives in the process standards each WO step cites.)

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. Make the part on the Parts tab with New Part (it gets `P-SN6-###`), or open the part if it exists.
2. On the part, fill the requirements before any work (this is the PP-04/PP-05 fix: requirements exist before work): Subteam, Layup type (which picks the technique, §7.5), Layup deadline, Mold Engineer and Manufacturing Engineer, Target weight (g), the Layup stack (per CS-002 §7.1) and Materials (plan).
3. Press + New run on the part. The run gets `WO-SN6-###` and copies the part's plan: engineers, deadline, mass target, technique, stack, BOM and the part's first mold. For a remake, choose Use a previous run as the starting point and tick what to carry; Start fresh copies the part's own plan.
4. On the run, set the quality checks with numeric targets in Quality (+ check). Mass is prefilled from the part's Target weight.
5. The run's steps come from its technique. If the checklist does not fit the job, fix the technique, not the run: pick the right Layup type before the run starts, or ask a lead to add a technique (§7.5). Members cannot delete steps. A step that does not apply is signed with a note saying why.
6. Cross-team parts: the requesting subteam's requirements (thickness, DXF rev, mass) go in the WO and their lead is named on the release sign-off.
7. If the build feeds a decision rather than the car, start it from the R&D tab with + Part or + Run (§4). A run started on an R&D part is R&D with nothing to remember. Until a part has a run, the R&D part checkbox on its page (in edit mode) can be flipped either way. After that, only a lead can press Move to season, once, and nothing moves a season part back. The part keeps its ID when it moves (§4.1 rule 2), so its label, its traveler and its QR all stay valid.

New WO on the Work Orders tab makes a run with no part. Use it only for a one-off job that will never be remade.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. Work the steps in order; blocker steps block until bought off (the app enforces this; on paper the blocker rows are shaded: no initials, no moving on).
2. Each step: buy-off (§4), a note, and photos. Press the camera on the step row (Add photos to this step) to attach photos straight from the phone; they land on that step and in the run's Photos section. Steps that need a note (machining, the drop test) also suggest a photo before signing; a photo is never required.
3. Deviations from the frozen stack or spec are a run revision, done as CS-002 §7.2 steps 4 to 6 say: quick, visible, counted.
4. **Which lots went in.** Buying off an infusion or a wet layup asks which fabric roll, which resin lot and which hardener lot, alongside the resin system and the finish time it already asked for. Each field is pre-filled with whatever is currently open, so the usual answer is one confirmation. "I don't know / not recorded" is a valid answer and is recorded as such. That is deliberate: a required field that can only be satisfied by naming a lot gets satisfied by naming the wrong one, and a confident wrong lot is worse than an honest gap (§8, and the same principle as the retro sentinel in §4). The same buy-off asks Materials used for each BOM line (CS-002 §7.4 step 4). A lot picked by scanning its label is recorded as scanned, so a checked lot and a remembered one read differently later.
5. Link the part to its mold records (`MOLD-SNx-###`) in the part's Mold section; a split mold is two links. Each run points at the one mold it was laid in, filled from the part's first mold; a run on the other half of a split mold is its own run. The mold's location, sealing record and Parts pulled count live on the mold, where they stay true across every work order that uses it, instead of being copied into each one.
6. Update the mold's location whenever it physically moves (PP-10). Scanning the mold and then the shelf is the fastest way and needs no typing.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. Fill the actuals in Quality (mass, thickness, Ω table, etc.), check the photos, and set the status to Complete. If an issue on the run is still open, the app opens the closeout list instead; dispose each one (§7.6).
2. Nothing to export by hand: every save writes straight to the shared database and is live for the whole team immediately. The durable archive is the lead's monthly Backup (header button; on a phone, Backup database in the ⋯ menu) into the team Drive: Firestore is reliable, but a plain JSON file nobody can lock the team out of is the backup that matters. Restore, lead-only, reads that file back.
3. Print one copy for the physical binder at RFS if the part is safety/inspection-relevant (mech tech evidence).

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. At the weekly meeting the lead brings the status board (Reports, Print status board) or shows it on screen, and clears the Dashboard's Stopped lane first: it lists every run held at a blocker nobody has signed. The board replaces re-asking "where is X?" and feeds the weekly summary.
2. The lead runs Backup (one click, header; on a phone, in the ⋯ menu) monthly; see §7.3. Nothing weekly is required since the database itself is always current; monthly is just the archive cadence.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
A technique is a checklist and the blockers and holds on it: each step's rule (blocker, starts the cure, or the cure hold), the evidence it needs and the training it needs to sign. A part's Layup type picks its technique, and a run copies the steps when it is created.

1. Anyone can read the techniques on the Reports tab under Layup techniques.
2. Only a lead changes them. Add a technique always starts from a copy (Name, Start from); Edit steps changes one; Archive hides a custom technique from new runs. Built-in techniques are never archived.
3. Editing a technique never changes a run that already exists. A run made on an older version says its checklist has changed and offers Add them for the new steps, touching nothing already signed.
4. A technique that lays up a stack shall keep its Stack frozen blocker ahead of the first physical step, and a technique with a drop-test blocker shall keep it ahead of the resin step. The step editor lets a lead remove either; this rule is what stops it. Mold wet lay and Foam wrapped have no drop-test step; CS-007 §7.5 says why a lead does not add one there and where the readings go instead.
5. A lead who adds, edits or archives a technique shall open a revision of this standard within two weeks, so the table below catches up (CS-000 §2). The app holds the live checklists; this table is their value at this revision.

The built-in techniques as the app ships them (`app/workorders.js`, STD_STEPS, 2026-10-10). Blockers, holds, evidence and training are in brackets.

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
| Technique | Layup type | Steps in order |
|---|---|---|
| Mold infusion | MOLD INFUSION | Stack frozen (blocker; needs a layup stack). Mold design review (blocker; needs the CAD; Mold design). Glue mold stock (ShopSabre CNC). Machine mold (needs a note; ShopSabre CNC). Seal and release mold. Dry stack and bag (Resin infusion). Drop test, 1 inHg or less over 10 min (blocker; needs a note; Resin infusion; the number is CS-006 §7.4's). Infuse (starts the cure; Resin infusion). Cure and demould (cure hold). Trim and finish |
| Glass infusion | GLASS INFUSION | Stack frozen (blocker; needs a layup stack). Prepare plate and release. Dry stack and bag (Resin infusion). Drop test, 1 inHg or less over 10 min (blocker; needs a note; Resin infusion). Infuse (starts the cure; Resin infusion). Cure and demould (cure hold). Cut to DXF, confirm revision. Finish |
| Mold wet lay | MOLD WET LAY | Stack frozen (blocker; needs a layup stack). Mold design review (blocker; needs the CAD; Mold design). Glue and machine mold (needs a note; ShopSabre CNC). Seal and release mold. Wet layup and bag (starts the cure; Wet layup). Cure and demould (cure hold). Trim and finish |
| Foam wrapped | FOAM WRAPPED | Stack frozen (blocker; needs a layup stack). Shape foam core (Foam core). Wet layup over core (starts the cure; Wet layup). Cure (cure hold). Trim and finish |
| Other | (blank, or any type no technique claims) | Define acceptance criterion: target and method, set before work starts (blocker; needs a note). Execute. Verify against criterion |

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. An issue shall be raised on the run it holds up: ⚠ Raise an issue at the foot of the run's Issues section, or ⚑ (Report an issue on this step) on the step where it happened.
2. Close it in the run's Issues section: Disposition (UAI (Use As Is), Corrective Action, Rework, Scrap or Other), What happened (the root cause), What was done, then Resolve. The issue's own page has the same three, under What happened, the disposition prompt, and Resolve, with the Resolve issue button.
3. A run shall not complete while any of its issues lacks a Disposition, What happened or What was done. The app enforces Disposition and What was done: setting the run Complete opens the closeout list, with Resolve on each issue and Resolve all & complete work order at the foot. It does not check What happened, so the person closing out does.
4. A false alarm is cancelled with Cancel ticket (false alarm), not disposed.
5. If a fix did not hold, press Reopen on the issue's page. It withdraws the disposition and clears What was done, keeps What happened, and the run is held again until the issue is disposed a second time.

The What was done prompt follows the disposition: Scrap asks "Why could it not be saved?", UAI asks "Why is it acceptable as it is?".

![The issue path on a run: raise it (⚠ Raise an issue, or ⚑ on a step), then Disposition, What happened and What was done; the app holds Complete until every issue has a Disposition and What was done. Reopen loops back and clears the disposition.](figures/cs013-issue-path.v2.png)

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
1. A finished or abandoned part or run should be archived, not deleted. Any member can Archive one on its page in edit mode, or several with Select… on the list. An archived record leaves the lists, the Dashboard and the Season tab but keeps every field and who archived it; the archived chip on the list shows them, each with Restore.
2. Delete is for a record that should never have existed, and only a lead deletes parts, runs and issues. Deleting a run takes its issues and uploads with it.
3. A deleted record goes to Reports, Recently deleted, and can be put back with Restore for 30 days (`TRASH_DAYS` in `app/core.js`). Restoring brings back everything deleted with it.
4. After 30 days a lead presses Empty them, and the records are gone for good with their uploads.
5. A deleted ID is never reissued (§4.1 rule 2).

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text:
| Check | Target | Method | Record where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every part has a run before it consumes carbon or machine time | 100% | The Work Orders tab lists Parts with no run yet; lead check at the weekly meeting | none |
| Blocker steps bought off in order | No downstream work past an unfinished blocker | App enforcement / shaded rows on paper | WO |
| Monthly Backup run | Every month during build season | Lead | Drive folder timestamps |
| Retro honesty | No fabricated buy-offs on retro WOs | "not recorded (retro)" convention | WO fields |
| R&D builds are marked as such | 100% | Lead check at the weekly meeting: a part not in the season plan is either marked R&D or is a gap | Part `rnd` flag |
| Issues disposed and explained before Complete | 100% | The app blocks Complete (closeout list, §7.6) | Run's Issues section |
| Steps that need training signed by trained people | Every override (training, evidence, cure hold) has a written reason | The app blocks it; the lead reads the override entries in the event logs at the weekly meeting | Run's Event log (in Notes & log) |

sections.title: CS-013 Work Orders & Part Traceability
sections.text: The live database is the team's day-to-day part-history record, shared and current for everyone at once; the monthly Backup JSON in Drive is the archive nobody can lock the team out of. Master-Tracker-style views (spreadsheets, summaries) may continue as *views* built from that record. The WO is the source of truth (same rule as CS-002 §9).

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
| | |

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
In SN5 the inventory sheet was written at season start and never touched again, so nobody knew what was on the shelf, what was on order, or when to reorder (PP-02). Nobody could say which roll or which jug went into a panel either (PP-09), and chemicals ended up in a food fridge (PP-10). The app now turns a delivery into one record per roll or jug, on the shelf it actually went to, with its vendor lot, expiry and UC EH&S tag. That only works if the delivery is logged the day it arrives and the records are right when they are made.

This standard says how a delivery becomes records, how a container's dates and state are kept, how our records stay matched to the campus EH&S chemical inventory, and what a person checks before saving anything an AI read off a slip or a label.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
Covered: receiving deliveries, donations, sponsor material and legacy stock into the app; lot records for fabric, resin and hardener, and consumables; received, opened, emptied and expiry dates; UC EH&S tags on chemical containers and reconciliation with the campus RSS Chemicals inventory; the ✨ packing-slip and container-label reads used at receiving.

Not covered:

- Approving, buying and paying for a purchase, and the Budget tab: CS-012.
- Where things are stored, minimum stock and the Running out card: CS-011.
- The printed FEB label, where it goes and what it says, and the EH&S tag as a container's label: CS-001.
- Recording which lots went into a part at the cure buy-off: CS-013 §7.2 step 4.
- Tooling board and offcuts, which are logged under Inventory → Boards, not at the desk (CS-011 §7.3).

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
- **Lot**: one record for one physical thing on a shelf. Fabric, resin and hardener are one record per roll or container. A consumable is one record carrying a count (How many). IDs are `FAB-SN6-###`, `RSN-SN6-###` and `CON-SN6-###`, each with its own counter (`fb.js`). Resin and hardener share the `RSN` prefix; the record's Role says which.
- **Material type**: what kind of thing a lot is across every container of it (`IN2`, `AT30`, `WEST-206`). The reorder count, the grouped shelf rows and the TDS and SDS buttons all key on it (`materials.js`).
- **Vendor lot number**: the lot or batch number the manufacturer printed on the container or the slip. Blank when none is printed.
- **EH&S tag**: the UC EH&S barcode sticker campus puts on every chemical container for the RSS Chemicals inventory. A Data Matrix square marked RSS, with a 24-character code of letters and digits printed in six groups of four. The last 12 characters are reprinted down the right edge (the edge print), which is the part still readable on a wrapped or scuffed label (`core.js`, EHS_LEN 24, EHS_TAIL 12). Example, made up: `CA00 0000 0000 0000 0024 3F1C`. Stored in the lot's EH&S barcode field. FEB never prints one.
- **RSS sublocation tag**: the same kind of sticker on a shelf or cabinet. Stored in the storage location's EH&S barcode field.
- **Incoming**: the card on the storage map listing every purchase line bought and not yet fully received.
- **State**: Sealed, Open, Empty or Expired (`shop.js` LOT_STATE). A received lot starts Sealed.
- **Received, Opened, Emptied, Expires**: the lot's date fields. Received comes from the desk's Arrived date. Opened and Emptied are stamped by the Open and Empty buttons on the lot's page (and by "now empty" when logging use). Changing State in Edit stamps nothing, so use the buttons.
- **Expiry from**: where the Expires date came from: "vendor label" (a person typed it), "vendor label (AI read)" (a ✨ read set it and nobody has typed over it) or "shelf-life table" (Link materials worked it out from Received plus the TDS shelf life).
- **How full**: Full, Half, Low or Empty. A coarse level, not a measurement.
- **Hazard**: flammable, not flammable, or blank. Blank means unknown, and an unknown lot cannot trigger the storage map's flammables warning.
- **AI read**: a value a ✨ button filled from a photo (packing slip, container label, receipt). A draft un

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
Chemical containers arrive sealed, so the hazard at receipt is a damaged or leaking one, and a container filed in the wrong place.

1. Wear nitrile gloves when you unpack and shelve chemical containers.
2. Before you touch a damaged or leaking container, read its SDS (§5). Do not receive a leaking container onto a shelf: leave it in its packaging, set it apart from other chemicals, and tell a lead. The lead decides what happens to it.
3. Put chemicals straight onto a location CS-011 §6 allows for them. Never a fridge (the food-fridge incident, #composites 2026-02-17, PP-10).
4. The receiver shall set Hazard on every resin, hardener and chemical consumable lot the day it is received: open the lot's page, press Edit, set Hazard. Receiving does not set it yet. Read it off the SDS §2: "flammable" when the SDS lists a flammable gas, aerosol or liquid (GHS H220 to H226, or an older OSHA Class I flammable liquid), otherwise "not flammable". The EH&S import applies the H-code half of this test (`ehsimport.js` ehsHazard); the OSHA Class I clause covers older US-format sheets such as Airtac's.

None of the shipped rules is (the epoxies are marked not flammable, and acetone, IPA, Airtac and clear coat have no restock row), so today the desk does not warn. 5. Expired and emptied chemical containers leave through campus EH&S. [lead input needed: the RFS disposal route.] An emptied container stays in the app as Empty until it is retired in RSS (§7.10).

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.section: 7.1 Before it arrives: purchase lines and Incoming
sections.text:
The Incoming card on the storage map lists every purchase line on the Budget tab that has not yet fully arrived ("bought, not yet on a shelf"). Each line shows its price each, the `BUY-SN6-###` chip, the vendor and "ordered Nd ago", counted from the purchase's Date ordered. A ⚠ appears after 14 days (`inventory.js` INV_STALE_ORDER_DAYS). A partly received line reads "N of M in · K to come". A line leaves the card once the records made from it account for its full quantity.

1. When you log a purchase, add one line item per thing that will go on a shelf, with the count ordered (CS-012 §7.9). A purchase with no line items never appears on Incoming.
2. Set the purchase's Date ordered to the day the order was placed.
3. When a line shows ⚠, the purchaser checks the order with the supplier and writes what they learned in the purchase's Notes.
4. If a line will never arrive (short-shipped or cancelled), tell a lead. The app has no button to close a line short yet, so it stays on Incoming until a lead deals with it.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
Open the desk the way that matches where you are standing:

| Where you are | Press | What the desk starts with |
|---|---|---|
| Inventory → Storage map | Receive a delivery (toolbar) | The "Receiving desk" with the On order strip above an empty sheet |
| A line on the Incoming card | Arrived ▸ | Every open line of that purchase as a row, with name, quantity still to come, supplier and $ each filled in |
| A shelf's page | Receive delivery | The sheet locked to that shelf, headed "Add to this shelf" (the phone case) |
| Scan, pointed at an EH&S tag no record wears | Log it (in "No record wears EH&S tag … yet. Log the container at the receiving desk?") | A Resin row with the code already in its EH&S tag cell |

1. Open the desk one of the four ways above.
2. If the desk shows "In the last hour: [name] added N. Same delivery?", ask that person before you type anything. Two people logging the same box is how a shelf ends up with two of everything.
3. On the full desk, use the strip above the sheet: On order lists purchases with open lines, with Take all N for a whole order and Take for one line; Shelves lists the storage locations by site, and picking one sets the shelf on every row that has none.
4. If you leave before finishing, the sheet is kept on this device for 24 hours (`receiving.js` RX_DRAFT_MAX_AGE_MS) and the Inventory toolbar shows "Finish N lines". After 24 hours it is discarded. It is not shared with anyone else's device.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
The sheet has three header fields (Supplier, Arrived, New lines land on) and one row per kind of thing, with the columns Class, What is it, How many, Shelf, Vendor lot, EH&S tag, Expires and $ each. EH&S tag and Expires apply to Resin, Hardener and Consumable rows only; a Fabric row shows a dash there.

1. Set Supplier.
2. Set Arrived to the day the delivery came in. It becomes the Received date of every record made from this sheet.
3. Set New lines land on to the shelf most of the delivery goes to.
4. Start a row and pick its Class first: Fabric, Resin, Hardener or Consumable. Class decides how many records the row makes and which fields it gets. Type the first letter; the arrow keys deliberately do not change it.
5. Put the resin and the hardener of a kit on separate rows, Resin and Hardener. The cure buy-off offers hardener lots, and lots with no Role, as the hardener; set Role on every RSN lot so a resin is never offered there.
6. Type What is it as the container names it. A name already on a shelf brings its Material type, supplier and $ each with it, and the materials table fills a blank Material type. Rows filled by Arrived ▸ or Take all do not pick up the Material type: after Create N records, press Link materials on the Materials list (§7.7 step 3).
7. Type How many. Fabric, Resin and Hardener rows make one record per roll or container ("3 records"). A Consumable row makes one record carrying the count ("1 of 50"). The desk refuses more than 50 tracked units (`receiving.js`, the review check on tracked rows) on one row: split the row, or log a box of small items as one Consumable with a count.
8. Set Shelf on any row going somewhere other than the default. A row with no shelf lands in No location on the storage map; put it away the same day (CS-011 §7.3).
9. Type Vendor lot exactly as printed. Leave it blank if nothing is printed.
10. Fill EH&S tag per §7.6 and Expires per §7.7.
11. Type $ each, the price of one unit, from the purchase line or the receipt. Arrived ▸ fills it from the purchase.
12. Press Enter to start the next row; it carries the class, shelf and supplier forward.
13. If you paste a block copied from an order email, each line becomes a row. Check the Class, How many and Shelf of every pasted row; the toast reminds you of class and shelf, so check How many as well.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.section: 7.4 Reading a packing slip with ✨ From packing slip
sections.text:
✨ From packing slip appears under the sheet when a lead has AI features on (§5). It reads a photo or a PDF of the slip and adds one row per shipped line: the name, the quantity shipped (not ordered or backordered), and the vendor lot and expiry only where the slip prints them for that line. An expiry printed as month and year is read as the last day of that month (`functions/index.js` SLIP_PROMPT). What each thing is (class, Material type, supplier, cost) comes from the app's own tables, never from the model.

The rule, for this button and every other ✨ fill (✨ Read label in §7.7, ✨ Fill from receipt in CS-012 §7.2): anything a ✨ button fills is a draft. The person saving it shall check every row against the paper, the container or the receipt before saving. An AI-read expiry stays marked "vendor label (AI read)" until a person types over it. An AI read is never a source for a number in a standard (CS-000 §2).

1. Press ✨ From packing slip and photograph the slip, or pick its PDF.
2. Wait for "N lines read from the slip. Check the class, the shelf and the count on each." The status bar shows each phase while it runs. Blank rows on the sheet give way to the slip's rows.
3. Check every row against the slip and against what is physically in the box: Class, What is it, How many, Vendor lot, Expires. Fix a wrong cell by typing in it.
4. Remove any row for a thing that is not in the box with the bin icon (Remove this line).
5. Where the container itself prints an expiry, type it into Expires from the container. That clears the AI mark.
6. If the read fails or finds no lines, type the rows, or paste them from the order email.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.section: 7.5 Confirming: "Create N records?", Print N labels or Undo
sections.text:
1. Press Review N records, or Ctrl+Enter. The confirm "Create N records?" lists the rows grouped by shelf.
2. Untick anything that did not actually turn up.
3. Read every warning under the list: EH&S tag counts that do not fit the number of containers (§7.6 step 4), a tag on two lines or already on another record ("one tag, one container"), and flammable items landing on a location not rated for them (§6). Fix them with Back to the sheet.
4. Press Create N records. Every record starts Sealed, dated with Arrived. If the app cannot get IDs (no connection), it writes nothing and says so; try again when back online.
5. The bar "N records added" offers Print N labels and Undo. Labels are never printed automatically.
6. Label the records per CS-001 §7.1 and §7.2. A chemical container wearing an EH&S tag gets no FEB label: the tag is its label (CS-001 §7.2). Print N labels prints one for every record in the batch, so when the batch holds tagged containers, print from Inventory → Labels instead.
7. In Inventory → Labels, set What to Material lots.
8. Tick only the records without a tag, and press Preview N labels.
9. If something is wrong, press Undo. It deletes the records just made and puts the rows back on the sheet. Bin any labels already printed for them.
10. For a partial delivery, receive only what came. The rest stays on Incoming as "N of M in · K to come".
11. When every line of the purchase is in, set its Order status to Arrived on the Budget tab (CS-012 §7.1 table; §7.9 step 6). Receiving does not change it.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
Every chemical container on campus wears a UC EH&S tag (§4). CS-001 §7.11 covers the tag as the container's label and recording a tag on a container already on a shelf. This section covers recording it at the desk.

1. For each Resin, Hardener or chemical Consumable row, press the camera button in the EH&S tag cell and scan the tag on each container in the row. The camera stays open; each scan adds a code, and a repeat is skipped ("is already on this line").
2. If the camera fails, type all 24 characters from the face of the tag. For several containers on one row, separate the codes with spaces. Codes are given to the row's records in the order typed.
3. Do not record a new container by its 12-character edge print. The edge print finds a container already recorded (Scan, Move, CS-001 §7.11), but typed at receipt it saves a short code that will not match the RSS inventory.
4. Give one code per container: the number of codes on a row equals How many. The confirm warns when a row has more codes than containers, or two or more codes but fewer than containers. One code on a multi-container row raises no warning, so count them yourself.
5. If the confirm says a tag is already on another record, that container is already tracked and is not part of this delivery. Take it off the sheet.
6. The desk does not check a code's length. Count the characters against the tag before you press Create N records; a code that is not 24 characters saves anyway, and shows later with a ? after it on the shelf page and as "check the tag" in the EH&S reconciliation export.
7. A chemical container with no tag yet: leave the cell blank and give it a 5522 FEB label (CS-001 §7.2). When campus tags it, record the tag in its EH&S barcode field (CS-001 §7.11). The FEB label stays on.
8. Consumables that are not chemicals (cups, gloves, bag film) have no tag; leave the cell blank.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
1. At the desk, type Expires off the container for every resin, hardener and chemical consumable that prints one. Fabric has no expiry field.
2. If the container prints only a manufacture date and a shelf life, work out the expiry from the label (manufacture date plus shelf life) and type it into Expires.
3. On the Materials list, Link materials fills blanks from the materials table, but only on records that have no Material type (imports, old records, and rows filled by Arrived ▸ or Take all). It sets the Material type from the name, and a blank Expires from Received plus the TDS shelf life, stamped "shelf-life table". It never changes a filled field, and it lists everything before writing ("Link N records"). It does not reach a lot whose Material type the desk already filled, so that lot's Expires comes from step 1 or 2. The shelf lives in the table are datasheet figures: IN2 and AT30 12 months (`03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-IN2-Infusion-Resin.pdf`), XCR 12 months (`03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-XCR-Epoxy-Coating-Resin.pdf`), both when stored as the TDS says, and DP420 24 months from manufacture (`03 Datasheets/3m-scotch-weld-epoxy-adhesive-dp420-black.pdf`, p.5) (`materials.js`).
4. A shelf-life date counts from the day we received the container, not the day it was made, so it can run later than the manufacturer's date. Type the label's date over it whenever the label gives one.
5. To read a label with the camera, open the lot's page and press ✨ Read label (resin, hardener and consumable lots, when AI features are on). Photograph the label.
6. In the "From the label" sheet, compare each offered value (Vendor lot number, Expires, Material) with the container. Empty fields come pre-ticked; a filled field says what it "replaces". Untick anything that does not match, then press Apply. The §7.4 rule applies: check before Apply.
7. Read Expiry from on the lot when you need to know how far to trust a date (§4). Typing a date over "vendor label (AI read)" changes it to "vendor label".
8. Set Hazard per §6 step 4.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.section: 7.8 Opening, using up and emptying a container
sections.text:
The cure buy-off pre-fills the most recently opened lot of each class (`workorders.js` defaultLot). With two open jugs of AT30 on the bench that default is wrong for one of them. The TDS gives a second reason: hardeners deteriorate quickly once exposed to air (R14).

1. You should open one container of a material at a time: finish the open one, or set it aside, before breaking the seal on the next.
2. When you break the seal, open the lot's page (scan its FEB label or its EH&S tag) and press Open (not Edit → State). The app stamps Opened with today's date.
3. At the cure buy-off, confirm or correct the lots it offers (CS-013 §7.2 step 4).
4. When you finish a layup, you should log what you used on the work order (Consume on the material line, or Materials used at the cure buy-off) and answer The lot afterwards: still fine, running low, or now empty.
5. When a container runs out, pick "now empty" in The lot afterwards, or press Empty on its page. The app stamps Emptied and sets How full to Empty.
6. An emptied container should be marked Empty, never deleted. An Empty record counts as zero toward the minimum (CS-011 §4), and the EH&S reconciliation needs it to tell campus the container is gone (§7.10).
7. When you notice a container's level has changed, set How full (Full, Half, Low, Empty) in Edit.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
The storage map shows "N expired" on a shelf holding a lot past its Expires date that is not Empty. The cure buy-off does not check expiry.

You should check Expires on the container or its lot page before you mix (CS-008 §7 step 1). Past it, ask a lead before it goes on a part.

[lead input needed: whether expired resin, hardener or XCR may be used for R&D or a test panel, what test it needs first, and the disposal route through campus EH&S.]

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.text:
Campus keeps its own inventory of every tagged container in RSS Chemicals. Ours and theirs agree only if someone compares them. The owner is the member holding the campus chemical-inventory role. [lead input needed: who holds it.]

1. Once a month, at the stock walk (CS-011 §7.1), open Inventory → Export and, under EH&S reconciliation, press Copy for Sheets (or Download .csv). Rows that need attention sort first.
2. Paste it into a sheet in the season's Drive folder.
3. Work every note on a chemical container (resin, hardener, chemical consumable); a non-chemical consumable such as cups or gloves shows "no EH&S tag on record" and needs nothing. "no EH&S tag on record" on a chemical container: find the container and record its tag (CS-001 §7.11), or give an untagged one a 5522 FEB label. "check the tag": compare the code with the face of the tag and correct it. "emptied" with "retire it in RSS too": retire that container in RSS.
4. Compare the `ehsBarcode` column with the RSS export (it is the unpunctuated code, so a lookup lands). Walk the shelves with the `printed` column, which matches the sticker character for character.
5. A container RSS lists and the app does not: log it at the desk (Scan → Log it, §7.2).
6. For many such containers at once, a lead runs EH&S import (Inventory toolbar, lead only). First export the inventory from the RSS Chemicals web app.
7. In EH&S import, choose the file (.xlsx, or a re-saved .csv).
8. Tick our sublocations (Formula Electric's start ticked).
9. Set "Their shelf is our" for each sublocation.
10. Untick any container we deliberately do not track.
11. Press Create N records.
12. EH&S import never edits or deletes, and skips any code a record already wears. It guesses class and role from the name and Hazard from the H-codes, and carries over the received and expiry dates. Check each new record's Class, Role and Hazard afterwards.

sections.title: CS-014 Receiving, Lots & EH&S
sections.section: 7.11 Donations, sponsor stock and legacy stock
sections.text:
1. Receive donated or sponsor material through the desk like any delivery, from Receive a delivery. There is no purchase, so no Arrived ▸.
2. Name the sponsor or donor in Supplier.
3. Leave $ each blank. Donated stock stays un-costed.
4. For legacy stock found on a shelf with no record, set Arrived to the day you log it: the Received date then means "logged", which is all we know.
5. Treat chemical containers as in §6, §7.6 and §7.7: Hazard, EH&S tag, Expires.
6. Asking a sponsor for material is CS-012 §7.6.

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 1. IN2 resin and AT30 hardener mix ratio (AT30 SLOW or FAST)
sections.text:
IN2 resin and AT30 hardener mix 100:30 by weight, with AT30 SLOW or AT30 FAST (CS-008 §5). Weigh both on a scale to 1 g: IN2 publishes no ratio tolerance (CS-008 §5). AT30 SLOW is the infusion default.

Also called: IN2, AT30, hardener, slow hardener, fast hardener, AT30 ratio, infusion resin, mix ratio, how much hardener, 100 to 30.

| Hardener | Ratio by weight | Pot life (datasheet) | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| AT30 SLOW | 100:30 | 120–150 min at 25 °C in the TDS table; the TDS text says 80–100 min, so plan on 80–100 min | Infusion default |
| AT30 FAST | 100:30 | 10–14 min at 25 °C in the TDS table; the TDS text says 9–14 min, so plan on 9–14 min | Small infusions only |

Source: the IN2 TDS, `03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-IN2-Infusion-Resin.pdf`, as copied into CS-008 §5.

1. Weigh resin and hardener on the 1 g scale (CS-008 §7 step 2).
2. Write both masses on the work order.
3. Mix for at least 2 min, scraping the walls and base (CS-008 §7 step 3).
4. Double-pot: pour into a second cup and remix with a fresh stick.

Want a pot life between SLOW and FAST? You may blend AT30 FAST and SLOW, as long as the total stays 100:30 by weight (CS-008 §6). Never mix off-ratio to speed up or slow down the cure. Off-ratio gives an uncured, sticky part.

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 2. West 105 mix ratio: how much 205 fast, 206 slow or 209 extra slow hardener (pumps and scale)
sections.text:
West 105 with 206 or 205 is 5:1 by volume on the pumps. West 105 with 209 is 3:1 by volume and needs a different pump head (CS-008 §5). Check the pump head before the first stroke: the wrong pump is the classic wrong-ratio trap (CS-008 §7 step 1).

Also called: West, West System, 105, 205, 206, 209, fast hardener, slow hardener, extra slow, pumps, pump ratio, mix ratio.

| Hardener | Pumps (by volume) | By weight | Scale tolerance (by weight) | Pot life, 100 g at 72 °F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 206 slow (wet layup default) | 5:1 | 5.36:1 | 4.84–6.19:1 | 20–25 min |
| 205 fast | 5:1 | 5.19:1 | 4.83–6.20:1 | 9–12 min |
| 209 extra slow | 3:1 | 3.68:1 | 3.30–4.03:1 | 40–50 min |

All figures are from the West TDSs, each row from its own 105/2xx sheet (CS-008 §5).

1. Check the pump head matches the hardener: 3:1 for 209, 5:1 for 205 and 206.
2. Pump full strokes only (CS-008 §7 step 2).
3. Write the strokes or masses on the work order.
4. Mix for at least 2 min, scraping the walls and base, then double-pot (CS-008 §7 step 3).

Do not blend 205 and 206: no datasheet on file covers it (CS-008 §6). After a long gap between uses, mix a small test batch to check the pumps meter correctly and the batch cures (CS-008 §7 step 9). Cloudy or crystallized 105 after a cold spell: warm it to 125 °F and stir until clear before it goes in the pump (CS-008 §7 step 8).

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.text:
XCR mixes 100:41 resin to hardener by weight, which is 2:1 by volume (CS-008 §5). Pot life is 8 min at 20 °C for a 150 g mix, so mix small (XCR TDS, `03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-XCR-Epoxy-Coating-Resin.pdf`, as copied into CS-008 §5).

Also called: XCR, coating resin, sealer, mold sealer, seal coat, sealing resin.

- Weigh it to 1 g. XCR publishes no ratio tolerance (CS-008 §5).
- Minimum temperature: 15 °C (59 °F), the datasheet figure (CS-008 §5).
- FEB hold: 12 h before the release system goes on. That is the team's hold; the datasheet gives initial cure as 8 h 30, handleable at about 9 h at 20 °C (CS-008 §5).
- The app does not lock the XCR hold. No work-order step starts an XCR cure, so the 12 h is watched by hand (CS-008 §5.1).

Batch size, how many coats and the overcoat window are in QR-004.

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 4. How long before I can demould (demold)? Cure time and the FEB hold for each resin
sections.text:
Wait the FEB hold, counted from the end of the layup or infusion: 48 h for IN2 + AT30 SLOW, 24 h for IN2 + AT30 FAST, 24 h for West 105 with 206 or 205, 36 h for West 105 + 209, and 12 h for XCR before release (CS-008 §5).

Also called: demould, demold, de-mould, cure hold, FEB hold, wait time, cure time, how long to cure, when can I pull the part.

| Resin (as the app names it) | FEB hold (team) | Datasheet figure (manufacturer) |
|---|---|---|
| IN2 + AT30 SLOW | 48 h | demould 18–24 h at 25 °C |
| IN2 + AT30 FAST | 24 h | demould 6–8 h at 25 °C |
| West 105 + 206 slow | 24 h | thin-film solid 10–15 h at 72 °F |
| West 105 + 205 fast | 24 h | thin-film solid 6–8 h at 72 °F |
| West 105 + 209 extra slow | 36 h | thin-film solid 20–24 h at 72 °F |
| XCR coating resin | 12 h | initial cure 8 h 30, handleable about 9 h at 20 °C |

The FEB hold is the team's, signed off by Simon Starbuck 2026-08-01, and it is the one that governs. The datasheet column is the manufacturer's (CS-008 §5, §5.1). West publishes no demould time; its thin-film cure is the nearest figure.

On a work order, "Cure and demould" ("Cure" on a Foam wrapped run) stays locked until the hold has run from the "Finished on" and "at" time entered when "Infuse", "Wet layup and bag" or "Wet layup over core" was signed (CS-008 §5.1). To see the hold in force today, press "why N h?" on the held step. Gel is not cure: fingernail-test the flange before you trust the clock (CS-008 §7 step 6).

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 5. Why is the hold longer than the datasheet? ("Why N hours?")
sections.text:
The FEB hold is a team decision, longer than the datasheet in every row on purpose. It lands on shift boundaries: 24 h means "come back tomorrow" and 48 h means "come back the day after tomorrow", which is after the weekend only for a Friday infusion (CS-008 §5.1). It was never worked out from the datasheet.

Also called: why N hours, why 48 hours, why so long, FEB hold, team hold, can I demould sooner.

A hold that ran out at 3 am would help nobody, because nobody is at RFS at 3 am. That is why the ratios against the datasheet look uneven: 1.3× for XCR, 3× for the FAST systems (CS-008 §5.1).

Both FAST systems hold 24 h. Buying FAST hardener to turn two infusions round in one day does not work under this rule. That is deliberate: the team has no record of a part ruined by waiting, and several of work being rushed (CS-008 §5.1).

The holds were signed off by Simon Starbuck on 2026-08-01. The live value is the app's. "Why N hours?" always shows the hold in force and who signed it, and says when a lead set it from the app (CS-008 §5.1). QR-001 §6 says how a lead changes one.

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 6. Can a lead change the hold or demould (demold) early?
sections.text:
Yes. A lead can sign the locked step early, or change a hold for every work order, and the app records both. A member who tries to sign early is turned away, and no hold can go below the datasheet figure (CS-008 §5.1).

Also called: override, skip the hold, early demould, early demold, change the hold, lead override.

Demould one part early (lead only):

1. On the locked step, sign through "Demould early?".
2. Answer "Why are you demoulding early?".
3. The app writes the reason, the lead's name and how many hours short it was to the work order's event log.

Change a hold for every work order (lead only):

1. Open a work order whose hold for that resin is running now. On the held step, press "why N h?" to open "Why N hours?". The link shows only while a hold is counting down (CS-008 §5.1).
2. Press "Change this hold…".
3. Enter "FEB hold (hours)".
4. Under "Signed off by", pick who signed it off and the date.
5. Press "Save".

The app refuses a hold below the datasheet figure, and a hold nobody signed off. "Revert to the code table" in the same window undoes a change. A lead who changes a hold shall open a revision of CS-008 within two weeks, so the table and the app agree again (CS-008 §5.1).

The app does not lock three cases: XCR mold sealing (watched by hand, CS-004 §7.3), any cure recorded as "Something else / not recorded", and retro work orders (CS-008 §5.1).

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 7. Pot life and working time for each resin
sections.text:
IN2 + AT30 SLOW: plan on 80–100 min (the TDS text, no temperature given); AT30 FAST: plan on 9–14 min. West 105 + 206 20–25 min, + 205 9–12 min, + 209 40–50 min (100 g at 72 °F). XCR 8 min at 20 °C (150 g) (CS-008 §5).

Also called: pot life, working time, open time, gel time, how long do I have.

Pot life is the usable time in the cup at the mass and temperature the datasheet quotes it for. A bigger batch or a warmer shop makes it shorter (CS-008 §4). Pick a system whose pot life fits the job with a margin (CS-008 §7 step 1).

| System | Pot life (datasheet) |
|---|---|
| IN2 + AT30 SLOW | plan on 80–100 min (the TDS text, no temperature given; its table says 120–150 min at 25 °C) |
| IN2 + AT30 FAST | plan on 9–14 min (the TDS text; its table says 10–14 min at 25 °C) |
| West 105 + 206 | 20–25 min at 72 °F (100 g) |
| West 105 + 205 | 9–12 min at 72 °F (100 g) |
| West 105 + 209 | 40–50 min at 72 °F (100 g) |
| XCR | 8 min at 20 °C (150 g) |

Sources: CS-008 §5, from the IN2, West and XCR TDSs in `03 Datasheets/`.

Mix the smallest batch that does the job and pour it out of the pot promptly: resin packed in a cup heats itself faster (CS-008 §6). A warm cup means use it now or spread it thin. A hot or smoking cup goes outside onto concrete and stays there. Do not bin it and do not pour water on it indoors. Nothing goes in the trash until it is fully cured and cool (CS-008 §6).

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 8. Shop too cold? Minimum temperatures and cold cures
sections.text:
Minimum cure temperatures (datasheet): West 206 60 °F (16 °C), 205 40 °F (4 °C), 209 70 °F (21 °C); XCR 15 °C (59 °F); IN2 + AT30 not stated. Cure at 20 °C or warmer where you can (CS-008 §5; §7 step 5).

Also called: cold shop, winter, temperature, minimum temperature, cure temperature, cold cure.

| System | Minimum temperature (datasheet) |
|---|---|
| West 105 + 206 | 60 °F (16 °C) |
| West 105 + 205 | 40 °F (4 °C) |
| West 105 + 209 | 70 °F (21 °C) |
| XCR | 15 °C (59 °F) |
| IN2 + AT30 | not stated |

Source: CS-008 §5, from the West and XCR TDSs.

The pot life and cure figures in CS-008 §5 assume 25 °C for IN2, 72 °F (22 °C) for West and 20 °C for XCR. A colder shop cures slower, and the hold does not stretch on its own, so test the flange, not the clock (CS-008 §5.1).

1. Cure at 20 °C or warmer wherever you can (CS-008 §7 step 5).
2. When you sign the layup or infusion, fill in "Shop temperature, °C (optional)".
3. Below the reference temperature the app warns "Colder than this number assumes, so it will run long. Test the flange, not the clock." The hold itself does not change (CS-008 §5.1).
4. Before you demould, fingernail-test the flange or trim zone for soft spots (CS-008 §8).

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 9. Mixing rules for every resin, and what to record
sections.text:
Weigh on the 1 g scale or pump full strokes, mix for at least 2 min scraping the walls and base, and double-pot anything going on a part surface (CS-008 §7). Never mix off-ratio to change the cure speed (CS-008 §6).

Also called: mixing, double pot, double-pot, scale, weigh, expiry, expired resin, Resin mixed, batch.

1. Check the expiry: the EXP date on the jug's label, or the Expires date on its lot page. Past it, ask a lead before it goes on a part (CS-008 §7 step 1).
2. Weigh to 1 g, or pump full strokes for West, and write the masses on the work order (CS-008 §7 step 2).
3. Mix for at least 2 min, scraping the walls and base (CS-008 §7 step 3).
4. Double-pot: transfer to a second cup and remix with a fresh stick.
5. When you sign the layup or infusion, pick the resin you actually mixed under "Resin mixed" (CS-008 §7 step 6).
6. Choose "Something else / not recorded" only for a resin not in the CS-008 §5 table. Then write the resin in the step note; its demould time is a lead's call.
7. Spread leftovers thin on scrap, or leave them outside to cure (CS-008 §7 step 7).

Forged CF mix math: the finished part mass is about cavity volume × 1.4 g/cc, the fiber is 60% of that (weigh it out first), and the resin to mix is about fiber mass × 1.25; the excess squeezes out (CS-008 §7 step 4). Starving the mix made the first forged part brittle; it failed its bend test.

sections.title: QR-001 Mix ratios and cure holds
sections.section: 10. When is the part fully cured? (full strength)
sections.text:
Full strength takes days to weeks, not hours: at least 14 days at 25 °C for IN2, at least 14 days at 20 °C for XCR, working strength in 1–4 days for West with 206 or 205, and maximum strength in 4–9 days for West with 209 (CS-008 §5).

Also called: full cure, fully cured, full properties, full strength, post-cure, when can I load it.

Demould is not full cure. A part out of the mold after its FEB hold is still curing. Avoid structural or fit loading before full cure where you can (CS-008 §4). The team cures ambient with no oven, so there is no post-cure to shorten this (CS-008 §5.1).

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 1. Infusion setup checklist, start to finish
sections.text:
Peel ply, then flow mesh stopping 30–50 mm short of the outlet; resin trap between bag and pump; at least 27 inHg; drop test 1 inHg or less over 10 min; only then mix IN2:AT30 at 100:30 by weight (CS-006 §7.2 to §7.5).

Also called: infusion, infuse, VARTM, resin infusion, infusion checklist, infusion setup.

1. Stack frozen on the work order; mold sealed and released with its checks passed (CS-006 §7.1).
2. Resin on hand of at least (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.3, and every consumable cut before any resin is mixed (CS-006 §7.1).
3. Two people for anything bigger than a coupon, one experienced with infusion (CS-006 §7.1).
4. Plies down, peel ply over the laminate and flange edges (CS-006 §7.2).
5. Flow mesh over the whole part, stopping 30–50 mm short of the outlet side (CS-006 §7.2).
6. Feed spiral on the inlet flange, outlet spiral toward the catch pot; resin travel inlet to outlet about 0.5 m at most (CS-006 §7.2).
7. Tacky tape, bag, pleats at every corner (CS-006 §7.3).
8. Outlet line to the resin trap, then the pump; inlet line clamped shut (CS-006 §7.3).
9. Pull to 27 inHg or better (CS-006 §7.4).
10. Drop test: lose 1 inHg or less over 10 min, readings in the step note (CS-006 §7.4).
11. Mix (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.2–1.3 of IN2:AT30 at 100:30 by weight (CS-006 §7.5).
12. Infuse, clamp the inlet, sign "Infuse" (CS-006 §7.5).
13. Wait the FEB hold: 48 h SLOW, 24 h FAST, from inlet clamp (CS-006 §7.6).

Each line has its own section below.

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 2. Before you start an infusion: what has to be ready
sections.text:
Before any resin is mixed: the stack is frozen on the work order, the mold is sealed and released per CS-004 with its checks passed, resin on hand is at least (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.3, and every consumable is cut (CS-006 §7.1).

Also called: infusion prerequisites, prep, staging, materials, training, who can infuse.

1. Check the stack is frozen and printed on the work order (CS-006 §7.1 step 1).
2. Check the mold is sealed and released per CS-004 and its quality checks passed.
3. Weigh the cut cloth and write the total dry fiber mass on the work order (CS-006 §7.2 step 1).
4. Check there is resin on hand of at least (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.3 (CS-006 §7.1 step 2).
5. Cut all consumables (peel ply, mesh, spiral, tubing, bag, tacky tape) before mixing.
6. Get a second person for any part bigger than a coupon. One of you has infused before (CS-006 §7.1 step 3).

Who can sign: "Dry stack and bag", "Drop test, 1 inHg or less over 10 min" and "Infuse" need Resin infusion training in the app. The app stops anyone else ("this step needs Resin infusion training"). Only a lead can sign without it, and the reason goes in the work order's event log (CS-006 §7.1 step 3).

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 3. Infusion stack order: peel ply, flow mesh and the mesh break
sections.text:
On top of the plies: peel ply over the full laminate and the flange edges, then flow mesh over the whole part, stopping 30–50 mm short of the outlet side. That gap is the mesh break: it slows resin at the end and cuts race-tracking (CS-006 §7.2 step 3).

Also called: flow mesh, infusion mesh, flow media, green mesh, mesh break, peel ply, spiral, spiral wrap, feed line, dry stack.

1. Wipe the workspace with IPA. Dust the released mold with a clean, dry microfiber only: no IPA, water or solvent on wax or PVA (CS-006 §7.2 step 1).
2. Cut cloth per the work order's ply table.
3. Lay the plies per the work order.
4. Tack a ply with Airtac 2 only where it needs holding: can at least 30 cm (12 in) from the surface, a light mist, then wait 10 s before placing the ply (CS-006 §7.2 step 2). Heavy spray inhibits the infusion.
5. Lay peel ply over the full laminate and past the flange edges.
6. Lay flow mesh over the entire part, stopping 30–50 mm short of the outlet side.
7. Place the feed spiral along the inlet side on the flange, not on the part surface unless the work order says so (it prints through) (CS-006 §7.2 step 4).
8. Place the outlet spiral toward the catch pot.

Resin travel from inlet to outlet is about 0.5 m at most, a rule of thumb from the SN5 Composites Info & Safety primer; it varies with resin and part shape (CS-006 §7.2 step 4). A bigger part needs more feeds, planned on the work order.

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 4. Bagging an infusion: tacky tape, pleats and the resin trap
sections.text:
Tacky tape round the full perimeter, VB160 cut oversized with a pleat at every corner, and the outlet line going to the resin trap and then the pump, never bag straight to pump. The inlet line stays clamped shut (CS-006 §7.3).

Also called: bag, vacuum bag, bagging, VB160, tacky tape, sealant tape, AT-200Y, pleats, resin trap, catch pot, through-bag connector.

1. Run tacky tape around the full perimeter on the outer edge of the flange, outboard of the spirals, peel ply and mesh, with at least ½ inch between them and the tape. Keep the backing on until final placement (CS-006 §7.3 step 1).
2. Cut VB160 oversized (CS-006 §7.3 step 2).
3. Add a pleat at every corner, and every 300–400 mm of perimeter on a curved mold (CS-006 §7.3 step 2).
4. Fit the through-bag connectors (CS-006 §7.3 step 3).
5. Connect outlet line to the resin trap, and the trap to the pump.
6. Clamp the inlet line shut.

The trap is mandatory. Without it, the first overlong pull fills the vacuum pump with resin and kills it (CS-006 §4). Tape over cut spiral-wrap ends: they pierce gloves and bags alike (CS-006 §6).

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 5. How much vacuum (inHg) before resin, and the infusion drop test
sections.text:
Pull to at least 27 inHg on the team gauge. Then close the valve to isolate the pump: the bag must lose 1 inHg or less over 10 minutes. No pass, no resin. After a pass, open the valve again (CS-006 §7.4).

Also called: drop test, leak test, leak-down, vacuum level, inHg, how much vacuum, 27 inHg.

1. Pull vacuum to 27 inHg or better. Full vacuum is about 29.9 inHg at sea level (CS-006 §7.4 step 1).
2. If the gauge will not pass 25 inHg, hunt leaks now: press tacky tape seams, listen, re-seat pleats and connector bases (CS-006 §7.4 step 1).
3. Close the valve to isolate the pump. The gauge must be on the bag side of the closed valve, never on the pump (CS-006 §7.4 step 2; CS-006 §5).
4. Read the gauge, wait 10 minutes, read it again.
5. Write the start and end readings in the note on the "Drop test, 1 inHg or less over 10 min" step. It will not take a member's signature without the note, and "Infuse" cannot be signed until it is. A lead can sign without it (Sign without it), and the reason goes in the work order's event log.
6. Failed? Keep hunting (seams, pleat folds, connector bases, spiral ends piercing the bag) and test again (CS-006 §7.4 step 3).
7. Passed? Open the valve again and check the gauge climbs back to 27 inHg before you open the inlet (CS-006 §7.4 step 4).

Do not mix resin until the drop test passes, even at 11 pm with people waiting (CS-006 §7.4). A gauge that reads "psi of vacuum" is reading something else: the team's gauges read inHg (CS-006 §4). Leak hunting in detail: QR-012.

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 6. How much IN2 resin to mix for an infusion
sections.text:
Mix about (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.2–1.3, at 100:30 IN2:AT30 by weight. Round up: starving an infusion mid-pull cannot be recovered (CS-006 §7.5 step 1).

Also called: resin math, how much resin, resin quantity, mix amount, batch size, IN2, AT30.

The 0.65 covers the laminate, aiming at about 60:40 fiber to resin by weight. The 1.2–1.3 covers what the mesh and the lines soak up (CS-006 §7.5 step 1). Have at least (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.3 on hand before you start (CS-006 §7.1 step 2).

1. Take the dry fiber mass you wrote on the work order.
2. Multiply by 0.65, then by 1.2 to 1.3. Round up.
3. Weigh IN2 and AT30 at 100:30 by weight (CS-006 §7.5 step 2).
4. Mix and double-pot per CS-008: at least 2 min, then a second cup and a fresh stick.
5. Record resin mixed against resin used on the work order, so the factor can be tuned.

Pot life: with SLOW, plan on 80–100 min. That is the TDS text, which gives no temperature; its table says 120–150 min at 25 °C (CS-006 §7.5 step 2). On a long infusion you may mix the total as two or more smaller batches and top up the pot as it draws down, keeping the inlet submerged (CS-006 §7.5 step 1).

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 7. Running the infusion: opening the inlet to clamping off
sections.text:
With 27 inHg or better confirmed and the drop test passed, open the inlet clamp slowly and watch the flow front. When resin reaches the outlet spiral and the laminate is fully dark, clamp the inlet and leave the pump running through gel (CS-006 §7.5).

Also called: infuse, infusing, flow front, open the inlet, clamp off, wet out.

1. Brace the resin cup (CS-006 §7.5 step 3).
2. Submerge the inlet line end fully. A slurping inlet injects bubbles.
3. Confirm the valve is open again after the drop test and the gauge reads 27 inHg or better (CS-006 §7.4 step 4; §7.5 step 4).
4. Open the inlet clamp slowly.
5. Watch the flow front for even progress and no race-tracking. A larger part takes about 20–30 min, sometimes longer (CS-006 §7.5 step 4).
6. When resin reaches the outlet spiral and the laminate is fully dark and wet, clamp the inlet (CS-006 §7.5 step 5).
7. Leave the pump running through gel.
8. Write the times (mix, open, full wet, clamp), resin mixed against used, gauge readings and anything odd, with photos, on the work order (CS-006 §7.5 step 6).
9. Sign "Infuse". Set "Resin mixed" to IN2 + AT30 SLOW or IN2 + AT30 FAST, set "Finished on" and "at" to the time you clamped the inlet, and fill in "Shop temperature, °C (optional)".

That clamp time starts the hold on "Cure and demould". Problems mid-infusion (race-tracking, a dry patch, bubbles): QR-012.

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 8. Do we degas the resin? (degassing IN2)
sections.text:
Sometimes. Degassing is optional: the team degasses IN2 sometimes, and the IN2 datasheet does not call for it (CS-006 §7.8). Degas when the part shows a visible cosmetic face, after pinholes or bubbles from the same mold, or when the mix looks cloudy.

Also called: degas, degassing, de-gas, vacuum chamber, bell jar, pinholes, bubbles in resin.

How (CS-006 §7.8):

1. Mix and double-pot first (CS-008 §7 step 3).
2. Put the mixed cup in the degassing chamber.
3. Pull vacuum until the foam rises and collapses.
4. Infuse straight away.

Which chamber, what vacuum level and how long under the bell are not written down yet: CS-006 §7.8 marks them for Nick to confirm. Ask a lead.

What to watch (CS-006 §7.8):

- The foam rises several times the resin's height before it collapses. Leave headroom in the cup, or it boils over into the chamber.
- Time under the bell comes out of the pot life: plan on 80–100 min for SLOW and 9–14 min for FAST (IN2 TDS text, CS-006 §7.8). A FAST mix can spend most of its pot life under the bell, so check the clock first.
- A warm cup means the pot life is nearly spent. Do not infuse it; treat it as a hot cup per CS-008 §6.

Degassed or not, keep air out: mix without whipping air in, keep the inlet submerged, hold 27 inHg or better, pass the drop test, and note on the work order where any bubbles showed and whether the resin was degassed (CS-006 §7.8).

sections.title: QR-002 Infusion setup checklist
sections.section: 9. When can I demould (demold) an infusion?
sections.text:
48 h for IN2 + AT30 SLOW and 24 h for IN2 + AT30 FAST, counted from the time you clamped the inlet. Those are the team's FEB holds (CS-006 §7.6 step 1; CS-008 §5.1). The datasheet demould figure is shorter: 18–24 h SLOW and 6–8 h FAST at 25 °C.

Also called: demould, demold, de-mould, cure hold, FEB hold, cure time, pull the part.

"Cure and demould" on the work order stays locked until the hold passes. Only a lead can override it, with a written reason (CS-006 §7.6 step 1). A colder shop runs longer than either figure, and gel is not cure.

1. Wait out the hold.
2. Demould (CS-006 §7.6 step 3).
3. Label the part per CS-001.
4. Photograph it, weigh it, and record both in the work order's quality checks.
5. Hand it on to trimming (CS-009).
6. On the Molds tab, open the mold, add 1 to Parts pulled and set Stage back to Sealed: the PVA came off with the part. It goes back to Ready for layup only after the next release (CS-006 §7.6 step 4).

Full mechanical properties take at least 14 days (CS-006 §7.6 step 2). Trimming can be scheduled freely, but avoid structural or fit loading before then. Every resin's hold and the reasons behind it: QR-001.

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.section: 1. Wet layup bag stack, in order: peel ply, breather, bag
sections.text:
From the part up: wet laminate, peel ply past the laminate edges, breather over the peel ply but held back from every part edge, then the VB160 bag sealed with tacky tape, with a resin trap between bag and pump (CS-007 §7.4).

Also called: bag stack, bagging order, vacuum bag, bag, breather, bleeder, batting, peel ply, release ply, wet layup bag.

1. Lay peel ply over the full laminate, past its edges (CS-007 §7.4 step 1).
2. Lay breather over the peel ply, held back from every part edge it could bond to (CS-007 §7.4 step 2).
3. Run tacky tape and bag with VB160 (CS-007 §7.4 step 3).
4. Pleat every corner, and every 300–400 mm of a curved perimeter (CS-007 §7.4 step 3).
5. Put the resin trap between bag and pump, per CS-006 §7.3.

How far back to hold the breather: CS-007 sets no distance. The rule is that it touches no part edge it could bond to, because resin that wicks into breather at an edge glues it on (CS-007 §4).

Where the work order says so, you may swap the peel ply for a release film (A4000R) or a mylar sheet, or add a caul plate over the peel ply. These are still under test (2026-09): write which one you used on the work order and photograph the finished surface (CS-007 §7.4 step 4).

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.section: 2. Before you mix West: shop temperature and what to cut first
sections.text:
Check the shop is at or above the hardener's minimum before mixing: 206 needs 60 °F (16 °C), 205 needs 40 °F (4 °C), 209 needs 70 °F (21 °C). These are the West datasheet minimums (CS-007 §7.1 step 4).

Also called: minimum temperature, cold shop, hardener choice, 205, 206, 209, prep, wet layup prerequisites.

Below the minimum, pick a hardener whose minimum the shop meets, or wait.

1. Check the stack is frozen and printed on the work order (CS-007 §7.1 step 1).
2. Check the mold is sealed and released per CS-004 with its checks passed, or the plate is waxed, or the foam core is shaped and dry-fitted.
3. Cut the cloth per the work order's ply table (CS-007 §7.1 step 2).
4. Weigh the dry cloth and write the total dry fiber mass on the work order.
5. Cut peel ply, breather, bag and tacky tape to size before any resin is mixed (CS-007 §7.1 step 3). Pot life spent hunting scissors is pot life lost.
6. Read the shop temperature and check it against the hardener (CS-007 §7.1 step 4).

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.section: 3. How much West resin to mix, and the pump ratio
sections.text:
Mix about dry fiber mass × 0.9 of resin. Pump 5:1 by volume for 206 and 205, one full stroke of each pump per shot, never partial strokes. 209 is 3:1 on a different pump head (CS-007 §7.2).

Also called: resin math, how much resin, West, West System, 105, pumps, mix ratio, how much hardener.

The 0.9 is more than the 60:40 fiber to resin target implies, on purpose: the squeegee and breather take the excess out, and the cured part lands near 60:40 (CS-007 §7.2 step 1).

| Hardener | Pumps | By scale (weight) | Pot life per 100 g at 72 °F |
|---|---|---|---|
| 206 slow (default) | 5:1 | 5.36:1 | 20–25 min |
| 205 fast | 5:1 | 5.19:1 | 9–12 min |
| 209 extra slow | 3:1, different pump head | 3.68:1 | 40–50 min |

Sources: West TDSs, as copied into CS-007 §7.2.

1. Work out the mix: dry fiber mass × 0.9.
2. Check the pump head matches the hardener before the first stroke.
3. Pump full strokes only, one of each per shot.
4. Mix per CS-008: at least 2 min, then double-pot.
5. Write mixed and final masses on the work order (CS-007 §7.2 step 1).

A bigger job is several small pots, not one large one. A pot that warms is about to gel (CS-007 §7.2 step 3).

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.text:
Wet out ply by ply: resin on, then squeegee until the ply is shiny-wet with the weave still visible, not swimming. Chase every dry, white patch before the next ply goes on; you will not see it again (CS-007 §7.3 step 1).

Also called: wet out, wet-out, wetting, squeegee, hand layup, dry patch, white fibre, white fiber.

1. Put resin on the ply.
2. Squeegee until it is shiny-wet with the weave visible.
3. Look for dry, white patches and work resin into them.
4. Check the ply against the run's stack ("Stack & BOM") as it goes on (CS-007 §7.3 step 2).
5. Put on the next ply.

A substitution or an extra ply gets edited into the run's stack, with the reason in that ply's Notes (CS-007 §7.3 step 2). A pen tick on a printed traveler is allowed as well.

Swimming in resin is past wet-out, not better (CS-007 §4). The acceptance check is no white or dry weave visible, ply by ply (CS-007 §8).

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.section: 5. Vacuum and drop test for a wet layup
sections.text:
Pull to 25 inHg or better, then isolate the pump: the bag shall lose 2 inHg or less over 10 minutes, then open the valve again. Write the start and end readings in the note on "Wet layup and bag" ("Wet layup over core" on a Foam wrapped run) (CS-007 §7.5).

Also called: drop test, leak test, leak-down, vacuum level, inHg, 25 inHg, vacuum crush.

1. Pull to 25 inHg or better (CS-007 §7.5 step 1).
2. Close the valve to isolate the pump. The gauge must be on the bag side of the closed valve (CS-007 §7.5 step 2).
3. Read the gauge, wait 10 minutes, read it again.
4. Pass is a loss of 2 inHg or less (CS-007 §7.5 step 2).
5. Write both readings in the step note.
6. Failed? Hunt leaks per CS-006 §7.7 (QR-012) and test again.
7. Passed? Open the valve again and check the gauge climbs back to 25 inHg before you walk away (CS-007 §7.5 step 4).

On light foam cores, watch for vacuum crush. If the core dents, reduce the vacuum and write the level that held on the work order, per part (CS-007 §7.5 step 3).

There is no separate drop-test step on the Mold wet lay or Foam wrapped techniques, so the app does not block on this test. A drop-test step placed before "Cure and demould" or "Cure" would switch the cure hold off, which is why the readings go in the "Wet layup and bag" note (CS-007 §7.5).

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.section: 6. Signing the layup and when to demold (demould)
sections.text:
Leave it bagged under vacuum overnight at least. The FEB hold before demold is 24 h for 206 and 205 and 36 h for 209, counted from when you finished bagging (CS-007 §7.6). These are team holds; the datasheet thin-film cure is 10–15 h, 6–8 h and 20–24 h at 72 °F.

Also called: demold, demould, de-mould, cure hold, FEB hold, sign off, buy-off, cure time, pull the part, when can I pull it, take it off the mold, how long to wait, unbag.

1. Leave the part bagged under vacuum overnight at least (CS-007 §7.6 step 1).
2. Before you leave, sign "Wet layup and bag" ("Wet layup over core" on a Foam wrapped run). Signing needs Wet layup training.
3. Under "Resin mixed", pick West 105 + 206 slow, West 105 + 205 fast or West 105 + 209 extra slow, whichever you mixed.
4. Set "Finished on" and "at" to when you finished bagging.
5. Fill in "Shop temperature, °C (optional)". This starts the FEB hold.
6. Come back after the hold. "Cure and demould" ("Cure" on Foam wrapped) stays locked until then (CS-007 §7.6 step 2). Only a lead can sign it early, and the app makes them write why.
7. Write times and masses on the work order, label the part per CS-001 and hand it on for trim (CS-007 §7.6 step 3).
8. On the Molds tab, open the mold, add 1 to Parts pulled and set Stage back to Sealed: the PVA came off with the part (CS-007 §7.6 step 4).

A cold shop runs longer than these figures (CS-007 §7.6 step 1). Every resin's hold and why: QR-001.

sections.title: QR-003 Wet layup and the bag stack
sections.text:
The same wet layup over a shaped foam core instead of a mold: wet plies wrap the core, then peel ply, breather, bag. Watch for vacuum crush on the core: if it dents, reduce vacuum and write the level that held (CS-007 §7.7; §7.5 step 3).

Also called: foam core, foam wrapped, foam-wrapped, wing element, RW elements, E2 to E5, core.

In the app this is the Foam wrapped technique. Its steps are (CS-007 §7.7):

1. "Stack frozen".
2. "Shape foam core" (needs Foam core training).
3. "Wet layup over core" (needs Wet layup training). Signing it starts the cure hold.
4. "Cure" (the hold).
5. "Trim and finish".

Everything else, the resin math, wet-out, drop test and hold, is the same as a wet layup on a mold (QR-003 §3 to §6).

sections.title: QR-004 Mold sealing and release, in order
sections.section: 1. Mold sealing and release, in order
sections.text:
Clean, inspect, seal with XCR, wait the 12 h hold after the last coat, wax (4 coats minimum on a new mold), wait 1 h, PVA (2 coats), then label the mold and set it to Ready for layup (CS-004 §7.1 to §7.5).

Also called: mold prep, mould prep, seal and release, sealing, release, mold sealing order.
