- Technique: the step checklist a part's Layup type picks: Mold infusion, Glass infusion, Mold wet lay, Foam wrapped or Other (CS-013 §7.5).
- Issue: raised with ⚠ Raise an issue or ⚑ on a step; a run cannot complete until every issue has a Disposition, What happened and What was done (CS-013 §7.6 steps 1 and 3).
- OnHold: a run someone has parked. It blocks nothing (CS-013 §4).
- Retro WO: a back-filled SN5 record, `WO-SN5-*`; its unverifiable fields say "not recorded (retro)" (CS-013 §4).
- ME and RE: the Mold Engineer and the Manufacturing Engineer, the two engineer fields on a part (CS-013 §4; QR-009 §14).

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 9. Part, R&D part, study and coupon: which is which?
sections.text:
A part is something the car needs, built through runs. An R&D part is a real build that feeds a decision instead of the car, with every blocker, hold and evidence check still enforced. A study (`RDS`) holds coupons (`CPN`), test pieces with no work order and no cure hold (CS-013 §4).

Also called: R&D, R and D, research, test, trial; R&D part, R&D WO; study, R&D study, RDS; coupon, CPN, test piece, specimen, tensile coupon; test panel, PNL, flat panel; season part, deliverable.

- R&D builds: coupon campaigns, flat test panels, layup trials, sealing and grounding experiments, mold shakedowns (CS-013 §4).
- R&D is a property of the part, not a status. A work order inherits it from its part (CS-013 §4).
- An R&D part is kept off the Season tab, the Google Sheet mirror and the Parts and Work Orders lists. It lives on the R&D tab, and is marked `R&D` on screen, on the label and on the scan page (CS-013 §4).
- The R&D mark is a ruled box on the label's ID line. It is not a class word (CS-001 §4).
- Which to make: test pieces you will cut, measure and compare should go in a study. Anything with a mold, a checklist or a cure you need to sign should be a part and a run, marked R&D if it is not for the car (CS-013 §2).
- The panel a coupon is cut from is still a build; the pieces cut from it are bench records (CS-013 §2).

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 10. Stack and ply words: layup stack, ply table, stack frozen, as-built
sections.text:
The layup stack is the ordered list of plies from the mold surface (P1) outward, including cores, meshes and inserts (CS-002 §4). Stack frozen is the buy-off that locks a run's copy of it; the as-built is that copy as laid.

Also called: stack, layup, lay-up, layup schedule, ply table, ply book, plies; stack frozen, freeze, stack freeze; as-built; orientation, 0/90, ±45; 88, 195, 220, 670, spread tow, twill; sacrificial ply.

- Cloth naming: `<gsm> <weave>`, for example 88 spread-tow, 195 twill, 220 twill, 670 twill (Sigmatex). Always gsm, never "the thick one" (CS-002 §4).
- Orientation: warp direction against the part's 0° datum; 0/90 or ±45 for woven cloth (CS-002 §4).
- Inserts: a G10 insert is a ply in the table, like a core, with material and thickness (CS-002 §4).
- Plan and as-built: the plan is the stack on the part (Parts tab, Layup stack). The as-built is the copy each run takes when it starts. Editing the run's copy never changes the plan (CS-002 §4).
- Stack freeze: from the Stack frozen buy-off on, edits to the part's plan no longer reach that run (CS-002 §4).
- Sacrificial ply: the 88 spread-tow outer layer that absorbs sanding. It is the sanding budget; structural plies are not (CS-009 §4).

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 11. Material and inventory words: lot, material type, EH&S tag, How full
sections.text:
A lot is one record for one physical thing on a shelf: one roll of cloth, one jug of resin or hardener, or one record with a count for a consumable (CS-014 §4). Material type is what kind of thing it is across every container, such as `IN2` or `AT30`.

Also called: lot, batch, jug, roll, container, kit; material type; vendor lot, batch number; EH&S tag, UC tag, RSS tag, Data Matrix; expiry, expiration, use-by; How full; Hazard; stock walk; min stock, minimum, Running out.

- Lot IDs: `FAB-SN6-###`, `RSN-SN6-###` (resin and hardener share it; the Role says which) and `CON-SN6-###` (CS-014 §4).
- Vendor lot number: the batch number the manufacturer printed. Blank when none is printed.
- EH&S tag: the UC EH&S barcode sticker campus puts on every chemical container. A Data Matrix square marked RSS with a 24-character code. FEB never prints one (CS-014 §4).
- State: Sealed, Open, Empty or Expired. How full: Full, Half, Low or Empty (CS-014 §4).
- Hazard: flammable, not flammable, or blank, which means unknown (CS-014 §4).
- Expiry from: where the Expires date came from: vendor label, vendor label (AI read), or shelf-life table (CS-014 §4).
- Incoming: bought and not yet fully received (CS-014 §4).
- Min-stock: the level that triggers a reorder. Stock walk: the monthly check of every shelf against its record. Home location: the shelf (`BIN-SN6-###`) a thing belongs on (CS-011 §4).
- AI read: anything a ✨ button filled from a photo. A draft until a person checks it (CS-014 §4).

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 12. Label words: label, class word, QR code, R&D mark, engraving
sections.text:
A label is the printed 4 × 1 in tag with the name, the ID, a key line and a QR code (CS-001 §4). The QR code opens a public page naming the object, from any phone camera, with no account needed.

Also called: label, sticker, tag; QR, QR code, barcode, scan code; class word; R&D mark, R&D box; mark, marker, paint marker; engraving, engraved ID; Data Matrix, EH&S tag.

- Class word: what kind of object a record is (PART, MOLD, WORK ORDER, FABRIC, RESIN and so on). The app derives it from the ID prefix; it is not printed on the label except STORAGE (CS-001 §4).
- R&D mark: the word R&D in a ruled box on the ID line. Not a class word (CS-001 §4).
- Mark: a hand-written ID in oil-based paint marker where a label cannot go (CS-001 §4).
- Engraving: the ID cut into a mold during machining. The record of record for a mold (CS-001 §4).
- Data Matrix: the square code on an EH&S tag. FEB's own labels are QR; the app's scanner reads both (CS-001 §4).
- Custom label: a label with no record. Never for anything with a record (CS-001 §7.13).
- Which label goes where is QR-005.

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 13. Trim, sand and bond words: trim line, keying, open time, handling strength
sections.text:
The trim line is the part's cut boundary, transferred from the mold's scribe lines at demold. Keying is abrading a bond face so adhesive can grip; the team uses 120 grit (CS-009 §4).

Also called: trim, trimming, trim line, edge; sand, sanding, key, keying, scuff; open time, work life; handling strength, clamp time; load-carrying bond, structural bond, insert, rod end; bond, glue, bonding.

- Open time: the longest a joint may wait after adhesive goes on a face before it is closed and fixed. 20 min for DP420 (CS-009 §4).
- Handling strength: the point where a bonded joint can be unclamped and moved, not loaded. 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F) for DP420 (CS-009 §4).
- Load-carrying bond: any bond that carries load on the car: an insert, a rod end, a mount, a bracket (CS-009 §4).
- Sacrificial ply: the 88 spread-tow outer layer that absorbs sanding; it is the sanding budget, and structural plies are not (CS-009 §4; QR-009 §10).
- Grounding point: the fastener or tab where a part's conductive path meets chassis ground. Surface path: a conductor added to a cured part's surface (CS-010 §4).
- Steps are in QR-013.

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 14. People and roles: Composites Lead, ME, RE, certified operator
sections.text:
The Composites Lead signs each standard's Approver row (CS-000 §4). On each part, the ME (Mold Engineer) and RE (Manufacturing Engineer) are the two engineer fields, picked from the app's roster (CS-002 §4, CS-013 §4).

Also called: lead, comp lead, composites lead; ME, mold engineer; RE, manufacturing engineer; certified operator, HOT; purchaser; approver; Paul; Steve.

- Lead: a lead is not trained by being a lead. A lead may sign a step that needs training without it, and writes why (CS-013 §4).
- Person fields: every field that names a person is picked from the roster. Use “name” only for someone not on the app (CS-013 §4).
- Certified operator: did the RFS ShopSabre training and HOT. RFS's own record is the authority; the app's ShopSabre CNC training mirrors it (CS-005 §4).
- Larry: reviews the CAM you made yourself before it runs; G10 runs only with his say-so (CS-005 §2, §4).
- ESO: confirms HV isolation before anyone measures resistance on an installed part (CS-010 §6).
- Purchaser: a member who fronts money and gets reimbursed (CS-012 §4).
- Approvers by amount: under $50 the subteam lead, $50 to $250 the division lead, over $250 the President or VP (CS-012 §4).
- Stock-walk owner: named by the lead at season start (CS-011 §7.1).
- Paul: the app's helper, which searches these documents. Steve: the team's joke helper; nothing he says is a rule.

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 15. Places and channels: RFS, Jacobs basement, etch locker, #composites
sections.text:
RFS is Richmond Field Station, where the team manufactures: the ShopSabre, the RFS container and the shop are there. Finished parts live in the Jacobs basement, never the etch locker (CS-011 §7.3).

Also called: RFS, Richmond, the shop, the field station; Jacobs, Jacobs Hall, Jacobs basement; etch locker; RFS container, container; flammables cabinet; General Box; Slack, #composites, #aerodynamics, #purchasing-slackbot, #purchasing; weekly meeting.

- Storage sites as the app names them: RFS container, Jacobs basement, Flammables cabinet, Dry sealed bin, General Box, Other (CS-011 §7.3).
- Etch locker: finished parts are never stored there (2026-04-20 agreement, CS-011 §7.3).
- Jacobs Hall also has the OMAX waterjet (CS-009 §5).
- #composites: the team's channel. #aerodynamics: where aero parts are often defined.
- #purchasing-slackbot: where purchases are requested and reimbursed through the bot. #purchasing was retired on 2026-10-07 (CS-012).
- Weekly meeting: the composites meeting, now on Wednesdays. Older documents say "Monday meeting" (CS-000 Rev D history).
- Which shelf holds what is QR-014.

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 16. Purchasing words: reference ID, REQ number, /purchase, Charged to
sections.text:
A reference ID is the budget line a purchase is paid from, such as `COMP-011`; composites lines start `COMP-` (CS-012 §4). A REQ number is the purchasing bot's number for a request, such as `REQ-000064`.

Also called: reference ID, budget line, budget code, COMP-, TRAN-012, -000; REQ, request number; purchasing bot, Flux, the bot; /purchase, /bigorder, /reference, /reimburse; Charged to; Order status, Reimbursement; reimburse, reimbursement, paid back.

- Purchasing bot: the Flux bot in #purchasing-slackbot. `/purchase` requests one purchase, `/bigorder` several items on different reference IDs, `/reference` lists the reference IDs, `/reimburse` takes a reference ID and an amount (CS-012 §4).
- A `-000` ID means an item the budget never listed (CS-012 §4).
- Charged to: the Budget tab field naming the budget a purchase lands on. Blank, or Composites, means ours (CS-012 §4).
- Order status (the goods) and Reimbursement (the money): the Budget tab's two tracks for one purchase (CS-012 §4).
- Restock: the Purpose for the shared Easy Composites order, which replaced SN5's "basket" doc (CS-012 §7.4).
- How to buy something and get paid back is QR-015.

sections.title: QR-009 Words the team uses
sections.section: 17. Machining words: ShopSabre, HOT, ATC, CAM review, Max-Z
sections.text:
The ShopSabre is the CNC router at RFS that cuts the team's molds. HOT is the RFS hands-on-training sign-off you need before you run it on your own (CS-005 §4). The Shopbot in Jacobs is the machine the team used before it.

Also called: ShopSabre, CNC, router, Shopbot, HOT, hands-on training, ATC, tool changer, CAM review, Larry, max-Z, cut depth.

- Max-Z: the machine's maximum cut depth. A taller mold is split into sections with alignment datums unless the split is waived (CS-003 §4).
- ATC: the automatic tool changer. It swaps tools from its rack mid-program and measures each tool's length, so a tool change needs no manual re-zero (CS-005 §4).
- CAM review: Larry reviews the CAM you made yourself before it runs (CS-005 §4).
- Certified operator: did the RFS ShopSabre training and HOT. RFS's record is the authority, and the app's ShopSabre CNC training mirrors it (CS-005 §4).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 1. What tabs does the app have?
sections.text:
The sidebar lists twelve tabs: Dashboard and Season at the top; Parts, Work Orders, Molds, Inventory and R&D under Build; Schedule and Budget under Planning; Documents, Reports and People under Team (`app/core.js` TABS, GROUPS).

Also called: app, web app, FEB Composites, the website, tabs, pages, menu, sidebar, nav, navigation.

| Group | Tab | What it is for (from its tooltip) |
|---|---|---|
| (top) | Dashboard | The team-wide picture |
| (top) | Season | The blueprint: every part we mean to make |
| Build | Parts | Every part, its mold, its stack and its runs |
| Build | Work Orders | One run at making a part |
| Build | Molds | Molds, stack plans and tooling board |
| Build | Inventory | What we have and where it lives |
| Build | R&D | Coupon studies, test pieces and trials |
| Planning | Schedule | The season by station, or the week by person |
| Planning | Budget | Purchases, arrivals and reimbursement |
| Team | Documents | Datasheets, uploads and the team shelf of links |
| Team | Reports | Exports, print boards, labels |
| Team | People | The roster and who carries what |

On a phone the sidebar is behind the Menu button at the top left, or swipe in from the left edge. On a wide screen, Collapse at the foot of the sidebar shrinks it to icons.

Build runs in the order the work happens: you make the part, then the run that makes it, pulled off a mold, from material in Inventory (`app/core.js`).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 2. Where is tooling board? (Stock is gone)
sections.text:
Tooling board is under Inventory → Boards, one record per sheet or offcut (`BRD-SN6-###`). There is no Stock tab any more: old Stock links and scanned board codes open Inventory or Molds instead (`app/core.js`, `app/inventory.js`).

Also called: tooling board, board, foam board, Precision Board, PBLT, offcuts, remnants, Stock, stock tab, rack, board rack.

1. Open Inventory.
2. Press Boards in the row at the top (Storage map, Items list, Materials list, Boards).
3. Press + Board to record a new sheet or offcut.

The stack planner picks thicknesses only from boards recorded here, so a board that is not in Boards does not exist to the planner (CS-003 §5).

Stack plans and the cut list live on the Molds tab, not here (QR-010 §3).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 3. Where are molds, stack plans and the cut list?
sections.text:
Everything about molds is on the Molds tab: + Mold to plan a new one, Cut list, Labels and Plan from Fusion along the top, and the list of molds with their stage. A mold's stack plan (`STK-SN6-###`) shows under Mold file on the mold's page (`app/molds.js`).

Also called: mold, mould, tool, molds tab; stack plan, board plan, stock plan, STK; cut list, cutting list; mold stage.

| What you want | Where |
|---|---|
| Plan a new mold's stack | Molds → + Mold |
| The cut list for blanks | Molds → Cut list (shows once a stack plan exists) |
| Mold labels | Molds → Labels |
| The Fusion add-in download | Molds → Plan from Fusion (QR-011) |
| A mold's current plan | The mold's page → Mold file; older plans under Earlier, marked Superseded |
| Molds by stage | The stage filter (All stages) above the list |

The filter chips "retired" and "no home" show retired molds and molds with no location.

A mold that will not be used again is retired, never deleted (CS-003 §4).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 4. Where are resin, cloth and consumables?
sections.text:
On Inventory. Storage map shows every shelf and what is on it; Items list and Materials list show the same things as lists. Receive a delivery, Labels, Custom label and Export sit on the same toolbar (`app/inventory.js`).

Also called: inventory, materials, resin, hardener, cloth, fabric, carbon, consumables, jugs, rolls, shelf, storage, find, location.

| What you want | Where |
|---|---|
| What is on a shelf | Inventory → Storage map, then the shelf |
| Resin, hardener, fabric and consumable lots as a list | Inventory → Materials list |
| Panels, jigs and storage locations as a list | Inventory → Items list |
| Log a delivery | Inventory → Receive a delivery (QR-006) |
| What is on order and not yet here | The Incoming card on the Storage map |
| A new shelf or bin | Storage map → + Location |
| Print labels for many records | Inventory → Labels |
| The EH&S reconciliation | Inventory → Export |
| Import from campus RSS | Inventory → EH&S import (leads only) |

There used to be separate Items and Materials tabs. Since 2026-08-04 they are views of Inventory, and old links to them land there (`app/core.js`).

To find one thing fast, scan its label with the scan button in the top bar, or search with Search (⌘K).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 5. Where did Tickets, Items, Materials, Stock and Weekly Plan go?
sections.text:
They are hidden now, and old links still work. Items and Materials are views of Inventory. Stock opens Inventory → Boards or the Molds tab. Weekly Plan is the Week by person view of Schedule. Tickets became issues on a work order (`app/core.js` TABS).

Also called: tickets, projects, PROJ, items tab, materials tab, stock tab, weekly plan, week plan, missing tab, find, location, lost tab, moved, renamed, hidden tab.

| Old tab | Where it is now |
|---|---|
| Items | Inventory → Items list |
| Materials | Inventory → Materials list |
| Stock | Inventory → Boards for board; Molds for stack plans |
| Weekly Plan | Schedule → Week by person |
| Tickets | An issue on the run it holds up, in the run's Issues section (QR-007) |

The Tickets tab was shelved on 2026-08-25, not deleted. Every `PROJ-SN6-###` record is still in the database, and a link to one still opens its page (`app/core.js`).

Schedule has two views at the top: Season by station and Week by person (`app/timeline.js`).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.text:
On the Reports tab, always open, under Recently deleted. Press Restore on a row to put it back. A deleted record stays for 30 days with its uploads (`app/reports.js`; CS-013 §7.7).

Also called: recently deleted, deleted, bin, trash, recycle bin, undo delete, restore, recover; archived.

Each row says what was deleted, who deleted it, how long ago and how many days are left. Restoring one brings back everything deleted with it, such as a run and its issues.

Past 30 days a lead presses Empty them, and the records are gone for good (CS-013 §7.7 step 4).

An archived part or run is not in Recently deleted. It is hidden from the lists but kept whole: press the archived chip on the Parts or Work Orders list to see archived records, each with Restore (CS-013 §7.7 step 1).

The rest of the Reports tab, top to bottom: the weekly status board (Print status board), Layup techniques, and Exports and maintenance, which holds Export a CSV, Labels (Label sheet, Custom label, Label media) and, for leads, Maintenance (`app/reports.js`).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 7. Where are the standards and datasheets?
sections.text:
Datasheets (TDS and SDS) are on the Documents tab, under Datasheets. The CS standards are not listed on the Documents tab today: ask Paul, who searches them and links the section he quotes (`app/documents.js`, `app/paul.js`).

Also called: standards, CS standards, SOP, procedure, quick reference, QR; datasheet, TDS, SDS, MSDS, safety sheet; documents, docs, files.

1. For a datasheet, open Documents and look under Datasheets, or type its name in "search documents…".
2. For a resin or hardener you are holding, open its lot page. The TDS and SDS buttons there open that material's sheets (CS-014 §5).
3. For a standard, press Ask Paul in the top bar and ask the question. Each answer lists its Sources; press one to open the standard beside the chat.

The top of Documents is the Team shelf: links pinned with + Pin a link, for the things people keep asking for (the master tracker, the meeting deck). + Upload document adds a file of your own (`app/documents.js`).

The standards files are still shipped with the app, so a standard that was issued stays retrievable. They are only left off the Documents list (`app/documents.js`).

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 8. How do I ask Paul or Steve?
sections.text:
Press Ask Paul (the speech-bubble button in the top bar). It shows only when a lead has AI features on. The panel has a Paul and Steve switch, Chats for your saved conversations, and New chat (`app/paul.js`, `app/core.js`).

Also called: Paul, ask Paul, chat, AI, assistant, helper, bot; Steve, Fibreglast; chats, chat history, new chat.

1. Press Ask Paul in the top bar.
2. Type the question. If a record is open, Paul starts from it ("Looking at …"); press × on that chip to ask without it.
3. Press a number in the answer, or a line under Sources, to open where it came from.
4. Press Chats to see saved conversations, and Back to return.
5. Press New chat to start over.

Paul answers from the team's records, the standards and the datasheets, and cites each one. Steve is the team's joke helper: every Steve answer carries "Steve is always wrong" and an Ask Paul instead button. Under a Paul answer, "What would Steve say?" asks Steve (`app/paul.js`).

Never act on anything Steve says. Check any number from Paul against the source he links.

sections.title: QR-010 Where things are in the app
sections.section: 9. The top bar: scan, search, notifications and backup
sections.text:
The top bar holds Scan a label, Search (⌘K), Ask Paul, Notifications and the light or dark theme switch. On a wide screen it also shows the version with What's new, Backup, and Sign out. On a phone those are under More (⋯) (`app/core.js`).

Also called: top bar, header, scan, scanner, QR scanner, search, find, notifications, bell, backup, sign out, log out, version, what's new.

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Scan a label | Opens the camera; reads an FEB label or a UC EH&S tag and opens the record (CS-001 §7.12) |
| Search (⌘K) | Searches every record (parts, runs, issues, purchases, molds, boards, stack plans, shelves, lots), people and documents, and shows the shelf a thing is on |
| Ask Paul | Opens Paul, the app's helper (QR-010 §8) |
| Notifications | Your notifications, with a count of unread ones. Not shown to a guest |
| Backup / Backup database | Downloads the whole database as one file |
| What's new | What changed in this version |

On a phone, More (⋯) holds Dark theme or Light theme, Change photo, Backup database, Sign out and the version line. Leads also see Restore from backup and the ✨ AI features switch with the month's spend (`app/core.js`).

A guest (View as guest) can read everything and change nothing, and sees Sign in instead of Backup.

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 1. How do I install the Fusion add-in?
sections.text:
On the app's Molds tab, press Plan from Fusion. It opens the latest release page. Download `FEBPlanStock-<version>.zip`, unzip it, double-click the installer for your computer, then quit Fusion and open it again (CS-003 §5; add-in README).

Also called: Fusion, Fusion 360, add-in, addin, plugin, plug-in, FEBPlanStock, Plan stock, install, installer.

1. In the app, open the Molds tab and press Plan from Fusion.
2. Download `FEBPlanStock-<version>.zip` from the release page.
3. Unzip the whole download. The installer has to see the FEBPlanStock folder next to it.
4. On a Mac, double-click `Install on Mac.command`. On Windows, double-click `Install on Windows.bat`.
5. Quit Fusion and open it again.
6. Check that the FEB panel is on the Utilities tab of the Design workspace, with a Plan stock button on it.

To load it without restarting: Utilities, Add-Ins, the Add-Ins tab, select FEBPlanStock, press Run (add-in README).

On first use the panel shows the app's sign-in card. Sign in with your own composites app account. It remembers you on that machine, and your name is stamped on the molds you plan (INSTALL.txt).

The Windows installer follows Autodesk's documented path but had not been run on a Windows machine when it shipped. If you install on Windows, tell the composites lead how it goes (INSTALL.txt).

To update, download the newer zip and run the installer again. It replaces the add-in and keeps your settings (INSTALL.txt).

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 2. macOS says "Apple could not verify it is free of malware"
sections.text:
That is expected the first time you run the installer from a download, and it clears in three steps: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, then double-click the installer again and press Open (INSTALL.txt).

Also called: Mac security warning, Gatekeeper, unidentified developer, cannot be opened, malware warning, Open Anyway, quarantine.

1. Press Done on the dialog.
2. Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security.
3. Scroll down to Security. Find the line about "Install on Mac.command" and press Open Anyway.
4. Double-click the installer again.
5. Press Open.

It happens once per download and does not come back (add-in README). The team does not pay Apple to sign the installer, which is why the dialog appears (INSTALL.txt).

The installer also clears the quarantine flag a browser puts on every file in a downloaded zip, so the add-in itself loads without a second warning (add-in README).

Do not copy the add-in folder in by hand to get round the dialog. Copying by hand overwrites `credentials.json`, which the installer keeps (add-in README).

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 3. Planning a mold's stock from Fusion, step by step
sections.text:
Open the mold design, press Utilities tab → FEB panel → Plan stock, select the Mold body (one body at a time), set density in the app's mold dialog that opens in the palette, and press Plan (CS-003 §7.1 step 9).

Also called: plan stock, stock plan, stack plan, board plan, plan from Fusion, mold body, bottom face, CAM stock.

1. Open the mold design in Fusion.
2. Press Utilities tab → FEB panel → Plan stock.
3. Select the Mold body. Plan one body at a time (CS-003 §7.1 step 8).
4. If the mold is not modelled bottom-down (a split mold on its side), also select the Bottom face: the flat face the stack is glued up from (CS-003 §7.1 step 9).
5. Press OK. The FEB Composites palette opens on the right with the mesh loaded.
6. Sign in if the palette asks. The mold opens by itself once you have.
7. In the mold dialog, set the board density. For a range, use Board density, min (lb/ft³) and Board density, max (lb/ft³) (CS-003 §5).
8. Press Plan.
9. Save the Fusion document yourself. The add-in saves nothing to it (CS-003 §7.1 step 9).

Grades shall not be swapped silently: plan at one grade, or give the range in the dialog (CS-003 §5).

With Boards set to choose them for me, from stock (the default), the planner picks thicknesses only from boards recorded in Inventory → Boards. I'll pick the thicknesses is not checked against the rack: use it only for boards you have in hand. Either way it splits any stack over 6 in into sections (CS-003 §7.1 step 8). If no board of your density is recorded, add boards, widen the range, or plan at a density that is on the rack (add-in README).

Plan the stack before the Mold design review (CS-003 §7.1 step 8).

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 4. Where does the plan go after I press Plan?
sections.text:
Into the app. The planner creates the mold record at Designed with the plan (`STK-SN6-###`) as its Mold file, and Fusion draws the blanks as see-through bodies in a component named after the plan. Use them as CAM stock (CS-003 §7.1 steps 8 and 9).

Also called: STK, stack plan, Mold file, where did my plan go, blanks, blocks, stock bodies, component.

| Where | What you find |
|---|---|
| Fusion | A component named after the plan (`STK-SN6-###`), one see-through body per blank. Fusion confirms "[plan] is saved in the app … Nothing is saved to this document yet." |
| App, Molds tab | The new mold record (`MOLD-SN6-###`) at stage Designed |
| App, the mold's page | The plan under Mold file, and the Stack drawing (under the heading Stack, below Mold in stock) |
| App, Molds → Cut list | The blanks to cut. The cut list does not check the review: cut only for a mold whose Mold design review is signed (CS-003 §7.2; §7.3 step 1) |

Running Plan stock again on the same mold replaces that component in Fusion (add-in README).

STL planning is marked beta. Check the Stack drawing on the mold page (under the heading Stack) before anyone cuts, and plan from dimensions if it looks wrong (CS-003 §7.1 step 8).

Re-plans are a lead's. On a mold that already has a plan, a lead presses Re-plan; the old plan stays under Earlier, marked Superseded. Cut and machine only from the current plan (CS-003 §7.1 step 8).

A split mold's pieces are separate mold records. Link every piece on the part page with + Link a mold…, then + Link another mold…. Each piece gets its own run and its own design review. + New run fills in the part's first linked mold: on the second piece's run, set Mold ID in the run's Details to that piece's `MOLD-SN6-###` (CS-003 §7.1 step 10).

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 5. The app says my Fusion add-in is out of date
sections.text:
The app found an add-in older than it expects. Reinstall it: press Plan from Fusion on the Molds tab, download the newest zip, run the installer again, and restart Fusion (`app/fusion.js`; CS-003 §5).

Also called: out of date, old add-in, outdated, update the add-in, version mismatch, add-in version, reinstall.

The message reads: "This machine's Fusion add-in is [its version] and the app expects [the minimum]. Reinstall it from Plan from Fusion on the Molds tab." It shows once per page and never stops you: an old add-in usually still plans a mold, it just misses what the newer one learned to send (`app/fusion.js`).

1. On the Molds tab, press Plan from Fusion.
2. Download the newest `FEBPlanStock-<version>.zip`.
3. Unzip it and run the installer over the old install. That is how you update.
4. Quit Fusion and open it again.

The add-in carries the app's own version number, not one of its own. The number on the zip is the app version it was built against, so an add-in and an app showing the same number are a matched pair (add-in README).

An add-in old enough to send no version at all also counts as out of date (`app/fusion.js`).

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 6. What does the split waiver measure?
sections.text:
Nothing. Ticking "Machined depth stays under 6in" is a claim by the person ticking it. The app records who ticked it and when and shows the mold as split waived, but it does not measure the cavity (CS-003 §7.1 step 6; `app/molds.js`).

Also called: split waiver, split waived, no split, do not section, max-Z, max Z, cut depth, tall mold, 6 inch, sections.

The planner splits any stack over 6 in into sections automatically (CS-003 §7.1 step 6, `app/slicer.js`, 152.4 mm). The checkbox in the mold dialog stops that.

Tick it only when the design keeps the cutter within 6 in of a face it can reach (CS-003 §7.1 step 6):

- a shallow cavity in a tall blank;
- dowelled inserts;
- a face machined from both sides.

Leave it clear and a tall stack is split into sections, with the split's dowel and datum features designed in CAD, not improvised at the machine (CS-003 §7.1 step 6).

The design reviewer checks the claim. Mold design review check 6 asks for height within machine max-Z, or splits with alignment features designed, or a split waiver with the reviewer having checked the deepest machined point and the tool's reach past the collet (CS-003 §7.2). The machine's max-Z value is in CS-005 §5.

sections.title: QR-011 Fusion add-in: planning stock
sections.section: 7. The add-in does nothing, or the mold never opens
sections.text:
Read `febplanstock.log` beside the installed add-in first: one line per step. If the palette says a mold from Fusion is waiting on something, do that thing (sign in, wait for the rack to load) and the mold opens by itself (add-in README; `app/fusion.js`).

Also called: not working, nothing happens, stuck, add-in broken, palette blank, log file, error, troubleshooting.

| What you see | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|
| "A mold from Fusion is waiting on a sign-in." | Sign in in the palette. The mold opens once you have |
| "... waiting on a real sign-in (guests cannot create molds)" | Press Sign in and sign in with your own account |
| "... waiting on the rack to load" | Wait a few seconds; the board list is still loading |
| No board of your density on the rack | Add boards in Inventory → Boards, widen the range, or plan at a density that is recorded |
| A sign-in failure in a Fusion message box | Check `credentials.json`, or sign in in the palette yourself |
| Nothing after "sent mesh" in the log | The add-in reloads the page once. If that fails, close the palette, stop and run FEBPlanStock under Utilities, Add-Ins, and try again |

If the palette is closed, Plan stock reopens it (add-in README).

If none of this helps, send `febplanstock.log` to the composites lead with what you were doing (INSTALL.txt).

To remove the add-in, delete the FEBPlanStock folder from Fusion's AddIns directory (INSTALL.txt).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 1. My bag won't hold vacuum: where to look for the leak
sections.text:
Look at the tacky tape seams first, then the pleat folds, the connector bases and the spiral ends, which can pierce the bag. If the gauge will not pass 25 inHg, hunt now: press the seams, listen, re-seat pleats and connector bases (CS-006 §7.4).

Also called: leak, leaking, air leak, losing vacuum, bag won't hold, won't pull down, vacuum leak, bag leak.

1. Press along every tacky tape seam, all the way round (CS-006 §7.4 step 1).
2. Listen for a hiss.
3. Re-seat each pleat fold.
4. Re-seat each through-bag connector base.
5. Check the spiral-wrap ends: a sharp cut end pierces the bag (CS-006 §7.4 step 3). Tape them over.
6. Soapy water only on hose fittings and connectors outside the bag: brush it on and watch for bubbles. Never on bag film, pleats or tape seams over a dry stack; find those by pressing and listening (CS-006 §7.7).
7. Pull vacuum again and re-run the drop test.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Do (CS-006 §7.7) |
|---|---|---|
| Gauge won't reach 25 inHg | Perimeter leak, connector base, pleat fold | Press seams, re-seat. Soapy water only on fittings and connectors outside the bag, never on the bag over a dry stack |
| Passes 27, then creeps down | Micro-leak: spiral end or bag puncture | Patch with a square of tacky tape; drop test again |
| Leak you cannot find | Air coming through the mold, or a sharp edge piercing the bag | See QR-012 §3 |

The same hunt applies to a wet layup bag (CS-007 §7.5 step 2). Do not mix resin for an infusion until the drop test passes (CS-006 §7.4 step 3).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 2. What passes the drop test? (inHg numbers for infusion and wet layup)
sections.text:
Infusion: pull to 27 inHg or better, isolate the pump, and lose 1 inHg or less over 10 minutes, then open the valve again (CS-006 §7.4). Wet layup: pull to 25 inHg or better and lose 2 inHg or less over 10 minutes (CS-007 §7.5).

Also called: drop test, leak test, leak-down, leakdown, vacuum test, pass fail, inHg.

| Process | Vacuum before the test | Pass | Where the readings go |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infusion | 27 inHg or better | 1 inHg or less lost in 10 min | Note on "Drop test, 1 inHg or less over 10 min" |
| Wet layup | 25 inHg or better | 2 inHg or less lost in 10 min | Note on "Wet layup and bag" ("Wet layup over core" on Foam wrapped) |

Sources: CS-006 §7.4 steps 1 and 2; CS-007 §7.5 steps 1 and 2.

1. Pull to the vacuum in the table.
2. Close the valve to isolate the pump. The gauge must be on the bag side of the closed valve, never on the pump (CS-006 §5; CS-006 §7.4 step 2).
3. Read the gauge.
4. Wait 10 minutes.
5. Read it again.
6. Write both readings in the step note.
7. On a pass, open the valve again and check the gauge climbs back to the vacuum in the table before you open the inlet or walk away (CS-006 §7.4 step 4; CS-007 §7.5 step 4).

On an infusion the drop-test step will not take a member's signature without the note, and "Infuse" cannot be signed until it is (CS-006 §7.4 step 2). A lead can sign without it (Sign without it), and the reason goes in the work order's event log. Fail means keep hunting and test again; no resin until it passes (CS-006 §7.4 step 3).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 3. Air leaking in from nowhere (a leak you cannot find)
sections.text:
If you have pressed every seam and still lose vacuum, look next at the mold itself (an unsealed back or side, or a crack), and at a sharp mold edge or mesh corner piercing the bag from inside (CS-006 §7.7).

Also called: leak you can't find, mystery leak, leak from nowhere, air through the mold, pinhole, bag puncture.

1. Sand or radius sharp mold edges, or edge them with breather (CS-006 §7.7).
2. Chamfer or tape down the flow mesh corners.
3. Check whether the mold's back and sides were sealed. Sealing them is shop practice; CS-004 does not yet require it (CS-006 §7.7).
4. Check the mold for cracks.
5. Patch any bag puncture with a square of tacky tape.
6. Drop test again.

This fix list is shop practice (Larry, #composites 2026-04-03), recorded in CS-006 §7.7.

If the gauge passes 27 inHg and then creeps down, it is more likely a micro-leak at a spiral end or a small bag puncture: patch it with a square of tacky tape and drop test again (CS-006 §7.7).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 4. Dry spot or resin not flowing during an infusion (resin still wet)
sections.text:
A dry patch far from the inlet while the resin is still wet: call the experienced infuser about an emergency second feed, and do not pierce the bag yourself (CS-006 §7.7). The usual causes are mesh that did not cover the area, or resin travel over 0.5 m from the feed.

Also called: dry spot, dry patch, starved area, unwetted, white fibre, white fiber, resin starved, flow stopped, resin not flowing, stopped flowing, flow front stalled, stuck.

1. While the resin is still wet, call the experienced infuser (CS-006 §7.1 step 3) about an emergency second feed. Do not pierce the bag yourself (CS-006 §7.7).
2. Write what happened and where on the work order, with a photo (CS-006 §7.5 step 6).

Prevent it next time (CS-006 §7.2):

- Flow mesh over the entire part, stopping 30–50 mm short of the outlet side.
- Resin travel inlet to outlet about 0.5 m at most. A larger part needs more feeds, planned on the work order.
- Mix enough: (dry fiber mass × 0.65) × 1.2–1.3, rounded up. Starving an infusion mid-pull cannot be recovered (CS-006 §7.5 step 1).

Full wet-out is checked through the bag at clamp time and again after demould: no dry patches (CS-006 §8).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 5. Dry spot found after the part has cured
sections.text:
A dry patch in a cured part cannot be fixed by more resin through the bag. Record it as a defect on the work order and assess it against the part's quality checks (CS-006 §7.7). Photograph it.

Also called: dry spot, dry patch, cured dry spot, defect, white fibre, white fiber, starved laminate, porosity.

1. Photograph the dry area (CS-006 §7.5 step 6).
2. Record it as a defect on the work order (CS-006 §7.7).
3. Assess it against the work order's quality checks.
4. Note for the next run what caused it: mesh coverage, travel distance over 0.5 m, or not enough resin (CS-006 §7.2; CS-006 §7.5 step 1).

The full wet-out check is no dry patches visible, at clamp time and after demould, recorded in the work order's quality checks with photos (CS-006 §8).

For a wet layup, dry patches are caught ply by ply: squeegee each ply until it is shiny-wet with the weave visible, and chase every dry, white patch before the next ply goes on, because you will not see it again (CS-007 §7.3 step 1).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 6. Race-tracking: resin racing along one edge
sections.text:
Race-tracking is resin finding a fast path, usually along an edge, and reaching the outlet before wetting the middle. Clamp the inlet briefly, rely on the mesh break, and note it for the next mold: tape a dam (CS-006 §7.7).

Also called: race-tracking, racetracking, racing, edge flow, resin running along the edge.

1. Clamp the inlet briefly (CS-006 §7.7).
2. Open the inlet again slowly, as at the start (CS-006 §7.5 step 4).
3. Write where it raced on the work order.
4. For the next part on this mold, tape a dam at that edge.

The mesh break is the built-in defence: flow mesh stops 30–50 mm short of the outlet side, which slows resin at the end and cuts race-tracking through the exit (CS-006 §7.2 step 3).

If resin fills the resin trap fast, it is over-pulling past full wet. The trap is doing its job: clamp the inlet earlier next time, and empty the trap before it nears the pump port (CS-006 §7.7).

sections.title: QR-012 Bag leaks and dry spots
sections.section: 7. Bubbles: foamy resin at the inlet, or bubbles under the bag
sections.text:
White, foamy resin at the inlet means the cup is slurping: re-submerge the line. Bubbles usually get trapped in the mesh, so note where (CS-006 §7.7). Bubbles under a bag that still holds: flush more resin through before clamping the inlet.

Also called: bubbles, air bubbles, foamy resin, froth, voids, pinholes, slurping inlet.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Do (CS-006 §7.7) |
|---|---|---|
| White or foamy resin at the inlet | Bubbles from a slurping cup | Re-submerge the line; note where bubbles trap in the mesh |
| Bubbles under a sound bag | Air drawn in during the pull | If the bag still holds, flush more resin through before clamping the inlet (shop practice, Larry, #composites 2026-04-03) |

1. Keep the inlet line end fully submerged in the cup for the whole infusion.
2. Brace the cup so it cannot tip.
3. If you see bubbles, write where on the work order, and whether the resin was degassed.

Pinholes from the same mold before? Degassing the resin is optional and covered in QR-002 (degassing).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 1. When can I trim a part after it comes out of the mold?
sections.text:
Not before the FEB hold for its resin has run: 48 h for IN2 with AT30 SLOW, 24 h for IN2 with AT30 FAST, 24 h for West 105 with 206 or 205, 36 h for West 105 with 209 (CS-008 §5; CS-009 §7.1 step 1). The holds are team values, longer than the datasheets on purpose.

Also called: trim, trimming, when to trim, cure time, cure hold, FEB hold, demould, demold, de-mould, how long to wait, Trim and finish.

- On the run, "Trim and finish" comes after "Cure and demould" ("Cure" on a Foam wrapped run). That earlier step carries the hold, and the app keeps it locked until the hold has run (CS-009 §7.1, CS-008 §5.1).
- The hold counts from the finish time recorded when the layup or infusion was signed (CS-008 §7 step 6).
- A cold shop runs long. Fingernail-test the flange rather than trusting the clock (CS-008 §5.1).
- Gel is not cure. A part that feels hard can still be soft at the flange (CS-008 §4).
- The datasheet figure for each system and why the holds are longer: QR-001.

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 2. How do I trim a part to the trim line?
sections.text:
Tape the cut path over the trim line, cut outside the line with the Dremel and a reinforced cut-off wheel, then sand to the line (CS-009 §7.1). The dust extractor runs and a second trained person is present for every cut of cured carbon.

Also called: trim, trimming, cut, cutting, edge, trim line, scribe line, Dremel, cut-off wheel, cutting carbon.

1. Check the FEB hold has run (CS-009 §7.1 step 1; QR-013 §1).
2. Mark the cut from the scribe-transferred trim line (CS-009 §7.1 step 2).
3. Tape the cut path. The tape controls chips and shows the line under dust.
4. Put on a half-facepiece respirator with OV/P100 cartridges, nitrile gloves, long sleeves and safety glasses with side shields (CS-009 §6; QR-013 §3).
5. Start the dust extractor at the cut.
6. Check a second trained person, holding the Trimming and finishing training, is present (CS-009 §6; QR-013 §4).
7. Cut outside the line. A Dremel does not steer well enough to cut on it (CS-009 §7.1 step 3).
8. Sand to the line (QR-013 §5). The target is ±1 mm of the line, a team value (CS-009 §8).

Use reinforced cut-off wheels only: plain wheels shatter in CF (CS-009 §5).

Cutting flat panels on the waterjet, the ShopSabre or the bandsaw is CS-009 §7.5.

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 3. What PPE do I need to cut or sand carbon?
sections.text:
Required: a half-facepiece respirator with OV/P100 cartridges, nitrile gloves, long sleeves, safety glasses with side shields, and the dust extractor running at the cut (CS-009 §6). This covers cutting, sanding or machining cured CF, glass or G10.

Also called: dust, carbon dust, CF dust, PPE, respirator, mask, dust mask, P100, gloves, safety glasses, extractor, dust extraction.

- CF dust is the team's worst routine exposure (CS-009 §6).
- Gloves are also for the edges: cut CF splinters (CS-009 §6).
- The shop stocks A + P100 cartridges; 3M 60921 is the OV/P100 cartridge on file (CS-009 §6, `03 Datasheets/3M-spec-60921-OV-P100-Cartridge.pdf`).
- Solvent wipes (IPA, acetone) need nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Acetone gets through Ansell's 0.45 mm latex/neoprene/nitrile 93-800 in 17 min (ASTM F739; 21 min by EN ISO 374), and Ansell gives no acetone time for thin nitrile; the team's brand may differ, so change gloves as soon as acetone wets them (CS-009 §6, `03 Datasheets/ANSELL-chart-TouchNTuff-93-800.pdf`).
- DP420: nitrile gloves and safety glasses with side shields are required, and a respirator with OV/P100 cartridges when ventilation is not adequate (CS-009 §6; QR-013 §8).
- Every chemical, family by family: QR-008.

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 4. Can I cut carbon on my own? The second-person rule
sections.text:
No. Nobody cuts cured carbon without a second trained person present (CS-009 §6). Trained means the person holds the Trimming and finishing training in the app. The rule was set in SN5, and the Composites Lead may change it.

Also called: supervision, buddy rule, second person, two-person rule, trained, training, cleared to cut, Trimming and finishing training.

- The Composites Lead adds the training in People → Catalog ("Add a training", CS standard CS-009) (CS-009 §6).
- The lead may gate the "Trim and finish" step on it from Reports → Layup techniques → Edit steps ("Training to sign") (CS-009 §6).
- On the ShopSabre and the bandsaw the same dust rules apply: extractor running, respirator on, second trained person present (CS-009 §7.5 step 3).
- The bandsaw needs RFS composites bandsaw training, and the Jacobs Hall OMAX waterjet needs Jacobs waterjet training (CS-009 §5).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 5. What grit do I sand with, and how far can I go?
sections.text:
Only through the sacrificial ply, the 88 spread-tow outer layer; structural plies are not a sanding allowance (CS-009 §7.2, §4). Grits: 120 for trim and keying, 400 for edges, 800 and up before clear coat (CS-009 §5, team grits).

Also called: sand, sanding, grit, sandpaper, wet and dry, finishing, edges, sand-through, sanding budget, sacrificial ply.

1. Read the run's stack before sanding anything (CS-009 §7.2 step 1).
2. In zones under 3 plies, hand-sand only. Count strokes and check often (CS-009 §7.2 step 2).
3. Sand edges 120 then 400 grit (CS-009 §7.2 step 3).
4. Where cosmetics or sealing matter, seal exposed edge fibers with a thin resin wipe. A raw CF edge wicks moisture and splinters into hands.

![Left: the sacrificial ply is the sanding budget; structural plies are not an allowance. Right: the catch-can failure, a machine sander on thin laminate at a taper, through the skin and into the substrate.](figures/cs009-sacrificial.v2.png)

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 6. Why no machine sander on thin laminate?
sections.text:
Because that is how the SN5 catch cans died: a machine sander on thin laminate at a taper went through the skin and into the substrate (CS-009 §7.2, §1). In zones under 3 plies, hand-sand only, count strokes and check often.

Also called: orbital sander, DA, random orbit, power sander, machine sanding, thin laminate, catch can, sand-through, sanding through.

- The damage happened on 2026-05-27 (CS-009 §1).
- Thin, tapered or wrapped metal parts are the worst case: sanding punctured the can wall at the taper (CS-010 §7.1).
- Do not sand thin laminates chasing contact (CS-010 §7.4 step 2).
- If weave shows past the plan, stop sanding and raise ⚑ on the step (CS-009 §7.2 steps 4 to 7; QR-013 §7).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 7. I sanded into the weave. What now?
sections.text:
Stop sanding, and report it with ⚑ (Report an issue on this step) on "Trim and finish" ("Finish" on a Glass infusion run) (CS-009 §7.2 steps 4 to 7). The run cannot complete until the issue is disposed.

Also called: sand-through, sanded through, sanded too far, weave showing, exposed weave, damage, defect, issue, ⚑.

1. Stop sanding.
2. Press ⚑ (Report an issue on this step) on "Trim and finish" ("Finish" on a Glass infusion run).
3. Add the spot under "Photos of the defect".
4. Leave the Disposition to the part's engineer or the Composites Lead.

The §8 check is "Sacrificial ply intact / no exposed weave past plan" (CS-009 §8). Weave past the plan is always an issue on the step, not a note.

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 8. DP420 ratio, open time and clamp time
sections.text:
DP420 mixes 2:1 by volume (B:A), 2:0.98 by weight, and the cartridge sets the ratio. Close the joint within the 20 min open time and keep it clamped until handling strength, 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F) (CS-009 §7.3, `03 Datasheets/3m-scotch-weld-epoxy-adhesive-dp420-black.pdf`).

Also called: DP420, DP 420, 3M glue, structural adhesive, epoxy glue, two-part glue, work life, open time, cure time, clamp time, handling strength, how long to clamp.

All numbers are datasheet figures from the DP420 TDS (CS-009 §5):

| What | Figure |
|---|---|
| Ratio | 2:1 by volume (B:A), 2:0.98 by weight |
| Open time | 20 min |
| Handling strength (unclamp and move, not load) | 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F) |
| Bond strength reported | after 7 days at 23 °C |
| Storage | 16-27 °C (60-80 °F) and 40-60% RH |
| Shelf life | 24 months from manufacture |

- The TDS gives no "24 h full cure". Older notes that say so are wrong (CS-009 Rev D history).
- Load is a separate question with its own team hold (CS-009 §7.6 step 8; QR-013 §11).
- PPE: nitrile gloves and safety glasses with side shields are required; a respirator with OV/P100 cartridges when ventilation is not adequate. You should add indirect vented goggles and a face shield, on the purchase list (CS-009 §6).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 9. How do I prep a surface for bonding?
sections.text:
Gloves on and ignition sources out first, then solvent, abrade, solvent: wipe both faces with IPA, abrade them with 120 grit until the gloss is gone, then wipe again with clean IPA and let them flash off (CS-009 §7.3 steps 1 to 3). The 120 grit is a team value; the TDS asks for clean, fine-grit abrasive.

Also called: bond prep, surface prep, key, keying, scuff, abrade, IPA wipe, acetone wipe, degrease, prep for glue.

1. Put gloves on and put out ignition sources before any solvent is opened (CS-009 §7.3 step 1).
2. Wipe both bond faces with IPA to lift oil and release agent.
3. Abrade both faces with 120 grit until the gloss is gone.
4. Wipe both faces again with clean IPA.
5. Let the faces flash off.
6. Change into clean gloves and keep them on. Do not touch the bond faces from here (CS-009 §7.3 step 4).

- On cured laminate and metal parts away from any mold, acetone may be used instead of IPA, as the TDS's own Acetone/Abrade/Acetone prep does (CS-009 §7.3 step 3).
- Never acetone on or near tooling board (CS-009 §7.3 step 3).
- On a metal insert or rod end, abrade the full bonded length, not a few file strokes (CS-009 §7.6 step 3).
- No silicone-adhesive tape (Kapton and most amber films) anywhere in the shop: trace silicone kills DP420 adhesion (CS-001 §6).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 10. How do I glue with DP420, step by step?
sections.text:
Prep both faces (IPA wipe, 120 grit until the gloss is gone, IPA again, let flash off), purge the cartridge in the EPX applicator until both sides flow, fit the mixing nozzle, apply, close and fix the joint within 20 min, and clamp for 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F) (CS-009 §7.3 steps 1 to 7).

Also called: DP420, glue, gluing, bond, bonding, adhesive, applicator gun, EPX, mixing nozzle, purge, squeeze-out, fillet.

1. Prep both faces: IPA wipe, 120 grit until the gloss is gone, IPA again, let flash off (CS-009 §7.3 steps 1 to 3; QR-013 §9).
2. Load the duo-pak cartridge in the EPX applicator and remove the cap.
3. Dispense a little until both sides flow evenly.
4. Fit the mixing nozzle.
5. Apply the adhesive.
6. Close and fix the joint within the 20 min open time.
7. Clamp so the squeeze-out forms a continuous fillet.
8. Leave the clamps on until handling strength, 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F).
9. Write the bond in the "Trim and finish" note ("Finish" on a Glass infusion run) and add a photo with "Add photos to this step" (CS-009 §9).

A continuous fillet with no starved zones is the acceptance look (CS-009 §8). A joint that will carry load also follows CS-009 §7.6 (QR-013 §11).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 11. Bonding an insert or rod end into a CF tube or part
sections.text:
Every load-carrying bond shall use DP420; never 5-minute epoxy or superglue (CA). Mask the threads, dam the tube, fixture it until 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F), and do not load it before the team hold (CS-009 §7.6). A rear wing rod-end bond failed on track in September.

Also called: insert, rod end, threaded insert, bonded insert, hardware, mount, bracket, load-carrying bond, structural bond, CF tube, carbon tube.

1. Prep both faces: IPA wipe, 120 grit until the gloss is gone over the full bonded length of a metal insert or rod end, IPA again, let flash off (CS-009 §7.3 steps 1 to 3; §7.6 step 3; QR-013 §9).
2. Mask the threads.
3. Dam the tube behind the insert, so adhesive cannot reach the threads or run down the tube. DP420 in a rod-end thread once locked the rod at a set length (CS-009 §7.6 step 4).
4. Purge the cartridge until both sides flow, then fit the mixing nozzle.
5. Hold the bondline at the gap the drawing calls for. The TDS's test bondline is 0.13 to 0.20 mm (5 to 8 mil); the team has not set its own gap (CS-009 §7.6 step 6).
6. Fixture or clamp the joint so it cannot move until handling strength, 2.5 h at 23 °C (73 °F).
7. Do not mount, torque or drive on it before the team hold. That hold is still [lead input needed]; the TDS reports bond strength after 7 days at 23 °C (CS-009 §7.6 step 8). The app does not enforce it.
8. Record adhesive and lot, prep done, time bonded and time first loaded (CS-009 §7.6 step 9; QR-013 §14).

![Section through a CF tube with a bonded insert: solvent, abrade, solvent on both faces; the bondline gap (DP420 TDS test bondline 0.13 to 0.20 mm); a dam inside the tube; masked threads; no load before the team hold.](figures/cs009-insert-bond.v2.png)

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 12. Can I use 5-minute epoxy, superglue or West 404 for a bond?
sections.text:
Not on anything that carries load. Every load-carrying bond uses DP420, and 5-minute epoxy and superglue (CA) are never used on a load-carrying joint (CS-009 §7.6 steps 1 and 2). West 105/206 thickened with 404 is for fillets and gap filling only.

Also called: 5-minute epoxy, five minute epoxy, quick epoxy, superglue, CA, cyanoacrylate, 404, thickened epoxy, filler, West 404.

- In September testing, an undertray insert turned out to have been bonded with 5-minute epoxy (CS-009 §7.6 step 2).
- West 404 is not for load-carrying bonds unless the Composites Lead approves. The 404 TDS rates it for hardware bonding; the team rule is stricter (CS-009 §5).
- A load-carrying bond is any bond that carries load on the car: an insert, a rod end, a mount, a bracket (CS-009 §4).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 13. How do I clear coat a part? Mix ratio and coats (LiME LiNE UC4:1)
sections.text:
Part B, the activator, stays shut until its SDS is on file (CS-009 §7.4 step 1). Then scuff, wipe with IPA, label, mix 4 parts UC4:1 clear to 1 part activator, and apply 2 medium wet coats 10 to 15 min apart (CS-009 §7.4).

Also called: clear coat, clearcoat, clear, UC4:1, LiME LiNE, Lime Line, activator, gloss finish, GH60, GH70, GH80.

1. Check Part B's SDS, or the hazard text from the can's label, is in `03 Datasheets/` and CS-009 §6 quotes its PPE. Until then, stop here (CS-009 §7.4 step 1).
2. Scuff the part.
3. Wipe it with IPA.
4. Apply the part label, which the clear coat goes over (CS-009 §7.4 step 2; CS-009 §5).
5. Mix 4 parts UC4:1 clear with 1 part activator (CS-009 §7.4 step 3).
6. Use the mix within its pot life, 2 h at 77 °F / 25 °C (CS-009 §7.4 step 4).
7. Apply 2 medium wet coats, 10 to 15 min apart. To recoat after 24 h, scuff first (CS-009 §7.4 step 5).
8. Leave it to cure before handling: dust free at 30 min, sand and buff at 12 to 24 h air dry, both at 77 °F / 25 °C (CS-009 §7.4 step 6).
9. Record the activator, the number of coats and the time in the "Trim and finish" note ("Finish" on a Glass infusion run) (CS-009 §7.4 step 7).

Every number here is a datasheet figure from the LiME LiNE TDS, `03 Datasheets/LIMELINE-TDS-UC4-1-Urethane-Clearcoat.pdf`, as copied into CS-009 §7.4. Part A PPE: a respirator with OV/P100 cartridges and nitrile gloves are required; you should wear tightly sealed goggles, which are on the purchase list (CS-009 §6; QR-008 §9).

sections.title: QR-013 Trim, sand and bond prep
sections.section: 14. Where do I record trimming, sanding and bonding?
sections.text:
In the note on the "Trim and finish" step ("Finish" on a Glass infusion run), then buy off the step, which records your name. Add photos of finished edges and bonds with "Add photos to this step" (CS-009 §9).

Also called: record, log, write up, note, step note, photos, buy-off, sign off, Trim and finish, Finish, Execute, first load.

- Measured checks go in the Quality section (Quality checks / acceptance criteria) (CS-009 §9).
- An insert bond records adhesive and lot, prep done, time bonded and time first loaded, in the note on the step where the bond is done: "Trim and finish", "Finish" on a Glass infusion run, "Execute" on an Other run (CS-009 §7.6 step 9).
- Clear coat records the activator, the number of coats and the time in the same note (CS-009 §7.4 step 7).

| Check | Target | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| Trim to scribe | ±1 mm of line (team value) | Quality checks / acceptance criteria |
| No sand-through | Sacrificial ply intact, no exposed weave past plan | Quality checks; weave past plan is a ⚑ issue |
| Bond squeeze-out | Continuous fillet, no starved zones | Step note and a photo |
| Insert bond record | All four items written; first load after the team hold | Step note |

(CS-009 §8)

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.text:
Molds live in the RFS container, and never in front of the knaack or screw boxes (CS-011 §7.3, PP-10). Every mold points at its shelf through its Home location field, so "where is the seat mold" is a lookup, not a Slack ask.

Also called: mold storage, mould storage, find a mold, store a mold, put away a mold, RFS container, container, home location.

- SN5 molds blocked everyone's boxes at RFS (CS-011 §1). That is why the rule names the knaack and screw boxes.
- The monthly walk checks every mold is in its home location; the target is 100% (CS-011 §8).
- A mold that will not be used again is retired, never deleted (CS-003 §4). It still needs a place.
- Moving a big mold between sites: two people for a mold over about 1 m² (CS-011 §7.4 step 1; QR-014 §12).
- To record where you put it: scan the mold, tap Move, scan the shelf (CS-011 §7.3 step 3; QR-014 §8).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.text:
Finished parts go in the Jacobs basement, which needs keycard access. Never the etch locker: that was agreed on 2026-04-20 after parts were evicted from it (CS-011 §7.3, §1).

Also called: part storage, finished parts, find a part, store a part, Jacobs, Jacobs basement, Jacobs Hall, etch locker, keycard.

- Parts travel padded and labeled (CS-011 §7.4 step 2).
- Each part's label carries its record, and scanning it shows its Location (CS-001 §9).
- Record the shelf when you put a part away: scan the part, tap Move, scan the shelf (QR-014 §8).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 3. Where do cloth, foam and tooling board go?
sections.text:
Cloth goes in the Dry sealed bin. Foam and tooling-board stock go in the RFS container, and tooling board is logged under Inventory → Boards, where the real board inventory lives day to day (CS-011 §7.3).

Also called: cloth, carbon cloth, fabric, roll, glass cloth, 195 twill; foam, core, Rohacell; tooling board, board, Precision Board, offcuts, Boards, Stock.

1. Put cloth rolls in the Dry sealed bin. No rule beyond the site (CS-011 §7.3).
2. Put foam and tooling-board stock in the RFS container.
3. Log each tooling board and usable offcut under Inventory → Boards (CS-011 §7.3 step 1).
4. Record the shelf on each cloth roll's lot with Move (QR-014 §8).

- One roll of cloth is one lot record, `FAB-SN6-###` (CS-014 §4).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 4. Where are resin and hardener stored? Can they share a shelf?
sections.text:
Resins and hardeners go in the chemical boxes or barrel, never in a food fridge (CS-011 §6). No app Site names the boxes or the barrel yet (CS-011 §7.3). As written today, CS-011 §6 also says to segregate hardeners from resins on different shelves.

Co-storage: see CS-011 §6; under review.

Also called: resin storage, hardener storage, chemical storage, store epoxy, IN2, AT30, West, 105, 206, XCR, chemical box, barrel, can resin and hardener be stored together, same shelf, segregate.

- Keep every resin and hardener container closed (CS-011 §7.6).
- Temperatures and shelf life: IN2 and AT30 10–25 °C, XCR 20–25 °C, 12 months each by the datasheets (CS-011 §7.6; QR-014 §10).
- By their SDSs, the resins and hardeners are not flammable (CS-014 §6). Which cabinet they live in is CS-011 §6's call, not the Hazard field's (CS-014 §6).
- Put chemicals straight onto a location CS-011 §6 allows for them (CS-014 §6 step 3).
- Wear nitrile gloves to unpack and shelve chemical containers (CS-014 §6 step 1).
- A leaking container does not go on a shelf: leave it in its packaging, set it apart from other chemicals and tell a lead (CS-014 §6 step 2).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 5. Where do flammables go? Acetone, IPA, Airtac, clear coat
sections.text:
Flammables go in the flammables cabinet: Airtac, acetone and clear coat by name (CS-011 §6). By their SDSs, Airtac 2, LiME LiNE Part A, acetone and 91% IPA are flammable; the epoxies are not (CS-014 §6).

Also called: flammables, flammables cabinet, flammable cabinet, acetone, IPA, isopropyl alcohol, Airtac, spray tack, clear coat, LiME LiNE, solvent storage.

| Material | Hazard by its SDS (CS-014 §6) |
|---|---|
| Airtac 2 spray | flammable |
| LiME LiNE UC4:1 Part A | flammable |
| Acetone | flammable |
| 91% IPA | flammable |
| IN2, AT30, XCR, West 105, 205, 206, 209 | not flammable |

IPA is flammable by its SDS too, but CS-011 §6 does not name it, and CS-004 §5 lists the 91% bottle in the Chemicals box. CS-011 §6 is under review.

In the app:

- The site is called Flammables cabinet. A storage location that may hold flammables has Rated for flammables set to Yes.
- Set Hazard on every chemical lot the day it arrives: open the lot's page, press Edit, set Hazard (CS-014 §6 step 4).
- A shelf card warns when it holds a flammable lot and is not a rated location.
- The Receiving desk warns "N flammable items would land on [shelf], which is not a rated location" only for a Material type whose restock rule a lead has marked flammable. None of the shipped rules is, so today the desk does not warn. Set Hazard on each lot from the SDS (CS-014 §6).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 6. Can chemicals go in a fridge?
sections.text:
No. Resin, hardener and every other chemical never go in a fridge (CS-011 §6, CS-014 §6 step 3). The rule comes from the food-fridge incident of 2026-02-17, when chemicals ended up in a food fridge (PP-10).

Also called: fridge, refrigerator, cold storage, keep resin cold, food fridge, freezer.

- The monthly walk checks it: open every location whose Type is fridge and check it holds no resin, hardener or other chemical lot. The target is 0 (CS-011 §8).
- The app does not warn about a chemical on a fridge-type location. The walk is the only check (CS-011 §8).
- Storage temperatures and shelf life: QR-014 §10.

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 7. Where do consumables go? Bags, peel ply, cups, gloves
sections.text:
Consumables go in the General Box at RFS (CS-011 §7.3). Anything that fits no site goes under Other, and the location is named after the place.

Also called: consumables, consumables box, General Box, bag film, VB160, peel ply, flow mesh, tacky tape, cups, mixing cups, sticks, gloves, nitrile gloves, cartridges, breather.

- A consumable is one lot record with a count, `CON-SN6-###` (CS-014 §4).
- A Material type at or below its minimum shows on the Running out card on Inventory → Storage map (CS-011 §5).
- Minimums for the blocking consumables (CS-011 §5): VB160 bag film 1 roll, peel ply 1 roll, flow mesh 1 roll, tacky tape 6 rolls, nitrile gloves 2 boxes per size, mixing cups 50, mixing sticks 50, respirator cartridges (A + P100) 2 sets.
- Reordering from the Running out card: QR-015.

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 8. Moved a mold or part to another shelf? Recording the move
sections.text:
Scan the object, tap Move, scan the shelf (CS-011 §7.3 step 3). To put several things on one shelf, open the shelf and use Move here (scan).

Also called: move, moving, moved, relocate, put away, record a move, change location, scan, Move here, location, home location.

One thing:

1. Scan the object's label, or open its record.
2. Tap Move.
3. Tap Scan the shelf and scan the shelf's label. The move saves as soon as the label reads ("Moved to …"). Or pick the shelf from Location and press Move it.

Several things onto one shelf:

1. Open the shelf on Inventory → Storage map.
2. Press Move here (scan).
3. Scan each object's label.

- The location is a controlled value: every shelf, bin and rack is its own record, so the walk checks reality against it instead of whatever string somebody typed (CS-011 §7.3).
- Something on the wrong shelf during the walk: fix it with Move as you go (CS-011 §7.1 step 3).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 9. How do I add a new shelf, bin or rack?
sections.text:
Press + Location on Inventory → Storage map, set its Site from the storage table, and put its printed label on the shelf's front edge (CS-011 §7.3 step 2, CS-001 §7.10). Every mold, part and material lot then points at a storage record.

Also called: new shelf, add a shelf, new bin, new location, storage location, BIN, rack, cabinet, shelf label, + Location.

1. Open Inventory → Storage map.
2. Press + Location.
3. Name it after the place.
4. Set Site: RFS container, Jacobs basement, Flammables cabinet, Dry sealed bin, General Box or Other.
5. Set Type (shelf, rack, cabinet, bin, box or fridge).
6. If it is rated for flammables, set Rated for flammables to Yes.
7. If campus EH&S has stuck an RSS sublocation tag on it, record that in EH&S barcode (CS-014 §4).
8. Print its label and stick it on the front edge (CS-001 §7.10).

The site names are the ones the app uses (Site on a storage location). CS-011 §7.3 notes they still need a field check against the real shelves.

A storage location's ID is `BIN-SN6-###` (CS-013 §4.1), and its label's key line reads STORAGE (CS-001 §4).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 10. What temperature does resin need, and how long does it keep?
sections.text:
IN2 and AT30: 10–25 °C (50–77 °F), tightly sealed, 12 months. XCR: 20–25 °C (68–77 °F), tightly sealed, 12 months. West 105 and its hardeners: room temperature, containers closed, usable for many years (CS-011 §7.6, datasheet figures).

Also called: storage temperature, shelf life, expiry, expiration, how long does resin last, out of date, cold resin, crystallized, crystallised, cloudy 105.

| Material | Store at | Shelf life | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| IN2 resin and AT30 hardener | 10–25 °C (50–77 °F), tightly sealed | 12 months when stored correctly | `03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-IN2-Infusion-Resin.pdf` |
| XCR resin and hardener | 20–25 °C (68–77 °F), tightly sealed | 12 months when stored correctly | `03 Datasheets/EC-TDS-XCR-Epoxy-Coating-Resin.pdf` |
| West 105 with 205, 206 or 209 | Room temperature, containers closed | Many years with proper storage | West TDSs (CS-011 §7.6) |

- These are datasheet figures, not team holds (CS-011 §7.6).
- Do not let West 105 freeze and thaw repeatedly: it crystallizes. Crystallized 105 is warmed to 125 °F and stirred until clear before use (CS-008 §7 step 8).
- After long storage, check the West pumps' metering and mix a small test batch to confirm it cures (CS-011 §7.6 step 2).
- Check the expiry before you mix; past it, ask a lead (CS-008 §7 step 1).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 11. How do I check what is on a shelf? The monthly stock walk
sections.text:
Open Inventory → Storage map, open each shelf's card, check the list against what is on the shelf, and press Confirm contents (CS-011 §7.1). The walk is monthly and takes about 15 minutes (team estimate).

Also called: stock walk, inventory check, stock check, stocktake, audit, Confirm contents, need a walk, Running out, what do we have.

1. Open Inventory → Storage map.
2. Open a shelf's card and check its list against the shelf.
3. Press Confirm contents (Confirm on the map card does the same).
4. Fix what is wrong as you go: Move, How full, or the shelf's Add here card for anything missing.
5. Open the Running out card. For any row without "on order", press Add N to a purchase.
6. Post the purchase request in #purchasing-slackbot the same day (CS-011 §7.1 step 5).

- The lead names the stock-walk owner at the start of the season (CS-011 §7.1 step 1).
- The "need a walk" chip counts shelves not confirmed in 30 days; the target is 0 (CS-011 §8).
- A shelf's page folds identical containers into one row by Material type (CS-011 §7.3).
- Mark an emptied container Empty rather than deleting it (CS-011 §7.1).

sections.title: QR-014 Where things are stored
sections.section: 12. Moving a big mold or a part between sites
sections.text:
Molds over about 1 m² take two people and a vehicle that actually fits them: plan it, don't discover it (CS-011 §7.4 step 1). Parts travel padded and labeled (CS-011 §7.4 step 2). The SN5 budget shows a U-Haul was needed for mold moves.

Also called: transport, moving molds, carrying a mold, van, U-Haul, car, trip to RFS, taking parts to Jacobs.

1. Plan the move ahead. A mold over about 1 m² needs two people.
2. Use a vehicle the mold actually fits in.
3. Pad and label parts before they travel.
4. At the other end, record the move: scan the object, tap Move, scan the shelf (QR-014 §8).

Heavy tooling-board stacks: two people to move anything over about half a sheet, and watch pinch points (CS-003 §6).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.section: 1. How do I get a purchase approved before I buy?
sections.text:
Run `/purchase` in #purchasing-slackbot with the budget reference ID, the amount and the reason, and buy only after the bot's approval DM arrives (CS-012 §7.1). For several items on different reference IDs, use `/bigorder`.

Also called: approval, approve, pre-approval, permission to buy, purchase request, /purchase, /bigorder, purchasing bot, Flux, #purchasing, #purchasing-slackbot, can I buy.

1. Pick the reference ID for the budget line that pays; `/reference` lists them (QR-015 §3).
2. Run `/purchase` in #purchasing-slackbot with the reference ID, the amount and the reason.
3. Wait. The bot sends the request to the approver for its amount: under $50 the subteam lead, $50 to $250 the division lead, over $250 the President or VP (CS-012 §4; QR-015 §2).
4. Buy only after the approval DM arrives.
5. Log it in the Budget tab and write the bot's REQ number in the purchase's Notes (CS-012 §7.9; QR-015 §7).

- #purchasing was retired on 2026-10-07. Requests go through the Flux bot in #purchasing-slackbot now (CS-012 Rev G history).
- Treat a purchase not logged in #purchasing-slackbot as not reimbursed (CS-012 §7.7 step 2).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.text:
By amount: under $50 the subteam lead, $50 to $250 the division lead, over $250 the President or VP (CS-012 §4, §7.1 step 2). The purchasing bot routes the request to the right one.

Also called: approval tiers, approver, who approves, spending limit, how much can I spend, subteam lead, division lead, President, VP.

| Amount | Approver |
|---|---|
| Under $50 | Subteam lead |
| $50 to $250 | Division lead |
| Over $250 | President or VP |

- A purchase under $50 still needs the subteam lead's approval. The app does not flag it (CS-012 §7.1).
- The Budget tab counts purchases over $50 whose Reimbursement is still Submitted, as "Over $50, unapproved" (CS-012 §7.1).
- The tiers were re-verified on 2026-10-07 and are unchanged (CS-012 Rev G history).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.section: 3. Which reference ID do I use?
sections.text:
The one for the budget line the money comes from: `/reference` lists them, and composites lines start `COMP-`. Testing purchases use `TRAN-012`. Use a `-000` ID only for something the budget never listed, and tell the lead (CS-012 §7.2 step 4).

Also called: reference ID, budget line, budget code, account, category, COMP-, TRAN-012, TRAN-002, -000, /reference, which code.

- A reference ID looks like `COMP-011` (CS-012 §4).
- A `-000` ID comes out of another line, which is why the lead needs to know (CS-012 §7.2 step 4).
- If the money is not composites', write the reference ID in the purchase's Charged to field, for example `TRAN-002` for RFS consumables. Leave Charged to blank for a `COMP-` line (CS-012 §7.9 step 3).
- Charged to blank, or "Composites", means it counts against the composites season total. Anything else is still tracked and still reimbursed, but not counted there (CS-012 §4).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.text:
Log the purchase in the bot and submit it within one month of buying, with `/reimburse`, the reference ID and the amount (CS-012 §7.2 step 5). You need the itemized receipt and the card statement line.

Also called: reimburse, reimbursed, reimbursement, paid back, pay me back, get my money back, /reimburse, expense, refund.

1. Photograph the itemized receipt, or save the PDF invoice an online order emails you (CS-012 §7.2 step 1).
2. Add the card statement, with other lines redacted (CS-012 §7.2 step 2; QR-015 §5).
3. Amazon: wait until the order shows Shipped or Delivered.
4. Pick the reference ID (QR-015 §3).
5. Submit within one month of the purchase with `/reimburse`, the reference ID and the amount.
6. Attach the receipt to the purchase in the Budget tab with + Add / scan receipt. Put the quote and order confirmation under Other files.
7. To use ✨ Fill from receipt, press Edit first, then check every line it proposes (CS-012 §7.2 step 7; QR-015 §8).
8. Move Reimbursement to Reimbursed when the money arrives (QR-015 §9).

- Deposits take up to a month (CS-012 §6).
- Season close has a hard finance deadline; SN5's was July 4 (CS-012 §7.7 step 1; QR-015 §12).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.section: 5. What does the receipt need to show?
sections.text:
An itemized receipt, or the PDF invoice for an online order, plus the card statement line. A card statement alone is not enough (CS-012 §7.2 steps 1 and 2).

Also called: receipt, invoice, itemized receipt, itemised receipt, card statement, bank statement, proof of purchase, order confirmation, redact.

- The receipt or invoice: itemized, so each thing bought is listed.
- The card statement: redact the other lines, but keep your name, address, the card's last 4 digits, the purchase and the date (CS-012 §7.2 step 2).
- Amazon orders must show Shipped or Delivered before you submit (CS-012 §7.2 step 3).
- Attach the receipt to the purchase in the Budget tab with + Add / scan receipt, and the quote and order confirmation under Other files (CS-012 §7.2 step 6).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.section: 6. Which payment methods are not reimbursed?
sections.text:
Cash, Venmo, Zelle and PayPal are not reimbursed. Ask the finance lead before paying with one. Gift cards: ask the finance lead first, because the 2025 rules excluded them (CS-012 §7.2 step 5).

Also called: payment method, how to pay, cash, Venmo, Zelle, PayPal, gift card, personal card, credit card, debit card, fronting money.

- Nobody fronts more than they are comfortable waiting about a month to get back. Deposits take up to a month (CS-012 §6).
- A lead names 2 to 3 regular purchasers, with the finance lead's knowledge, so no single card is the team's float (CS-012 §7.3).
- In SN5 almost all of the spend went through the lead's personal card (CS-012 §1).

sections.title: QR-015 Buying something and getting paid back
sections.section: 7. How do I log a purchase in the app's Budget tab?
sections.text:
